title: Deferring your admission
content_markdown:
If you are offered admission to full\-time study in the first year of a direct\-entry degree, you may be able to defer your studies for **one full academic year**\.

## Eligibility for deferred admission

You are eligible to apply for a deferral if **you have been admitted to year one of an undergraduate degree** and want to defer admission for reasons such as:

-   You are planning to take a gap year\.
-   You are required to complete mandatory military service\.
-   You will be participating in a Rotary program\.

**However, not all deferral applications will be approved\.**

You are **not** eligible to apply for a deferral for reasons such as:

-   You have been admitted to the second or upper years of a degree\.
-   You have been admitted to a limited enrolment degree, including but not limited to the Bachelor of Computer Science, Bachelor of Music, Bachelor of Midwifery, Bachelor of Education, Bachelor of Commerce, or Bachelor of Nursing at UBC Okanagan\.
-   You want to defer your admission to attend another post\-secondary institution\.

## How to apply

To apply for a deferral, you must meet the following conditions:

-   You must accept your offer of admission\.
-   You must fulfill the conditions of your offer of admission\.
-   You must submit a deferred admission request form \(see below\) **before** **July 1** if you are admitted to a UBC Vancouver program, or **before August 15** if you are admitted to a UBC Okanagan program\. Applications submitted after this date may be reviewed if your circumstances have changed beyond your control\. Please send your completed form as a scanned attachment to [admissions\.inquiry@ubc\.ca](mailto:admissions.inquiry@ubc.ca)\.

**[Deferred admission request form](https://you.ubc.ca/wp-content/uploads/2021/05/Deferred-admission-request-form_secured.pdf)**

114 KB PDF

Download this form to submit an admission deferral request\.

## Registering for courses

Because we are unable to approve all deferral applications, we recommend that you still register for your first\-year courses, even if your deferral request is pending\.

If your request is approved, you should withdraw from your courses\. If it is denied, you may choose to remain enrolled, or withdraw from your courses and cancel your registration at UBC\.

## Notifying UBC Student Housing

If you are granted deferred admission and have applied for residence, you should notify [UBC Student Housing](http://www.housing.ubc.ca/) directly\.

title: Funding for former youth in care
content_markdown:
If you are a UBC student who was formerly in care, you are encouraged to apply for two tuition waivers: the BC Provincial Tuition Waiver and the UBC Post Care Tuition Waiver\. The criteria for each waiver are different, but there is some overlap\. If you meet the eligibility requirements for both waivers, you will receive the BC Provincial Tuition Waiver\. Funding would apply toward your first undergraduate degree program at UBC\. If your application is deemed ineligible then you may submit an appeal by contacting us\.

## BC Provincial Tuition Waiver Program

The BC Provincial Tuition Waiver Program covers the cost of your tuition fees toward your first undergraduate degree if you were a youth in care in BC for a combined two years or more\. You must be between 19 and 26 years old\. Find out more on the [BC Provincial Tuition Waiver Program website](https://www2.gov.bc.ca/gov/content/education-training/post-secondary-education/pay-for-school/provincial-tuition-waiver-program)\.

**[BC Provincial Tuition Waiver Request Form](https://you.ubc.ca/wp-content/uploads/2020/01/provincial-tuition-waiver-program-application.pdf)**

955 KB PDF

Download and complete this form\.

## UBC Post Care Tuition Waiver

The UBC Post Care Tuition Waiver covers the cost of tuition fees toward the completion of a first undergraduate degree for eligible students who have lived as youth in care in BC\.

### Eligibility

Please review the UBC post\-care tuition waiver application below to find out whether you are eligible, and fill out the form\.

**[UBC Post Care Tuition Waiver Application Form](https://you.ubc.ca/wp-content/uploads/2021/11/2022W-Post-Care-Tuition-Waiver.pdf)**

208 KB PDF

Download and complete this form\.

### How to apply

Submit your signed application\(s\) and consent form\(s\) to [sabrina\.materie@ubc\.ca](mailto:sabrina.materie@ubc.ca) \(Vancouver campus\) or [halyna\.petryshyn@ubc\.ca](mailto:halyna.petryshyn@ubc.ca) \(Okanagan campus\) after you have [applied for admission to UBC](http://you.ubc.ca/applying-ubc/)\.

Or drop it off in person at:

-   Vancouver campus: Brock Hall \(1874 East Mall\) at the Advisory Centre on the main floor\.

-   Okanagan campus: University Centre \(206Z – 3272 University Way\) at the 2nd floor front desk\.

## Youth Futures Education Fund

The [Youth Futures Education Fund](https://www.vancouverfoundation.ca/youthfutures) provides funds to help with living expenses for students who were previously in government care and are attending a post\-secondary institution on a provincial tuition waver\.

## Youth Education Assistance Fund

The Youth Education Assistance Fund provides grants to students between the ages of 19 and 24 years who have been in care in BC\. You may be eligible for a grant of up to $5,500 per year per program\.

Find out more on the [StudentAid BC website](https://studentaidbc.ca/explore/grants-scholarships/youth-educational-assistance-fund-former-youth-care)\.

## Agreements with Youth Adults \(AYA funding\)

The Agreements with Youth Adults \(AYA\) program can assist you if you have been in foster care or had a youth agreement\. This program can provide assistance, with costs of things such as housing, child care, tuition, and health care while you go back to school, or if you are attending rehabilitation, vocational or approved life skills programs\. For more information visit [Agreements with Young Adults\.](https://www2.gov.bc.ca/gov/content/safety/public-safety/protecting-children/youth-agreements)

## Aged Out brought to you by Former Youth in Care

This online resource was created by and for youth that have been in care or are currently in care\. This interactive website explores topics such as health and wellness, housing, and ID Needs\. For more information visit [Agedout\.com\.](https://agedout.com/)

## UBC Centennial Scholars Entrance Awards

The [UBC Centennial Scholars Entrance Award](https://you.ubc.ca/financial-planning/scholarships-awards-canadian-students/entrance-award/) program assists students who are transitioning to UBC from secondary school or another post\-secondary institution\. The purpose of the program is to financially support academically qualified students who show an interest in joining and contributing to the UBC community, but who would not be able to attend without significant financial assistance\.

Through the program, new students can access a variety of one\-time and renewable awards of up to $40,000, payable over four years\. For those studying on UBC’s Vancouver campus, there are opportunities to receive full\-ride awards that cover the full cost of your degree and living expenses\.

## Questions?

If you have questions about applying to UBC as a former youth in care, please contact us\.

title: Living in residence
content_markdown:
Going to university is not just about studying, it’s also a social adventure that, for many students, begins in “rez\.”

Each year, UBC houses almost 9,400 students in 12 residence complexes that circle the Vancouver campus\. You’ll find everything, from traditional\-style rooms and apartments to townhouses and condominium units, all designed to help you adjust to university and make connections on campus\.

And the location couldn’t be better: You’re surrounded by gardens, there’s a regional park next door, and the Pacific Ocean is within walking distance\.

[Embedded iframe \(view source\)](https://www.youtube.com/embed/XwE2kWVj0g4)

## Residence options

Most first\-year students live in Winter Session Residence from September to April\. Rooms and suites come with basic furnishings and a high\-speed internet connection\. Most first\-year students live in a shared room, although you may be assigned a single room\. Residence areas include [Totem Park,](http://vancouver.housing.ubc.ca/residences/totem-park/) [Place Vanier](http://vancouver.housing.ubc.ca/residences/place-vanier/), [Walter Gage](http://vancouver.housing.ubc.ca/residences/walter-gage/), [Fairview Crescent](http://vancouver.housing.ubc.ca/residences/fairview-crescent/), and [Ritsumeikan\-UBC House](http://vancouver.housing.ubc.ca/residences/ritsumeikan-ubc-house/)\.

## Residence support

No matter which residence you live in, you will be part of a supportive environment that’s designed to help you adjust to university and enjoy your time as a student\. Residence Advisors, current UBC students who have experience in residences and lots to offer younger students, live in your area and are plugged in to the resources and support that are available at UBC\.

When you hit a snag or need to vent, Residence Advisors can help\. They organize events that will connect you with fellow residents and campus opportunities, and help ensure you live in an environment that supports your academic success\. All residences also operate a front desk that is ready to help when the need arises\.

## Meal plans

Our campus [meal plans](http://vancouver.housing.ubc.ca/dining/meal-plans/ "UBC - Residence Meal Plans") offer flexibility and tasty, nutritious options\. If you live in Totem Park or Place Vanier, it is mandatory to purchase a meal plan\. Students in other residences can purchase an optional campus dining plan for added savings and convenience at more than [30 Food Services outlets](http://www.food.ubc.ca/) around campus\.

Food Services can accommodate a variety of nutritional needs and health conditions that require a specific eating plan\. Please email them in advance if you have special dietary needs at [meal\.plan@ubc\.ca](mailto:meal.plan@ubc.ca)\.

## Residence costs

Your [costs will vary](http://vancouver.housing.ubc.ca/applications/fees-payments/) depending on what type of room you live in and what size of meal plan you choose\. A typical cost for a room and [meal plan](http://vancouver.housing.ubc.ca/dining/meal-plans/) is between $6,500 and $8,500 for the eight\-month school year\. Payments are spread over the school year\.

## Applying for residence

Most first\-year students will be eligible for a [guaranteed room in residence](http://vancouver.housing.ubc.ca/applications/how-we-assign-rooms/first-year-guarantee/)\. Every student coming to UBC’s Vancouver campus who will graduate from high school in 2015 can now live on campus and benefit from the exceptional academic and social support offered through our residence program\.

It’s best to start your residence application as soon as you apply for admission to UBC\. You can start your residence application when you [apply to UBC](https://account.you.ubc.ca/ubc/apply/apply_now.ezc), and then visit the [Student Housing and Hospitality Services \(SHHS\) Online Service Centre](https://secure.housing.ubc.ca/ "UBC Student Housing and Hospitality Services (SHHS) Online Service Centre") to finish your residence application\. Or, you can apply for residence directly from the Student Housing and Hospitality Services website, if you didn’t start the process during your application for admission to UBC\.

If you are considering both the Vancouver and Okanagan campuses for your studies, apply to both residences at the same time and you will only pay the application fee once\.

The Winter Session Residence application deadline is **May 1**\. If you wait until you are given an offer of admission to UBC to apply for residence, you may not get a space\.

## Important dates

| Date | Details |
| --- | --- |
| May 1 | Apply for residence by this deadline\. Complete residence preference and roommate requests online at the [Student Housing and Hospitality Services \(SHHS\) Online Service Centre](https://secure.housing.ubc.ca/ "UBC Student Housing and Hospitality Services (SHHS) Online Service Centre")\. |
| June 2 | Accept your academic offer of admission by this deadline in order to qualify for a guaranteed room in residence\. |
| June through August | Check your email regularly for your residence offer\. Once UBC sends your offer, you have one week to accept it and pay your $800 deposit online\. If you will be away in the summer, make arrangements to check your email regularly\. |
| Mid\-August | Watch for detailed room assignment information\. If you have a roommate, you’ll be able to contact each other in advance\. |
| Saturday before Labour Day | Residence [move\-in day](http://vancouver.housing.ubc.ca/residence-life/moving-in/ "UBC - Student Services")\! Bring your stuff to campus, meet your floormates and Residence Advisor, and start living and learning at UBC\. |

## After your first year

Residence is not guaranteed after your first year\. [Returning students](http://vancouver.housing.ubc.ca/getting-started/returning/) who want to live in residence are encouraged to apply for a space in Year Round Residence, which runs from May to April\.

title: Living off campus
content_markdown:
## Getting to and from campus

UBC is a 20\-minute bus ride from downtown Vancouver\. The campus is served by 13 bus routes with connections to destinations throughout the Greater Vancouver area\. Every full\-time UBC Vancouver student receives a reasonably priced [U\-Pass](http://www.upass.ubc.ca/upass/upassindex.html) that provides unlimited travel on bus, SkyTrain, and SeaBus\. The cost of the pass is included in your University fees\.

Check out UBC’s [Trek program](http://www.trek.ubc.ca/) for information on transportation options, including cycling and carpooling\.

## Off\-campus housing resources

If you are looking for off\-campus housing near UBC, there are many resources on the [UBC Student Housing and Hospitality Services website](http://www.housing.ubc.ca/off-campus-housing "UBC Off-campus Housing") that can help you in your search\.

## On\-campus hostel

As a commuter, you may find that there are times when it would be easier to spend the night on campus rather than head home\. Perhaps you have a late evening club meeting, or maybe you have an exam early the next morning and you want to stay late to study in the UBC Library\. For those occasions, the [Commuter Student Hostel](http://vancouver.housing.ubc.ca/other-housing/commuter-student-hostel/) offers rooms for just $30 a night\. You’ll be able to spend the night on campus and wake up ready for whatever the next day holds\.

## Orientation and transition

Whether you live on\- or off\-campus, when you become a student at UBC, you join a community\. On your first day at UBC, all new students take part in Imagine UBC, an exciting day\-long event where you’ll meet new friends and get connected with campus services and resources\.

Before and beyond your first day, we’ll work hard to keep you in the loop about how to be an active part of the UBC community\. All new students receive [New to UBC](http://blog.students.ubc.ca/newtoubc/), a bi\-weekly e\-newsletter with information about upcoming events and opportunities on campus\.

[Connections magazine](http://www.students.ubc.ca/newtoubc/download/commuter_student_connections.pdf) is published in the fall to help commuter students adjust to UBC\.

Your studies at UBC will also be a transition for your family\. [Commuter Student Parent Orientation](http://www.students.ubc.ca/parents/orientation.cfm?page=parent) is a great way for family members to get acquainted with UBC and to prepare them for the changes you’ll be experiencing\.

title: Getting involved
content_markdown:
Ask any current UBC student – one of the smartest things you can do while at UBC is to get involved on campus\. In fact, studies show that students who participate in student life tend to do better in their academics as well\. Between UBC programs, student government, and the hundreds of student\-run clubs available, you’ll be sure to find others on campus with interests similar to your own\.

What makes a great leader? How can you contribute to your campus and the wider community? UBC offers a number of opportunities to challenge yourself, make a difference, learn new skills, and help shape our developing campus community\.

title: Academics and learning
content_markdown:
Why is UBC such a great place for students to learn, grow, and develop? The answer is simple: UBC combines a solid reputation for academic excellence with a flexible, student\-centred learning environment\. And our location doesn’t hurt either\.

Find out below why we’re one of the [world’s top 40 research universities](http://ubc.ca/global/index.html)\.

## Undergraduate Research

As a UBC student, you’ll have the opportunity to participate in hands\-on research and interdisciplinary collaborations\. Work side by side with faculty members who are experts in their fields, contribute to research projects with global significance, and pursue your own unique interests – no matter how diverse\.

Whether you’re actively looking for research opportunities, or want to learn more before you dive in, UBC has a variety of resources, groups, and awards to support you in your ambitions\.

-   Attend the [Multidisciplinary Undergraduate Research Conference](http://murc.ubc.ca/)
-   Apply for a [Research Award](http://students.ubc.ca/career/campus-experiences/undergraduate-research)
-   Join the [Undergraduate Research Opportunities Club](http://www.uroubc.ca/)
-   Apply for a paid [Work Learn](http://students.ubc.ca/career/campus-experiences/work-learn) opportunity if you’re studying in Vancouver, or a [Work Study](http://students.ok.ubc.ca/careers/services/jobs/workstudy.html) opportunity if you’re a student in the Okanagan\.

## Learning Support

Learning extends further than textbooks and lectures, which is why UBC offers a wide range of supports to help you achieve your best\. From advising and tutoring to new educational technology and facilities, you have access to the people,  tools, and spaces that will help you succeed\.

### Advising and tutoring

Whether you want advice on picking courses or need help understanding challenging course materials, get the support you need on a drop\-in or by\-appointment basis\. Meet with an academic advisor to discuss your academics, join a peer\-assisted study session to hone your studying skills, or attend a tutoring session led by a senior student in your field\. Learn more about advising and tutoring services offered at the [Vancouver](http://students.ubc.ca/) and [Okanagan](http://students.ok.ubc.ca/welcome.html) campuses\.

### Learning spaces

As any student who has spent long hours researching or studying can tell you, finding space that’s conducive to learning is crucial\. As a UBC student, you’ll have access to state\-of\-the\-art classrooms, libraries, facilities, and technologies\.

#### Libraries

The [UBC Library](http://www.library.ubc.ca/), one of the largest in Canada, is home to extensive collections and electronic resources, as well as helpful services like research tutorials and real\-time chat with librarians\. With over 21 branches located in Vancouver and the [Okanagan](http://www.library.ubc.ca/ubco/), you have free and unlimited access to world\-class educational materials wherever you’re studying\.

#### Learning & Study Facilities

Both the Vancouver and Okanagan offer innovative learning spaces that combine information resources and services, and the latest in technology\. As a UBC student, you’ll have access to study spaces, group study rooms, wireless access, laptop lending programs, and classroom and lecture spaces at the [Irving K\. Barber Learning Centre](http://www.ikebarberlearningcentre.ubc.ca/) in Vancouver and the UBC Okanagan [Information Commons](http://www.library.ubc.ca/ubco/InfoCommons.html)\.

## Co\-op Education Programs

UBC’s popular [co\-op program](http://www.coop.ubc.ca/) lets you combine your studies with full\-time, paid work experience\. After being accepted to the program, you could find yourself learning forest conservation in northern British Columbia, editing books in Toronto, or designing software in California\. Learn more about [UBC co\-op programs and availability](http://www.coop.ubc.ca/)\.

## Community Learning Initiatives

At UBC, you have an opportunity to put down your books and venture into the community to learn, connect with new people, and make positive social change\. With a variety of options in Vancouver, the Okanagan, and abroad, it’s easy to find a community experience that fits your academic and personal interests\.

Learn more about [Vancouver](http://students.ubc.ca/career/community-experiences) and [Okanagan](http://students.ok.ubc.ca/cslprogram/welcome.html) community opportunities\.

title: Interdisciplinary studies and innovative programs
content_markdown:
UBC has historically been a pioneer in teaching across disciplines, and today we have more integrated first\-year programs than any other Canadian university\. We passionately believe that this style of teaching is one of the most effective ways for you to become a critical, independent thinker\.

Here are some examples of programs across UBC’s Vancouver and Okanagan campuses that embrace inter\- and multi\-disciplinary thinking:

## Applied Science

[Integrated Engineering](http://www.igen.ubc.ca/) – Rather than earning a degree in one specific area of engineering, gain background in several core disciplines through the Integrated Engineering Program\.

[Engineering One](http://web.ubc.ca/okanagan/engineering/undergraduate.html) –  This introduction to the engineering profession integrates math, chemistry, biology, and physics to show you, in a meaningful way, the connections between these fields and how the sum is greater than the parts, particularly when it comes to engineering challenges on everything from bridge construction to snowboard design\. Offered in the Okanagan\.

[Cognitive Science](http://web.ubc.ca/okanagan/ikbarberschool/programs/undergradprograms/general-ba.html) – This program brings philosophy, psychology, linguistics, and computer science together in the study of intelligence\. Part of the General Studies Program, this multidisciplinary option allows students to study cognition from a variety of approaches\.

## Arts

[Arts One](http://arts1.arts.ubc.ca/) – This program takes an innovative approach to the study of the humanities and focuses on English, History, and Philosophy\. Instead of attending several separate lectures, you’ll attend one weekly lecture taught by a dynamic team of instructors from a variety of academic disciplines\. The core of Arts One is its extensive reading list: you will read, discuss, and write essays about great works of literature, history, and philosophy, both ancient and modern\.

[Coordinated Arts Program](http://www.cap.arts.ubc.ca/) – This introduction to core arts disciplines is taught in small, 25\-person study groups\. Choose from four streams: Civil and Sustainable Societies; Individual in Society; Global Citizens; and PPE: Political Science, Philosophy & Economics\.

[Interdisciplinary Studies BA Program](http://www.interdisciplinary.arts.ubc.ca/) – This option provides an alternative to the traditional, department\-based major\. Design your own cross\-disciplinary course of study in consultation with an advisor\.

[International Relations](http://web.ubc.ca/okanagan/ir/welcome.html) –  Develop a solid background in the related fields of political science, history, sociology, anthropology, economics, and modern languages\.

[Philosophy, Politics & Economics](http://web.ubc.ca/okanagan/ppe/welcome.html) This program gives you an exceptional opportunity to view our world through three different lenses: philosophy teaches logic, ethics, and how to question critically; politics determine the rules by which we are governed; economics encompasses how we make decisions as individuals and groups in our increasingly global world market\. Placed into context with each other, these three fields allow you to form critical and informed opinions about the world in which you live\.

## Forestry

[Natural Resources Conservation](http://www.forestry.ubc.ca/students/undergraduate/prospective/degree-programs/natural-resources-conservation/) – Immerse yourself in the multidisciplinary world of conservation science and get prepared for a range of career options: from resource conservation to managing protected areas to landscape planning\.

## Land & Food Systems

[Global Resources Systems](http://www.landfood.ubc.ca/programs/grs_ug.htm) – This award\-winning program lets you combine language, travel, and science as your studies focus on a specific region of the world\.

## Science

[Science One](http://www.scienceone.ubc.ca/)  – This team\-taught program blends biology, chemistry, mathematics, and physics into a challenging format allowing you to hone your critical thinking, analytical skills, and independent thought through lectures, tutorials, laboratories, and field trips\.

[Coordinated Science Program](https://csp.science.ubc.ca/) – This popular program allows students to explore the connections between all scientific disciplines – biology, chemistry, physics, computer science, and math – in an intimate learning environment\.

[Environmental Sciences Program](http://www.ensc.ubc.ca/) – Interested in understanding the major environmental issues facing human societies? This program offers a integrative, cross\-disciplinary approach to the study of these important issues\.

[Earth & Environmental Sciences](http://web.ubc.ca/okanagan/eesc/welcome.html) is a multidisciplinary Bachelor of Science program that emphasizes the interactions between humans and the environment\. The program is extremely flexible; you can focus on the environment or the solid earth in your studies as well as enhance your program with related courses in biochemistry, biology, chemistry, geography, plus mathematics and statistics\.

[Integrated Sciences Program](http://intsci.ubc.ca/) – An alternative to the traditional, department\-based major\. Design your own cross\-disciplinary course of study in consultation with an advisor\.

title: Arts and culture
content_markdown:
[Arts and culture](https://you.ubc.ca/wp-content/uploads/2024/08/arts-culture.jpg)

UBC is home to a rich arts and culture scene\. From theatres and galleries to clubs and festivals, you can take advantage of a vast array of activities, groups, and venues on campus to seek inspiration and uncover hidden talents\.

[Students exploring an interactive art exhibit at the Okanagan Art Gallery](https://you.ubc.ca/wp-content/uploads/2024/08/okanagan-interactive-art-exhibit.jpg)

### Arts and culture on campus

On each campus, you’ll find performances, festivals, and events to awaken the artist in you\. Hear from established visual artists at the Visiting Artist lecture series on the Okanagan campus or take in an exhibition at the Morris and Helen Belkin Art Gallery on the Vancouver campus\. Pick up a pencil and participate in Draw by Night, a bi\-monthly social drawing party held at cultural venues in Kelowna, or see student masterpieces at the Hatch Art Gallery on the Vancouver campus\.

**Okanagan Campus**

[Explore arts and culture on campus](http://fccs.ok.ubc.ca/news-events.html)

**Vancouver Campus**

[Explore arts and culture on campus](https://www.arts.ubc.ca/arts-culture/)

[Image](https://you.ubc.ca/wp-content/uploads/2015/11/arts-clubs.jpg)

### Arts clubs and societies

Sing your heart out with the A Cappella Club or master the art of ceramics with the Pottery Club on UBC’s Vancouver campus\. Focus on digital practices with the Photography Club or learn the Argentine tango with the Latin Dance Club on UBC’s Okanagan campus\. Whatever club you choose, you’ll be connecting with like\-minded students who share your passion\.

**Okanagan Campus**

[Discover arts clubs on campus](https://www.suo.ca/student-associations/)

**Vancouver Campus**

[Discover arts clubs on campus](https://www.ams.ubc.ca/student-life/clubs/)

## Arts events and activities

UBC offers a vibrant culture with an eclectic mix of performances, festivals, events, and experiences\. Participate in an activity or attend an event to meet other students, get inspired, and have fun\.

### Draw by Night

**Okanagan campus**

Draw by Night is an ongoing bi\-monthly public event held at the Alternator Centre, Kelowna Art Gallery, and Kelowna Museum that promotes creativity, imagination, and collaboration through the process of drawing\.

[Draw with students, professionals, visual artists, and hobbyists](http://fccs.ok.ubc.ca/news-events/ongoing/drawbynight.html)  

### Persistence of Vision Film Festival \(POV\)

**Vancouver campus**

The POV Film Festival is an annual event showcasing short films written, directed, shot, edited, and produced by students in UBC’s [Film Production](https://you.ubc.ca/ubc_programs/film-production/) program\.

[Check out the work of emerging filmmakers](https://www.povfilmfest.com/)  

### Art on the Line

**Okanagan campus**

An annual gala and fundraiser, Art on the Line brings together the local arts community to celebrate the work of students, faculty, alumni, and artists practising in the community\.

[Enjoy live entertainment, good food, and great art](http://fccs.ok.ubc.ca/news-events/ongoing/art-on-the-line.html)  

### Opera Tea Series

**Vancouver campus**

Sip tea or coffee while you attend a concert of opera arias and song favourites in the theatre or the [UBC Botanical Garden](http://www.botanicalgarden.ubc.ca/)\.

[Enjoy opera in a casual setting](https://chancentre.com/events/opera-teas/)  

### Indigenous Art Intensive

**Okanagan campus**

UBC Okanagan’s Indigenous Art Intensive offers an educational series of courses, lectures, art shows, and opportunities to create art\. It features a series of world\-renowned speakers, a variety of related undergraduate and graduate credit courses, and a group of resident artists who will be working to create a new body of work\.

[Learn more about this month\-long residency](https://gallery.ok.ubc.ca/programming/indigenous-art-intensive/)  

## Blending Visual Arts with Computer Science in UBC Okanagan’s Bachelor of Media Studies

When Kai was in high school researching university programs, the Bachelor of Media Studies at UBC Okanagan was the interdisciplinary program that he was looking for\.

-   [Kai studying on his laptop](https://you.ubc.ca/wp-content/uploads/2023/02/StudentStory_KaiH-768x512.jpeg)
    
    “\[UBC Okanagan's Bachelor of Media Studies program is\] a very interesting degree because it takes a lot of practices from visual arts and computer science and blends them together\.\.\. it exposes you to so many different things and later it allows you to narrow things down and specialize in a certain digital field\.”
    
    Kelowna, Canada \| Bachelor of Media Studies
    
    [Read more](https://you.ubc.ca/ubc-life/blog/blending-visual-arts-with-computer-science-in-ubc-okanagans-bachelor-of-media-studies/)
    

## Arts and cultural spaces

[Chan Centre for the Performing Arts](https://you.ubc.ca/wp-content/uploads/2015/11/1-chan.jpg)

### Chan Centre for the Performing Arts

**Vancouver campus**

From classical, jazz, theatre, and opera to world music, the Chan Centre for the Performing Arts has earned an international reputation for its exceptional programming\.

[Check out concerts and events](http://chancentre.com/)  

[FINA Art Gallery](https://you.ubc.ca/wp-content/uploads/2015/11/3-fina.jpg)

### FINA Art Gallery

**Okanagan campus**

The FINA art gallery hosts exhibitions throughout the year – some by visiting artists, some by faculty members, and many by BFA and MFA students\.

[Discover original artwork by UBC faculty and students](https://fccs.ok.ubc.ca/about/studios/)  

[Museum of Anthropology](https://you.ubc.ca/wp-content/uploads/2015/11/5-anthro.jpg)

### Museum of Anthropology

**Vancouver campus**

The Museum of Anthropology, a place of extraordinary architectural beauty, features almost 10,000 objects from around the world, from massive totem poles to stunning pieces in wood and ceramic\.

[Discover provocative programming and vibrant exhibitions](http://moa.ubc.ca/)  

[Image](https://you.ubc.ca/wp-content/uploads/2015/11/university-theatre.jpg)

### University Theatre

**Okanagan campus**

The University Theatre presents quality live performances for the campus community and the general public\.

[Watch cutting\-edge live performance](https://events.ok.ubc.ca/venue/campus-administration-building-adm-university-theatre-adm026/)  

[Image](https://you.ubc.ca/wp-content/uploads/2015/11/2-belkin.jpg)

### Morris and Helen Belkin Art Gallery

**Vancouver campus**

Internationally recognized for its exhibitions, programs, and online projects, the Belkin Art Gallery is one of Canada’s premier showcases for contemporary art\.

[Explore contemporary art and approaches](http://belkin.ubc.ca/)  

[Frederic Wood Theatre](https://you.ubc.ca/wp-content/uploads/2015/11/4-fredwood.jpg)

### Frederic Wood Theatre

**Vancouver campus**

Award\-winning faculty join passionate undergraduates, graduate students, and doctoral candidates to produce insightful, invigorating, and innovative productions at the Frederic Wood Theatre\.

[Watch award\-winning faculty and students on stage](http://theatrefilm.ubc.ca/events/venues/frederic-wood-theatre/)  

[Visitors admiring art and the UBC Okanagan Gallery](https://you.ubc.ca/wp-content/uploads/2024/08/UBCOkanagan-gallery.jpg)

### UBC Okanagan Gallery

**Okanagan campus**

As a university gallery, managed and located within the Faculty of Creative and Critical Studies, the UBC Okanagan Gallery is committed to research\-creation, exhibitions, performance, publications, permanent collection and acquisitions, curatorial studies and community\-engaged programs\.

[Explore the gallery](https://gallery.ok.ubc.ca/)

content_markdown:
## The University of British Columbia \(UBC\) supports the protection of privacy\.

### Use of personal information

The personal information you provide through this website is collected pursuant to section 26 of the [Freedom of Information and Protection of Privacy Act](https://universitycounsel.ubc.ca/subject-areas/access-and-privacy-general/access-to-information/about-fippa/), RSBC 1996, c\.165\. The personal information is collected for recruitment purposes and other related UBC purposes that may include the following:

-   Providing information and advice on your course and program needs
-   Informing you of upcoming recruitment events
-   Providing ongoing service and assistance to understand your post\-secondary educational needs
-   Statistical purposes

Your personal information will only be accessible by authorized UBC employees and representatives, or as otherwise permitted by law\. UBC will not disclose your personal information to an outside third party unless permitted by law\.

At any time you can update your profile in this system to let us know if you no longer wish to receive emails, phone calls, and/or mailings from UBC recruitment offices, or to retire your record\. To indicate how you would like us to communicate with you, please [log in to the Future Student Portal](https://account.you.ubc.ca/login), go to your **Profile**, and update your **Communication preferences**\.

### Security

Your personal information is kept on a secure server located in Canada that is not available to the public\. If you are currently located outside Canada, UBC employees and representatives may also need to store and access your personal information outside Canada for the purposes listed above\.

Although UBC makes every effort to maintain the security of this website and your personal information, UBC cannot guarantee against, and is not responsible for, unauthorized access or fraudulent use of your personal information\.

UBC reserves the right to amend this statement at anytime without notice\.

For further information about this website and the collection of personal information, please [contact us](https://you.ubc.ca/contact-us/)\.

### Website information and online advertising

We may work with third parties, on occasion, using cookies, web beacons, and similar technologies to collect or receive information from this website and use that information to provide measurement services and targeted ads\. This helps us promote our website \(and UBC\) to those who have already shown an interest in UBC\.

You can opt out of this collection and use of information for ad targeting at any time: [Understanding Online Advertising](http://www.aboutads.info/consumers/ "Understanding Online Advertising")\.

### Legal information and terms of use

Visit [UBC’s legal information and terms of use](https://www.ubc.ca/site/legal.html?utm_campaign=UBC+CLF&utm_medium=CLF+Global+Footer&utm_source=http%3A%2F%2Fyou.ubc.ca%2Fprivacy%2F) for more information\.

title: UBC Life
content_markdown:
## Life on UBC’s Vancouver Campus

With popular beaches, international food, and a lively social scene, the campus is so easy to live on that some students say they hardly need to leave\.

UBC’s Vancouver campus is a vibrant community with almost 32,000 undergraduate students\. It feels like its own little city but it’s within easy reach of beaches, downtown, and mountains\. You can go from exploring a rainforest trail in [Pacific Spirit Regional Park](http://www.vancouvertrails.com/trails/pacific-spirit-regional-park/), to relaxing on Jericho Beach, to shopping on [Robson Street](http://robsonstreet.ca/) — all in one day\.

[Explore Vancouver Campus](http://you.ubc.ca/ubc-life/vancouver/)

## Life on UBC’s Okanagan campus

UBC’s Okanagan campus is an active, young community nestled among orchards, mountains, and beautiful lakes\. It’s an amazing place to live, learn, play, and grow\.

The Okanagan campus is a close\-knit community with over 7,000 undergraduate [students](http://essaylab.org/admission-essay/)\. That means you’ll see plenty of familiar faces in and around our new state\-of\-the\-art facilities\. And with all of the recreational and cultural opportunities nearby, there’s never a shortage of great things to do\.

title: Sports and recreation
content_markdown:
[http://you\.ubc\.ca/wp\-content/uploads/2013/06/SportsClubs1\.jpg](http://you.ubc.ca/wp-content/uploads/2013/06/SportsClubs1.jpg)[SportsClubs](http://you.ubc.ca/wp-content/uploads/2013/06/SportsClubs1.jpg)

From Olympic champions to professional superstars, UBC connects you to a tradition of sporting excellence\. Thanks to state of the art facilities and exceptional programs, the University has produced 231 Olympians, won 24 national swimming titles in the last 13 years, and claimed multiple championships in basketball, golf, soccer, volleyball, rowing, and field hockey over the past decade\.

What does this mean for you? Whether you’re an elite athlete or a casual competitor, UBC’s campuses offer you the opportunities and spaces necessary for an active lifestyle\. Take a look at the teams, classes, and varsity sports you can participate in\. Which will you choose?

### Varsity Teams and Opportunities

Go UBC, go\! The UBC Thunderbirds in Vancouver and UBC Heat in the Okanagan are powerful contenders in university athletics: our 37 varsity teams have claimed over 101 national championships, the highest of any Canadian university\. Considering that success, it’s no surprise that UBC has produced:

-   214 Olympic participants
-   Medal holders in Olympic and World competition
-   Major League Baseball draft picks
-   A world\-record holder in swimming \(Brian Johns\)

#### Our Teams

UBC Thunderbirds \(Vancouver campus\): Born in 1934, the UBC Thunderbirds represent a tradition of excellence in athletics and sportsmanship\. The Thunderbirds compete in 13 sports in two leagues – the [Canadian Interuniversity Sport](http://www.universitysport.ca/e/index.cfm) \(CIS\) league and the US\-based [National Association of Intercollegiate Athletics](http://naia.cstv.com/) \(NAIA\)\. Visit the [UBC Thunderbirds website](http://www.gothunderbirds.ca/) to see the full list of teams and sports represented\.

UBC Heat \(Okanagan campus\): The UBC Heat fields teams in basketball \(men’s and women’s\), soccer \(men’s and women’s\), and volleyball \(men’s and women’s\) in the [Canada West Universities Athletic Association](http://www.canadawest.org/landing/index) \(CWUAA or Canada West\)\. Canada West is one of four conferences in the CIS \([Canadian Interuniversity Sport](http://english.cis-sic.ca/landing/index)\), the governing body for the highest level of amateur sport in Canada\. The Heat men’s and women’s golf team, as well as the men’s and women’s cross country team, competes in the CCAA \([Canadian Collegiate Athletic Association](http://www.ccaa.ca/?language=en)\)\.

Interested in joining your campus’s varsity team? Contact the Head Coach of the sport you’re interested in to learn more about programs, scholarship opportunities, and open try\-outs at the beginning of the season\.

Team Pages: [UBC Thunderbirds](http://www.gothunderbirds.ca/) \| [UBC Heat](http://athletics.ok.ubc.ca/welcome.html)

### Intramurals and Recreation

Not every sports enthusiast is a high\-level varsity athlete\. At UBC, that’s not a problem because we have one of the largest intramural sports programs of any university in Canada\. Offering literally hundreds of choices, [UBC REC](http://www.rec.ubc.ca/) in Vancouver and [UBC Campus Recreation](http://ok.ubc.ca/athrec.html) in the Okanagan have something for everyone, whatever their skill level\. From 10\-person voyageur canoe races to the world’s largest indoor triathlon, UBC’s campuses hold more than 30 annual special events, intramural leagues in eight sports, and over 50 fitness, dance, and martial arts classes\. Whatever your chosen activity, intramurals and recreation at UBC offer you a great way to meet friends, get some exercise, and have fun\!

Campus recreation: [Vancouver](http://www.rec.ubc.ca/) \| [Okanagan](http://www.ubc.ca/okanagan/campusrec/welcome.html)

### Fitness Facilities and Venues

Whichever campus you call home, both UBC’s campuses offer state of the art fitness facilities and venues to keep you on your game\. We have everything from an Olympic winter sports centre and football stadium, to an outdoor turf field and multi\-court recreation centre\.

#### UBC Vancouver Campus Facilities

Take your pick of activities at the centrally located [Student Recreation Centre](http://www.rec.ubc.ca/src/index.cfm), which holds three full size gyms, a fitness centre, studio, and martial arts dojo\. If you’re more water inclined, head to the Aquatic Centre’s 50\-metre indoor pool complex or the John MS Leakey Boathouse for rowing on the Fraser River\. You can also visit the state of the art [Thunderbird Winter Sports Centre](http://www.recreation.ubc.ca/ice/), a 2010 Winter Olympics venue, for figure skating drop\-ins or a game of hockey\.

The Vancouver campus is located in a temperate climate, you can play outside year\-round on natural and artificial turf fields, a public golf course, indoor and outdoor tennis courts, or explore Pacific Spirit Park’s many hiking, running, and biking trails\. Venture off campus and you’ll discover the natural attractions Vancouver is known for: mountain hiking trails, beaches, parks, three local ski hills, and the world\-class Whistler Blackcomb Ski Resort\.

#### UBC Okanagan Campus Facilities

The [Recreation Facility](http://camprec.ok.ubc.ca/welcome.html) on the UBC Okanagan campus is one of the finest in British Columbia and has hosted many local, national, and international events\. Inside, the facility includes gymnasiums, weight room, cardio equipment, and sports medicine and massage therapy clinics\. Step outside and you’ll find tennis courts, an international size soccer pitch, beach volleyball courts, and a lit multi\-sport court\. UBC Okanagan is growing quickly and plans are in the works to construct a new fitness centre, additional gymnasium space, and artificial fields\.

Kelowna and the beautiful Okanagan Valley also provide students with plenty of outdoor recreational opportunities, including skiing, golfing, biking, rock climbing, sailing, and much more\.

title: Financial planning
content_markdown:
Your university education is a substantial investment\. At UBC, we recognize the significant contribution you and your family make toward your degree\. We’re here to provide financial advising and support through scholarships, bursaries, and other assistance programs\.

## Health Insurance at UBC

As a UBC student, you must have both basic and extended health insurance\. Find out how to make sure you have the right coverage\.

Learn about health insurance at UBC

## UBC Okanagan International Welcome Award

The UBC Okanagan International Welcome Award is a $5,000 award applied to international students’ first\-year tuition at UBC Okanagan\. The award is for international students who apply to UBC with a UBC Okanagan degree listed as their first choice and who are accepted and enrol into their first\-choice program\.

Find out more about the award

[Find out more about the award](https://you.ubc.ca/financial-planning/scholarships-awards-international-students/#section-6 "Find out more about the award")

Starting September 2026, new international students who enroll at UBC Okanagan will receive $8,000 for their first year, applied as credit towards tuition fees through the UBC Okanagan Global Elevation Award\.

Find out more about the award

[Find out more about the award](https://you.ubc.ca/financial-planning/scholarships-awards-international-students/#section-5 "Find out more about the award")

Start planning your finances

[Image](https://you.ubc.ca/wp-content/uploads/2013/06/ubc-first-year-tuition.jpg)

## What will your first year cost?

Attending university has costs beyond your tuition fees, and in order to prepare, it’s important to start your financial planning early\. To get a whole picture of what your first year of university will cost, you’ll need to consider tuition, books, meals, living costs, and more\.

[Start planning your finances](http://you.ubc.ca/financial-planning/cost/)

## Scholarships and awards

UBC is dedicated to recognizing outstanding students for academic excellence and leadership\. There are merit\-based and need\-based awards and scholarships available to Canadian and international students\.

### Scholarships and awards for Canadian students

Last year, UBC and its donors awarded $10 million to incoming UBC students for excellent grades, community and school involvement, and demonstrated leadership\.

[Learn more](http://you.ubc.ca/financial-planning/scholarships-awards-canadian-students/)  

### Scholarships and awards for international students

### Awards for Indigenous students

UBC has a dedicated Indigenous Awards program for Canadian Indigenous students, and has almost $100,000 in Major Entrance Scholarships for Indigenous secondary school students\.

[Learn more](https://you.ubc.ca/financial-planning/scholarships-awards-canadian-students/indigenous-students/)

title: What will your first year cost?
content_markdown:
## How to plan your first\-year costs

When planning for your university costs, it’s important to consider both your first\-year costs as well as how your costs may change in your second, third, and fourth years\. We know how stressful financial planning can be, so let’s take this one step at a time\. We’ll help you plan for your first year on this page\. Later, you can find more information about the costs of your second year and beyond by reading up on [undergraduate tuition fees at UBC](https://students.ubc.ca/enrolment/finances/tuition-fees/undergraduate-tuition-fees)\.

-   Calculate costs specific to you using our [online first\-year cost calculator](https://you.ubc.ca/financial-planning/cost/#cost-calculator)\. Add up the total for tuition, books, and living costs\.
-   Download and complete our first\-year [budget\-planning worksheet](https://you.ubc.ca/financial-planning/cost/#budget)\. \(This worksheet is for your own reference only\.\)
-   Let our [Enrolment Services Advisors](http://students.ubc.ca/enrolment/finances/funding-your-studies/financial-advice) \(Vancouver\) and [Student Services and Financial Support](https://students.ok.ubc.ca/courses-money-enrolment/finances/) \(Okanagan\) help you and your family develop a financial plan\. If you’d like to schedule a financial advising appointment, [contact us](http://you.ubc.ca/contact-us/)\.
-   See our [fees and due dates](http://you.ubc.ca/financial-planning/financial-schedule/) for important fee deadlines in your first year\.
-   If you’re an international student and you wish to pay your UBC fees in your home currency, you’re encouraged to do so\. Our [international funds transfer method](https://students.ubc.ca/enrolment/finances/paying-tuition "UBC Student Services") allows you to lock into an exchange rate for 72 hours, during which time you can transfer funds to UBC via Western Union Business Solutions\.

**[First\-year budget\-planning worksheet](https://you.ubc.ca/wp-content/uploads/2018/08/ubc-budget-planning-worksheet.pdf)**

94 KB PDF

Download this fillable PDF template

## First\-year cost calculator

This is where you can calculate your financial plan and find your program’s tuition for your first year at UBC\.

Try as many options as you want\. The numbers will be updated each time you click the **Calculate** button\. All fees and costs are current estimates and are **based on a first\-year full course load**\. If you are pursuing a [Bachelor \+ Master of Management dual degree](https://you.ubc.ca/ubc_programs/master-management-dual-degree/), you’ll need to add $1,480\.50 \(Canadian citizens and permanent residents of Canada\) or $2,249\.90 \(international students\) to your first\-year tuition total below\.

### Looking ahead to second year and beyond?

Tuition is calculated on a per\-credit basis\. [Tuition fees are reviewed annually](https://students.ubc.ca/enrolment/finances/tuition-fees/undergraduate-tuition-fees) by the Board of Governors\. In recent years, tuition increases have been 2% for continuing domestic students and between 2% and 5% for continuing international students\.

*First\-year cost calculator fees last updated May 2021\.*

title: Presidential Scholars Awards
content_markdown:
UBC is looking for the most accomplished and promising Canadian citizens and permanent residents to join our community\. The Presidential Scholars Award program offers the most prestigious awards available to students who are entering UBC\. These include a one\-time award of approximately $5,000, and renewable awards of up to $40,000 on the Okanagan campus, and $80,000 on the Vancouver campus, each payable over four years\.

## Are you eligible?

High school and CEGEP students who are Canadian citizens and permanent residents are eligible for the Presidential Scholars Award\. These awards recognize students who excel across the board and who have demonstrated academic and leadership achievements in the arts, community, athletics, and school\.

## How do you apply?

Students wishing to be considered for a Presidential Scholars Award must apply to UBC by **December 1****,** and indicate that they would like to be considered for the award when asked in their [UBC application](https://myapplication.ubc.ca/apply)\. All sections of the [online application](https://you.ubc.ca/applying-ubc/how-to-apply/ubcs-online-application/) must be completed by December 1, including paying the admission fee, in order to qualify\.

All high school applicants will be evaluated for the Presidential Scholars Award for their first\-choice degree based on their [Academic Profile](http://you.ubc.ca/applying-ubc/how-to-apply/ubcs-online-application/ "UBC’s Online Application"), [Personal Profile](http://you.ubc.ca/applying-ubc/how-to-apply/personal-profile/ "Personal Profile"), and “scholarship short answer” sections of the online application\. We will not evaluate second\-choice degrees for a Presidential Scholars Award\.

## When will you be notified?

UBC will contact the majority of Presidential Scholars Award winners by the end of day on **April 27**\. Only successful award applicants will be contacted\.

title: Schulich Leader Scholarships
content_markdown:
The Schulich Leader Scholarships program recognizes students across Canada who demonstrate excellence in academics, leadership, charisma, and creativity, and plan to study in a STEM \(Science, Technology, Engineering, Mathematics\) area on either of UBC’s campuses during their undergraduate degree\.

Schulich Leader Scholarships were created by Canadian business leader and philanthropist Seymour Schulich and are managed by the UJA Federation of Greater Toronto\. Mr\. Schulich is a noted entrepreneur and philanthropist who believes strongly in supporting young people in their pursuit of science and technology\.

[Read about one Schulich Scholarship winner](http://you.ubc.ca/ubc-life/blog/vivians-story/ "Vivian’s Schulich story"), Vivian Tsang, who describes how the scholarship helped her to fulfill her academic dreams, or discover the stories of other UBC Schulich Scholars in the video below:

[Embedded iframe \(view source\)](https://www.youtube.com/embed/9j8NLKVj-n0)

## Are you eligible?

To be eligible, you must:

-   Be a Canadian citizen or permanent resident of Canada who is graduating from a Canadian high school, secondary school, or CEGEP in the 2021/2022 academic year\.
-   Be nominated by your high school, secondary school, or CEGEP\.
-   Meet the following criteria:
    1.  Academic excellence; **and**
    2.  Leadership, charisma, and creativity\.
-   Be entrepreneurial\-minded and intend to pursue a career in one or more of the focus areas of technology, engineering, entrepreneurship and business enterprise, and applied scientific research\.
-   Not be pursuing a career as a practicing physician and/or medical researcher \(e\.g\., doctor, dentist, nurse, psychologist, pharmacist, optometrist, etc\), and not intend to become a professor and conduct theoretical research\.
-   Not be focusing on activism \(i\.e\., environmental, political, or societal\)\.

Strong consideration will be given to students with financial need\.

### Eligible degree programs

To be eligible, you must apply to one of the STEM faculties listed below:

**UBC’s Okanagan campus**

-   Faculty of Applied Science \(includes Engineering\)
-   Faculty of Science

**UBC’s Vancouver campus**

-   Faculty of Applied Science \(includes Engineering\)
-   Faculty of Land and Food Systems
-   Faculty of Science

## Award value

Schulich Leader Scholarships in Engineering are valued at $100,000\. Recipients will receive annual payments of $25,000 over a period of four years if all renewal criteria are met\.

Schulich Leader Scholarships in STEM faculties outside of Engineering are valued at $80,000\. Recipients will receive annual payments of $20,000 over a period of four years if all renewal criteria are met\.

## How do you apply?

High school, secondary school, or CEGEP students in their final year of study are eligible to be selected by their respective schools as Schulich Leader nominees\. High schools may nominate one student per year; CEGEPs may nominate up to four students\.

For information on the application process, please visit the [Schulich Leader Scholarships](http://www.schulichleaders.com/) website\.

## When is the deadline?

The 2022/23 Schulich Leaders nomination period closes on **January 26, 2022** in Canada\. 

Nominees must submit a separate online Schulich Leader application by **February 16, 2022**\. A link to this application will be emailed by representatives from the Schulich Leader Scholarships office\. All letters of reference must be completed and received by the same date\.

## When will the winners be announced?

Schulich Leader Scholarship winners will be notified on or before **June 15, 2022**\.

title: Bursaries
content_markdown:
Bursaries are non\-repayable awards that are given to students on the basis of financial need\. At UBC, the following two bursary programs are available:

## General Bursaries

[UBC’s General Bursary program](http://students.ubc.ca/enrolment/finances/awards/ubc-bursary) is designed to help fill your “unmet need,” which is the gap between 1\) your assessed educational and living costs, and 2\) your available government assistance and expected financial contributions\.

This program covers most bursaries available to UBC students\. If you are entering UBC directly from high school or transferring from another college or university and you have unmet financial need, you should consider applying for both the bursary program and the Centennial Scholars Entrance Awards\.

### Are you eligible?

To be eligible, you must be a Canadian citizen or permanent resident who has a student loan and an unmet financial need\. Students in undergraduate, post\-baccalaureate, and graduate programs are all eligible unless the program is [designated as a professional program](https://academic.ubc.ca/bursary-support-designated-graduate-programs)\.

### How do you apply?

To apply, login to the [Student Service Centre](http://www.students.ubc.ca/ssc) and click **Apply for Bursary**\.

### When is the deadline?

If you’re starting your studies in September, the deadline is **September 15**\. If you’re starting in May, the deadline is **June 1**\.

Your student loans must be confirmed by the bursary deadline to be eligible for UBC bursaries\. To ensure you meet this deadline, we strongly recommend you apply for your student loans by **July 15** for Winter Session and **March 31** for Summer Session bursaries\.

If you have questions or need assistance, contact an [Enrolment Services Advisor](https://students.ubc.ca/about-student-services/enrolment-services-advisors) \(Vancouver campus\) or email [sis\.ubco@ubc\.ca](mailto:sis.ubco@ubc.ca) \(Okanagan campus\)\.

---

## Affiliation Bursaries

There are many different Affiliation Bursaries\. Eligibility for these bursaries is usually determined by connection to a specific club, trade union, company, geographic region, or demographic group\. The requirements for each bursary are unique\.

### Are you eligible?

To be eligible, you must be a Canadian citizen or permanent resident\. To determine your full eligibility for Affiliation Bursaries, complete an application and review the requirements for each award\.

### How do you apply?

You can apply for Affiliation Bursaries by completing the application on the [UBC Affiliation Bursaries web page](https://students.ubc.ca/enrolment/finances/awards-scholarships-bursaries/affiliation-bursaries)\.

This program requires a separate application from the General Bursaries\.

### When is the deadline?

The deadline to apply is **September 15**\.

If you have questions or need assistance, contact an [Enrolment Services Advisor](https://students.ubc.ca/about-student-services/enrolment-services-advisors) \(Vancouver campus\) or email [sis\.ubco@ubc\.ca](mailto:sis.ubco@ubc.ca) \(Okanagan campus\)\.

title: Work programs
content_markdown:
For many students, working part\-time while studying is a great way to earn some extra cash, meet new people, and get a break from studying\. UBC has programs that create well\-paid, on\-campus jobs for Canadian and international students\. Our on\-campus employers are flexible when it comes to working around exam and study schedules\.

## Work Learn and Work Study

With the popular [Work Learn](http://students.ubc.ca/career/campus-experiences/work-learn) and [Work Study](http://students.ok.ubc.ca/careers/services/jobs/workstudy.html) programs, you have the opportunity to develop professional skills and learn in a work environment\. To be eligible, you must be registered in courses at UBC and have a valid UBC student number\. Students can work in only one Work Learn position at any given time\.

The programs run from September to April during the Winter Session, and from May to August in the Summer Session\. For more information, including additional eligibility requirements for international students, visit the links below:

Vancouver Campus: [Work Learn](http://students.ubc.ca/career/campus-experiences/work-learn) \| Okanagan Campus: [Work Study](http://students.ok.ubc.ca/careers/services/jobs/workstudy.html)

## Co\-Op Education Program

Get valuable work experience in the field you’re studying with four, eight, twelve, and sixteen\-month paid co\-op terms\. With past employers such as the Canadian Space Agency, Microsoft, PepsiCo, and Adidas, co\-op experiences give you the foundation for a successful career after you graduate\.

Learn more about [Co\-Op Education Programs at UBC](http://www.coop.ubc.ca/)

## Undergraduate Research

You don’t have to be a graduate student to have your research taken seriously at UBC\. Apply for an undergraduate research award for a chance to work directly with professors, gain valuable academic work experience, and discover new research passions of your own\.

Learn about [Undergraduate Research Awards](http://students.ubc.ca/career/campus-experiences/undergraduate-research/NSERC-USRA)

title: Loans for Canadian and US students
content_markdown:
## Loans for Canadian students

Student loans are government\-funded financial assistance that you repay after completing your studies\. Student loans are beneficial because while you are registered in full\-time studies you are not required to make payments on your loan\. Instead, the government pays your interest during this time\. This means you can focus on your education instead of on managing your debt load\.

### Are you eligible?

If you’re Canadian, you’re eligible to apply for federal and provincial loans\. It’s important to keep in mind that to receive a loan or qualify for interest\-free status \(the government pays the interest on your loan\), you need to take at least 60% of a full\-time course load\. Dropping below the 60% threshold can cause you to lose your funding and have to begin repayment\.

### How do you apply?

You apply directly to the government assistance provider in your home province \(where you have been living before starting full\-time post\-secondary education\)\. This is a one\-stop process that considers you for both federal and provincial assistance\. For information on student loans in your home province, please see the list below\.

If you are a Canadian living abroad, apply through the Canadian province in which your parent or sponsor last lived\.

We encourage you to apply for student loans before **July 15** to ensure funds are available for September\.

### Contact us

If you have questions or need assistance, contact an [Enrolment Services Advisor](https://students.ubc.ca/about-student-services/enrolment-services-advisors) \(Vancouver campus\) or email [sis\.ubco@ubc\.ca](mailto:sis.ubco@ubc.ca) \(Okanagan campus\)\.

---

## Loans for US students

UBC is an approved Title IV institution\. US students can access funding through the William D\. Ford Federal Direct Loan Program\.

US students must apply for loans through the US government\. Dual citizens \(citizens of both the US and Canada\) may be able to apply for loans through both the US and Canadian governments\.

-   [US loans for students](https://students.ubc.ca/enrolment/finances/student-loans/loans-us)

The types of funding available through the Direct Loan Program are direct subsidized and direct unsubsidized loans \(previously Stafford loans\) and direct PLUS loans for parents \(previously parent PLUS loans\)\. UBC students are not eligible for Pell grants, Perkins loans, or other types of US Federal financial aid\.

We recommend that you submit UBC’s [US Loan Request form](https://webforms.students.ubc.ca/enrolment/finances/us-loans) by **June 30** to ensure loan funding for September\.

If you have questions or need assistance, contact an [Enrolment Services Advisor](https://students.ubc.ca/about-student-services/enrolment-services-advisors) \(Vancouver campus\) or email [sis\.ubco@ubc\.ca](mailto:sis.ubco@ubc.ca) \(Okanagan campus\)\.

title: Awards for students with disabilities
content_markdown:
UBC is committed to creating a welcoming and accessible community where all students can participate fully and are supported in realizing their potential\. To that end, we provide over 20 awards to students with disabilities\. These awards range in value and eligibility criteria\. A complete list of these awards is available on the application form\.

### Are you eligible?

To be eligible, you must:

-   Be a student with a disability and provide supporting documentation where required
-   Demonstrate financial need by fully answering all questions in the application \(for bursaries\)

Between August and September, applications are available on the [Awards for students with disabilities](https://students.ubc.ca/enrolment/finances/awards-scholarships-bursaries/awards-disabilities) page\. You may need to provide supporting documentation in some cases\.

The deadline to apply is September 15\. If you’re successful, you’ll hear from us by late November\.

### Presidential Scholars Awards

UBC has over $437,000 in Presidential Scholars Awards dedicated for Indigenous secondary school students, including renewable scholarships up to $40,000 each and one\-time awards up to $7,500 each\.

For more information on how to apply, please visit the [Presidential Scholars Awards](https://you.ubc.ca/financial-planning/scholarships-awards-canadian-students/presidential-scholars/) page\. Indigenous students who apply before the deadline will be considered for both general and Indigenous\-specific Presidential Scholars Awards\.

### Musqueam First Nation Scholarships

To acknowledge the strong relationship UBC has with the Musqueam First Nation, the President’s Office created this community\-based scholarship that will support students from the Musqueam First Nation in their undergraduate, post baccalaureate, or graduate studies\. The award is valued up to $5,500 annually and renewable for up to four years\.

Recipients will have demonstrated academic and leadership achievements including, but not limited to, engagement in the arts, athletics, school, and/or their community\. Recipients will be selected based on their ability to demonstrate their openness to continuing to learn who they are, where they come from, and their responsibility in enriching and carrying forward knowledge in their community and in the world\.

For more information on how to apply, please visit the [Musqueam First Nation Scholarship](https://students.ubc.ca/finances/awards-scholarships-bursaries/musqueam-first-nation-scholarship/) page\.

### UBC Centennial Scholars Entrance Awards

The UBC Centennial Scholars Entrance Award program assists students in transition from secondary school and other post\-secondary institutions to UBC\. The purpose of this program is to support academically qualified students who show an interest in joining the UBC community, but who would not otherwise be able to attend without significant financial assistance\. Through the program, new students can access a variety of one\-time and renewable awards of up to $80,000\.

For more information on how to apply, please visit the [UBC Centennial Scholars Entrance Award](http://you.ubc.ca/financial-planning/scholarships-awards-canadian-students/entrance-award/) page\. Indigenous students who apply before the deadline will be considered for both general and Indigenous\-specific Centennial Scholars Entrance Awards\.

### Indigenous Awards

If you are Indigenous \(First Nations, Inuit, and/or Métis\), you’re also eligible for a range of dedicated [scholarships, bursaries, and awards](https://students.ubc.ca/finances/awards-scholarships-bursaries/awards-indigenous/) specifically for Indigenous students\. The value, criteria, and deadlines vary by award, so please review details carefully\.

## Program\-specific Indigenous awards

### The Centre for Excellence in Indigenous Health Awards

[The Centre for Excellence in Indigenous Health](https://health.indigenous.ubc.ca/students/awards/) has awards for Indigenous students who are pursuing a degree in health sciences on UBC’s Vancouver campus\. The majority of the awards range from $750 to $2500 with one of the awards being for $10,000\.

### The Spitz Family Awards for Indigenous Women

A cornerstone of the [Spitz Fellows Program](https://www.sauder.ubc.ca/bachelor-commerce/overview/spitz-fellows-program) is The Spitz Family Awards for Indigenous Women\. These are renewable awards of $10,000 per academic year, with additional funding available for Fellows, based on financial need, for other student expenses\. The program recognizes direct\-entry and transfer students who demonstrate academic achievement, community engagement, tenacity, leadership skills, and service to others\.

## Need help with financial planning?

Having a financial plan is just as important as having an academic plan\. We have [online resources](http://you.ubc.ca/financial-planning/cost/) and advisors to help you\. If you are an Indigenous student who requires help with financial planning, awards, or sponsorship billing, please contact:

Recruiter Advisor, Indigenous Students  
604\.827\.2135  
[chloe\.erlendson@ubc\.ca](mailto:chloe.erlendson@ubc.ca)

title: Clubs and societies
content_markdown:
Joining a student\-run club is a terrific way to try something new, meet others with interests similar to yours, gain marketable skills like event organization, and have fun\.

## Student Government

UBC’s two campuses each have their own student governments that administer student\-run clubs, resource centres, and services\. There are lots of ways to get involved with your student government – apply for a paid position, volunteer, or run for a student leadership position in the annual elections\. Learn more getting involved with student government: Student Government: [Alma Mater Society](http://www.ams.ubc.ca/) \(AMS\) – Vancouver \| [University of British Columbia Students’ Union Okanagan](http://www.ubcsuo.ca/) \(UBCSUO\) – Okanagan

## Clubs

If you want to meet other like\-minded students, why not join a student\-run club? With over 400 clubs at UBC’s two campuses, there’s a good chance you’ll find one that matches your interests\. If you don’t see the club you’re looking for, start a new one\!

Here are some examples of student\-run clubs you can join:

-   Groups based on an academic major, such as the award\-winning International Relations Students Association or the Pre\-Med Club
-   Groups based on cultural interests, such as the Le Club Français or the Chinese Varsity Club
-   Clubs based on hobbies or sports, such as the Ski and Board Club and the Mountain Riders
-   Politically affiliated clubs, such as the Federal Young Liberals of UBC
-   Groups based around a religion, such as the the University Christian Ministry and the Muslim Students Association
-   And many, many more clubs

Clubs at UBC: [Vancouver](http://www.ams.ubc.ca/clubs/) \| [Okanagan](http://www.ubcsuo.ca/get-involved/student-associations/clubs/)

## Faculty Societies & Course Unions

Get out of the classroom and meet other students in your faculty or field by joining an undergraduate faculty society or course union\.

Vancouver: [Undergraduate Student Societies](http://www.ams.ubc.ca/leadership/faculty-societies/) \| Okanagan: [Course Unions](http://www.ubcsuo.ca/get-involved/student-associations/)

title: Leadership and volunteering
content_markdown:
[http://you\.ubc\.ca/wp\-content/uploads/2013/06/LeadershipVolunteer1\.jpg](http://you.ubc.ca/wp-content/uploads/2013/06/LeadershipVolunteer1.jpg)[LeadershipVolunteer](http://you.ubc.ca/wp-content/uploads/2013/06/LeadershipVolunteer1.jpg)

Ask any current UBC student – one of the smartest things you can do while at UBC is to get involved on campus\. In fact, studies show that students who participate in student life tend to do better in their academics as well\. Between UBC programs, student government, and the hundreds of student\-run clubs available, you’ll be sure to find others on campus with interests similar to your own\.

What makes a great leader? How can you be part of the solution to local, international, and environmental challenges? UBC has created leadership programs that give you opportunities to challenge yourself, make a difference, and learn new skills\.

## Learn to Lead

Prime Ministers\. Nobel Laureates\. CEOs\. Olympians\. UBC has been educating leaders for almost a century\. Our [leadership programs](http://students.ubc.ca/about/go-global/go-global-leadership-programs) can help you become one\.

-   Student Leadership Conferences – The largest of their kind in Canada, these events are held annually in Vancouver each January, and in the Okanagan each November\. With over 1,200 potential and current student leaders in attendance, the Student Leadership Conferences are an exceptional opportunity to network, gain new skills, and learn from other like\-minded peers\. These are not events to be missed\!

## Give Back

Volunteering is a great way to develop skills you can put to use both at UBC and after you graduate\.

-   [Centre for Community Engaged Learning](http://students.ubc.ca/about/centre-community-engaged-learning#student-programs "UBC - Centre for Community Engaged Learning") – Offers programs that place students in community settings \(non\-profits and inner city schools\) either as a required part of an academic course, or through voluntary co\-curricular placements like Trek, Reading Week and International Service Learning for a hands\-on, immersive experience\.
-   International Volunteering – Through [Go Volunteer: International Community\-Based Learning](http://www.students.ubc.ca/global/learning-abroad/international-service-learning/), part of UBC’s [Go Global: International Learning Programs](http://www.students.ubc.ca/global), you can participate in international community projects around the world\. Projects range from microfinance in South Africa and protecting endangered sea life in Greece to working at rural schools in Chile and caring for orphans in Madagascar\. Get hands\-on experience while you learn about international development issues and the role you can play in the global community\. Some placements may contribute to UBC academic credit\. The Global Service Learning Endowment supports the efforts of UBC students who help communities in need around the world\.
-   [AMS Connect](http://www.ams.ubc.ca/vex) – AMS Connect can match your skills and goals with volunteer and internship positions\.

## Keep it Green

Surrounded by forest, mountains, and ocean, it’s no surprise that UBC is a world leader in the [campus sustainability](http://www.sustain.ubc.ca/) movement\. You can do your part by taking the [Campus Sustainability Pledge](http://www.sustain.ubc.ca/sustainable_u/)\.
