-   [Complete the application](https://you.ubc.ca/applying-ubc/how-to-apply/application/)
-   [Disability\-related considerations](https://you.ubc.ca/applying-ubc/how-to-apply/disability/)
-   [Working with an education agent](https://you.ubc.ca/applying-ubc/how-to-apply/working-with-an-education-agent/)

## On this page:

-   [Disclosing your disability](https://you.ubc.ca/applying-ubc/how-to-apply/disability/#section-1)
-   [Special Consideration for Undergraduate Admissions](https://you.ubc.ca/applying-ubc/how-to-apply/disability/#section-2)
-   [STEPS Forward](https://you.ubc.ca/applying-ubc/how-to-apply/disability/#section-3)

## Disclosing your disability

You are under no obligation to disclose your disability in your application to UBC unless you believe your disability will impact your ability to meet the academic standards of your degree of study\. In order to access disability\-related accommodations, please register with the [Disability Resource Centre](http://students.ok.ubc.ca/drc/welcome.html) on the Okanagan campus or the [Centre for Accessibility](https://students.ubc.ca/access) on the Vancouver campus\.

## Special Consideration for Undergraduate Admissions

Applicants to UBC have very strong academic records\. You must meet both general admission requirements as well as degree\-specific requirements\. Many applicants with disabilities meet UBC’s admission requirements and are admitted directly to their degree of choice\. However, if an unsupported or recently\-diagnosed disability has impacted your ability to meet the admission requirements of your degree of choice, you can apply for special consideration for admission\.

Special consideration for admission may be granted if, for example, your academic performance has been affected because:

-   You have been recently diagnosed with a disability\.
-   Your disability was not accommodated completely or appropriately\.

If you have received appropriate accommodations for your disability throughout your studies, you may not be eligible for UBC’s special consideration for admission\.

### How to apply

To apply for special consideration for admission, please [review the list of eligible circumstances and complete the online form](https://ubc.ca1.qualtrics.com/jfe/form/SV_23QDxFpq0PjHEp0)\. Complete this form no later than the admission application deadline for your degree\.

### Contact us

For more information, contact the [Disability Resource Centre](https://students.ok.ubc.ca/drc/welcome.html) on the Okanagan campus or the [Centre for Accessibility](https://students.ubc.ca/about-student-services/centre-for-accessibility) on the Vancouver campus\.

**Note:** Some UBC faculties have different processes for special consideration for admission\. Please contact your faculty directly for more information\.

## STEPS Forward

If you have developmental or intellectual disabilities and are interested in attending post\-secondary education in a way that supports your strengths and learning style, you can study at UBC through an inclusive post\-secondary initiative with [STEPS Forward\.](https://www.bc-ipse.org/)

### What is STEPS Forward?

STEPS Forward’s BC Initiative for Inclusive Post\-Secondary Education \(BC\-IPSE\) provides support for students with developmental disabilities to access post\-secondary education\.

If you are eligible, you may enrol in UBC courses for four years in a specific area of study\. You’ll be part of the same classes, tutorials, and labs as UBC students studying for their degrees, but as a participating auditor: a status that allows your assignments and exams to be modified to suit your individual learning style\. You’ll also be supported by STEPS Forward inclusion facilitators at UBC to engage fully in your courses\. At the end of your studies, you’ll receive a Certificate of Completion at convocation alongside students earning their Bachelor’s degree in the same field\.

During your time at UBC, you’ll enjoy student life in the same clubs and social spaces as other undergraduates, and be supported in individualized ways to make decisions about what you want to explore on campus\.

Over the summer months \(April to August\), STEPS Forward will help you to find paid work, internships, training, networking, and other volunteer opportunities that relate to your career goals\.

### Who is eligible?

There are no minimum academic requirements to be accepted – instead, STEPS Forward will look at your desire to learn and have a typical student experience\. The initiative is committed to supporting the inclusion of students with significant and/or complex support needs\.

[Discover more](https://www.bc-ipse.org/uploads/6/2/0/8/62081869/2015_11_selection_criteria.pdf) about the criteria used to select students\.

### How to apply

1.  **Get in touch with us** to find out more about whether accessing your studies through UBC’s inclusive post\-secondary initiative \(STEPS Forward\) is right for you:
    -   If you’re interested in attending UBC Okanagan, contact Tiffany Thesen\-Yee at [tiffany@steps\-forward\.org](mailto:tiffany@steps-forward.org)or Vanessa Ly at [vanessa@steps\-forward\.org](mailto:vanessa@steps-forward.org)\.
    -   If you’re interested in attending UBC Vancouver, contact Elly Callele at [elly@steps\-forward\.org](mailto:elly@steps-forward.org) or Selena Mah at [selena@steps\-forward\.org](mailto:selena@steps-forward.org)\.

2.  **Attend an interview**\. The interview is a way for us to learn more about what you want to get out of post\-secondary education\. You’ll be asked questions about what you’re hoping to gain from the experience and how you’ll grow from UBC’s academic teaching and student life\. TIP: Before your interview, think about topics such as:
    -   What makes you feel great about going to school?
    -   Why do you want to continue your education after high school?
    -   How do you want to get involved with sports, clubs, and campus events?
    -   How can you get the most out of being a student with facilitator support?

3.  **Receive your offer\.** About a month after your interview, we’ll contact you to let you know if you are accepted\. If your application is successful, STEPS Forward will set up a series of meetings with you over the summer to prepare with you and your chosen family, advocates, or allies\.

title: After you've applied
content_markdown:
Every year UBC reviews more than 40,000 applications and sends out admissions decisions from December through to April\. After you submit your application, you may still have to submit additional documents\. This waiting period is a great time to tour the campus and plan your finances\.

### More on Applying to UBC:

-   [Admission requirements](https://you.ubc.ca/applying-ubc/requirements/)
-   [Indigenous admissions](https://you.ubc.ca/applying-ubc/indigenous-admissions/)
-   [How to apply](https://you.ubc.ca/applying-ubc/how-to-apply/)
-   [After you've applied](https://you.ubc.ca/applying-ubc/applied/)
-   [After you’ve been admitted](https://you.ubc.ca/applying-ubc/admitted/)
-   [What we look for](https://you.ubc.ca/applying-ubc/application-evaluation/)
-   [Dates and deadlines](https://you.ubc.ca/applying-ubc/dates-deadlines/)

## Watch: You've applied to UBC\. Now what?

Find out what happens after you’ve submitted your application, what you can do while you wait, and how to check your admission status\.

[Embedded video \(view source\)](https://you.ubc.ca/applying-ubc/applied/)[Media source](https://you.ubc.ca/wp-content/uploads/2025/05/Youve-applied-to-UBC.-Now-what_.mp4)Embedded video \(view source\)[English](https://you.ubc.ca/wp-content/uploads/2025/05/youapplied-nowwhat-captions.vtt)Embedded video \(view source\)

## Check your status

While we’re [evaluating your application](https://you.ubc.ca/applying-ubc/applied/application-evaluation/), you can log in to the Applicant Service Centre anytime for updates on your application status, upcoming deadlines, and outstanding documents and fees\. To access the Applicant Service Centre, you’ll need your EducationPlannerBC \(EPBC\) log in that you created during the application process\.

By May, UBC has offered admission to as many students as possible\. We won’t know if there are additional spaces to fill until all of those students have decided whether or not to accept their offers\. If you see in your Applicant Service Centre account that you have been waitlisted, there’s nothing left to do except wait a little longer\. We will notify you if a space becomes available\. If you wish to appeal an admission decision from UBC, please review the [formal appeals process](https://you.ubc.ca/applying-ubc/applied/admission-appeals/)\.

[Visit the Applicant Service Centre](https://myapplication.ubc.ca/)

## Submit your documents

UBC requires certain academic information to evaluate your application and determine whether you’ll receive an offer of admission\. Your document requirements will vary depending on where you’re applying from and what degree\(s\) you’ve applied to\.

[Review your document requirements](https://you.ubc.ca/applying-ubc/applied/submit-documents/)

## Check your first\-year credit eligibility

If you complete university\-level courses while in high school, you may be eligible for first\-year credit at UBC\. Find out if any of your Advanced Placement, British\-patterned education, or International Baccalaureate courses qualify\.

[Check for first\-year credit](https://you.ubc.ca/applying-ubc/applied/first-year-credit/)

## Plan your finances

It’s never too early to start planning your finances\. Use our online cost calculator to get a sense of your educational and living costs in first year, and start mapping out your [financial support](https://you.ubc.ca/financial-planning/)\. In addition to scholarships and awards, there are a number of ways to help, such as loans, bursaries, work programs, and more\.

[Start planning your finances](https://you.ubc.ca/financial-planning/cost/)

## Attend an event or tour

Sign up for a UBC applicant information event in your area, get your questions answered in an online information session, or come to the Okanagan or Vancouver for a campus tour\.

[Discover events and tours](https://account.you.ubc.ca/s/events)

## On this page:

-   [Admission requirements](https://you.ubc.ca/applying-ubc/application-evaluation/#section-2)
-   [Your grades](https://you.ubc.ca/applying-ubc/application-evaluation/#section-3)

-   [For post\-secondary transfer applicants](https://you.ubc.ca/applying-ubc/application-evaluation/#section-6)

## Watch: How UBC evaluates your application

You’ve applied to UBC\. Now what? Behind the scenes, UBC’s Undergraduate Admissions Office is taking a closer look at your application, including your grades, the courses you chose, and your personal profile\.

[Embedded content: How UBC evaluates your application](https://www.youtube.com/embed/olbxAIuVt_M?feature=oembed)

## Admission requirements

First, we make sure you meet UBC’s [admission requirements](https://you.ubc.ca/applying-ubc/requirements/)\. Have you graduated from high school? Can you demonstrate a certain level of English? Do you meet the specific requirements for the degree you’re applying to? If you meet these admission requirements, we take a closer look at your application\.

## Your grades

UBC considers your grades in all Grade 11 \(junior level\) and Grade 12 \(senior level\) classes, paying special attention to courses that relate to the degree you’re applying to\. Specifically:

-   **We look at your grades in all academic courses\.** That doesn’t include career education courses, physical and health education courses, faith\-based courses, skills\-based courses, or courses in applied design and technology\. To encourage you to explore subjects outside your comfort zone, we’ll exclude your lowest grade \(as long as the course is not a degree\-specific requirement or relevant to your intended area of study at UBC\)\.
-   **We look at your grades in courses that fall under key subject categories related to your chosen degree\.** Check the admission requirements for your chosen degree to see which of the following subject categories apply: Language Arts, Mathematics and Computation, Sciences, Second Languages, Social Studies, and Visual and Performing Arts\. If you completed a Grade 11 \(junior level\) and Grade 12 \(senior level\) course in the same subject, we’ll focus on the Grade 12 \(senior level\) grade\.
-   **We look at your grades in key courses\.** Your key courses will be determined by your chosen degree, but English 12 \(senior\-level English\) or Pre\-Calculus 12 \(senior\-level Calculus\) are among the most common\.

## Your course choices

UBC also looks closely at which courses you chose to take in high school\.

-   Did you pursue all of your academic interests by taking a range of different subjects?
-   Did you challenge yourself by taking academic courses, advanced courses, or first\-year university courses?
-   Did you demonstrate knowledge in your chosen area of study by taking courses related to the degree you applied to at UBC?

## Your achievements beyond academics

The [personal profile](https://you.ubc.ca/applying-ubc/how-to-apply/personal-profile/) is an important part of UBC’s online application\. It is required for most high school applicants, and for university or college transfer students applying to certain programs\. It gives us a sense of who you are, what you’ve overcome, and what you’ve achieved\. It also helps us assess whether you’re prepared for university studies and deserving of an entrance scholarship or award by telling us what you’ve learned about your experiences, your academic and extracurricular achievements, and your leadership qualities\.

## For post\-secondary transfer applicants

If you are a well\-qualified student attending a post\-secondary institution, we welcome your application to [transfer to UBC](https://you.ubc.ca/applying-ubc/requirements/university-college-transfer/)\. UBC may assess post\-secondary applicants on a combination of factors, including your grade point average \(GPA\), any required prerequisite courses, and a review of your overall academic history\. We may also require you to submit a [personal profile](https://you.ubc.ca/applying-ubc/how-to-apply/personal-profile/), supplemental application, portfolio, or audition\.

title: Submit your documents
content_markdown:
After you’ve applied to UBC, you must submit certain academic information in order for UBC to evaluate your application and determine whether you’ll receive an offer of admission\.

### More on After you’ve applied:

-   [Admissions decisions](https://you.ubc.ca/applying-ubc/applied/admissions-decisions/)
-   [Submit your documents](https://you.ubc.ca/applying-ubc/applied/submit-documents/)
-   [First\-year credit](https://you.ubc.ca/applying-ubc/applied/first-year-credit/)
-   [First\-year study options](https://you.ubc.ca/applying-ubc/applied/first-year-study-options/)
-   [How to change the degree you applied to](https://you.ubc.ca/applying-ubc/applied/change-degree/)
-   [Appeals](https://you.ubc.ca/applying-ubc/applied/admission-appeals/)

## On this page:

-   [Canadian high school students](https://you.ubc.ca/applying-ubc/applied/submit-documents/#section-2)
-   [International high school students](https://you.ubc.ca/applying-ubc/applied/submit-documents/#section-3)
-   [Canadian university or college transfer students](https://you.ubc.ca/applying-ubc/applied/submit-documents/#section-4)
-   [International university or college transfer students](https://you.ubc.ca/applying-ubc/applied/submit-documents/#section-5)
-   [Advanced Placement students](https://you.ubc.ca/applying-ubc/applied/submit-documents/#section-6)
-   [International Baccalaureate students](https://you.ubc.ca/applying-ubc/applied/submit-documents/#section-7)
-   [Where to submit your documents](https://you.ubc.ca/applying-ubc/applied/submit-documents/#section-8)
-   [Wondering if UBC has received your documents?](https://you.ubc.ca/applying-ubc/applied/submit-documents/#section-9)
-   [Irreplaceable documents](https://you.ubc.ca/applying-ubc/applied/submit-documents/#section-10)

Look for an email from UBC with the subject line “Your UBC Application – Next Steps” that outlines which documents you are required to submit, how you can submit them, and when you’re required to submit them\. Once you have applied, you can check for these instructions in the [Applicant Service Centre](https://myapplication.ubc.ca/)\. Please do not submit documents prior to completing your UBC application\.

If your deadline falls on a Saturday, Sunday, or Canadian statutory holiday, your documents will be due the next business day\. Documents received after your deadline will be accepted as long as your school has requested them before that date\. If you applied to a program that closed after January 15, your deadline might be later than those listed below\. Please check your “Your UBC Application – Next Steps” email for details\.

## Canadian high school students

#### British Columbia and Yukon

If you applied directly from high school, you’ll need to authorize UBC to receive your grades from the BC Ministry of Education\. To do so, you must [create a BCeID account](https://www.bceid.ca/), and then follow the instructions at the [student transcripts website](https://www2.gov.bc.ca/gov/content/education-training/k-12/support/transcripts-and-certificates)\.

When you order your transcript, select the option to “send my transcript now and allow this post\-secondary institution to request transcript updates\.” Choose the default date \(one year from the date of your order\) so that UBC receives your grades throughout the year\.

Do not send a paper copy of your transcript or report card\.

- **Row 1**

  - **Cell 1:**
  
    November to July
  
  - **Cell 2:**
  
    UBC will request and receive your grades and courses in progress directly from the BC Ministry of Education, including distributed learning course information submitted to the Ministry\.
    
    Please do not send paper copies of transcripts or report cards\.

- **Row 2**

  - **Cell 1:**
  
    February 15
  
  - **Cell 2:**
  
    Deadline to submit documents showing you meet the [English Language Admission Standard \(ELAS\)](https://you.ubc.ca/applying-ubc/requirements/english-language-competency/), or an [ELAS waiver request](https://you.ubc.ca/applying-ubc/requirements/english-language-competency#section-5) and supporting documentation\.

- **Row 3**

  - **Cell 1:**
  
    March 15
  
  - **Cell 2:**
  
    Deadline for UBC to receive your electronic grades from the BC Ministry of Education for your UBC academic assessment\.

- **Row 4**

  - **Cell 1:**
  
    June 30
  
  - **Cell 2:**
  
    Deadline to complete all coursework to meet UBC’s admissions requirements, including all distributed learning courses\.

- **Row 5**

  - **Cell 1:**
  
    July 31
  
  - **Cell 2:**
  
    UBC will receive your final grades from the BC Ministry of Education, including your final grades for all distributed learning courses\. Please ensure your distributed learning provider submits your final grades to the Ministry of Education in time for UBC to access these on July 31\.

#### Ontario

If you applied directly from high school, UBC will receive your grades electronically as long as you provided your Ontario Universities’ Application Centre \(OUAC\) reference number when you [completed the online application](https://you.ubc.ca/applying-ubc/how-to-apply/application/#section-4) to UBC\.

| February 15 | Deadline to submit documents showing you meet the [English Language Admission Standard \(ELAS\)](https://you.ubc.ca/applying-ubc/requirements/english-language-competency/), or an [ELAS waiver request](https://you.ubc.ca/applying-ubc/requirements/english-language-competency#section-5) and supporting documentation\. |

| June 30 | Deadline to complete all coursework to meet UBC’s admissions requirements, including all distributed learning courses\. |

#### Other Canadian provinces and territories

If you applied directly from high school, you’ll receive an email with instructions on how to upload copies of your transcript of grades and/or report card to the [Applicant Service Centre](https://myapplication.ubc.ca/)\. Your documents must be in PDF, TIFF, or JPG format, and must not exceed 2 MB\.

If you have completed two years of CEGEP, please refer to the document submission instructions for [post\-secondary institutions in Canada](https://you.ubc.ca/applying-ubc/requirements/university-college-transfer/)\.

| June 30 | Deadline to complete all coursework to meet UBC’s admissions requirements, including all distributed learning courses\. |
| July 31 | Deadline to submit your final transcripts \(electronic copies preferred\)\. |

#### Students who graduated from a Canadian high school before applying to UBC

If you applied to UBC after you graduated from a high school in Canada, you will receive instructions on how to submit your government\-issued high school transcript electronically or via the [Applicant Service Centre](https://myapplication.ubc.ca/)\.

    February 15

    Deadline to submit documents showing you meet the [English Language Admission Standard \(ELAS\)](https://you.ubc.ca/applying-ubc/requirements/english-language-competency/), or send an [ELAS waiver request](https://you.ubc.ca/applying-ubc/requirements/english-language-competency#section-5) and supporting documentation\.

- **Row 2**

  - **Cell 1:**
  
    March 15
  
  - **Cell 2 (colspan 2):**
  
    Deadline to submit your final grades\. All courses required for admission to UBC, including distributed learning courses, must be completed and appear with a final grade on an official Ministry of Education transcript by this date\. Upgraders are encouraged to submit confirmation of completed courses as soon as possible\.

## International high school students

You’ll receive an email with instructions on how to upload your transcripts and documents\. Please check the [Applicant Service Centre](https://myapplication.ubc.ca/) to find out what documents are required to be submitted\.

UBC encourages the submission of transcripts and documents electronically wherever possible\. If this option is available to you, talk to your school counsellor about sending UBC your documents through a third\-party provider\.

If you attended or are currently attending a Canadian high school outside of Canada, please refer to the document submission instructions for [Canadian high school students](https://you.ubc.ca/applying-ubc/requirements/canadian-high-schools/)\.

#### American curricula

  - **Cell 1:**
  
    February 15
  
  - **Cell 2:**
  
    Deadline to submit documents showing you meet the [English Language Admission Standard \(ELAS\)](https://you.ubc.ca/applying-ubc/requirements/english-language-competency/), or an [ELAS waiver request](https://you.ubc.ca/applying-ubc/requirements/english-language-competency#section-5) and supporting documentation\.

- **Row 2**

  - **Cell 1:**
  
    March 15
  
  - **Cell 2:**
  
    Deadline to submit transcripts which show courses in progress if you are currently attending high school\.

    Deadline to submit documents showing you meet the SAT/ACT requirement\. The submission of standardized test scores is optional\. Applicants who have a SAT or ACT test score and would like them to be considered as part of the UBC admissions process are welcome to submit their test score\. Applicants will not be at a disadvantage if they cannot or choose not to submit a test score\.

#### British\-patterned education

## Canadian university or college transfer students

Please check the [Applicant Service Centre](https://myapplication.ubc.ca/) for details on what documents you need to submit to UBC and how to submit them\.

UBC will ask for your transcript in one of the following ways:

-   We may ask that you request for your electronic transcript to be sent directly to UBC from your participating BC institution\(s\): Capilano University, Douglas College, Kwantlen Polytechnic University, Langara College, and University of the Fraser Valley\.

## Where to submit your documents

Where you submit your documents depends on whether you are asking to submit an unofficial document or an official document\. An official document is one sent directly from your school or a designated third\-party verification service\. An unofficial document comes directly from a student\.

Refer to the [Applicant Service Centre](https://myapplication.ubc.ca/) regularly to check which types of documents you need to submit\.

**If you are asked to submit an unofficial document you can:**

-   upload it into the Applicant Service Centre
-   send it by [email](mailto:final.grades@ubc.ca) to UBC

**If you are asked to submit an official document you can ask your school to:**

-   send it by [email](mailto:final.grades@ubc.ca)
-   use an approved third\-party delivery platform such as Clearinghouse, MyCreds, Scoir, or Parchment\. \(Please ensure that you have your documents directed to Undergraduate Admissions\)\.
-   send it by mail\. Documents for undergraduate applications to the Okanagan and Vancouver campuses may be sent to:

The University of British Columbia  
Undergraduate Admissions  
2016 – 1874 East Mall  
Vancouver, BC, Canada V6T 1Z1

Note that official documents need to be sent directly by your school to UBC \(electronically or in an official envelope\)\. Students cannot submit an official document\.

UBC will only review requested documents\. If you send documents that were not requested, it will delay our evaluation of your application\.

## Wondering if UBC has received your documents?

It will take 4 to 6 weeks for us to process your documents and indicate that we have received them in the [Applicant Service Centre](https://myapplication.ubc.ca/)\. Once you have submitted your documents, know we will honour the date it was submitted\. Thank you for your patience\!

**UBC encourages the submission of transcripts and documents electronically wherever possible\.**

## Irreplaceable documents

Documents submitted in support of an application become the property of UBC and will not be returned unless they are irreplaceable \(e\.g\. graduation certificates\)\. If you are submitting an irreplaceable document, please [contact us](https://you.ubc.ca/contact-us/) to make arrangements for delivery to UBC, and complete and submit the form below with your documents so we can return them once UBC’s evaluation of your application is complete\.

If you complete university\-level courses while in high school, you may be able to take fewer courses to complete your degree\. Find out which Advanced Placement, British\-patterned education, and International Baccalaureate courses are eligible for first\-year credit at UBC\.

Before appealing an admission decision from UBC, make sure you understand what makes an application competitive, the circumstances under which you can submit an appeal, and the documentation you’ll need to provide\. Whether you choose to appeal or not, you always have the option of studying at another post\-secondary institution and re\-applying to UBC in the future\.

-   [Appealing an admission decision](https://you.ubc.ca/applying-ubc/applied/admission-appeals/#section-2)
-   [Supporting documentation for an appeal](https://you.ubc.ca/applying-ubc/applied/admission-appeals/#section-3)
-   [What makes an appeal successful](https://you.ubc.ca/applying-ubc/applied/admission-appeals/#section-4)
-   [Re\-applying to UBC in the future](https://you.ubc.ca/applying-ubc/applied/admission-appeals/#section-5)

## What makes an application competitive

If you did not receive an offer of admission to UBC, you may be wondering why\. In most cases, there is no single reason\. Usually, some combination of the following factors would have made your application more competitive:

-   A higher overall average
-   A higher grade in a particular course
-   A higher Personal Profile score
-   Fewer applicants to the degree you applied for

## Appealing an admission decision

UBC will consider an admission appeal for one of two reasons:

-   We made an error in the admission process \(e\.g\., a miscalculation of your grades\)\.
-   A mitigating circumstance affected your academic performance \(e\.g\., a personal hardship, personal illness, family member illness or death\)\.

The following reasons are not acceptable for an admission appeal:

-   You think UBC should take another look at your application for admission\.
-   Someone with similar grades received an offer of admission\.
-   You really want to attend UBC\.
-   You were given offers of admission to other universities, so you feel you should have received an offer of admission to UBC too\.
-   You were so close to getting an offer of admission\.

For details on how to submit an appeal, please see the [Okanagan Academic Calendar](http://www.calendar.ubc.ca/okanagan/index.cfm?tree=2,16,0,0) or the [Vancouver Academic Calendar](http://www.calendar.ubc.ca/vancouver/index.cfm?tree=2,16,0,0)\.

## Supporting documentation for an appeal

If you are submitting an appeal due to mitigating circumstances, you must provide supporting documentation that proves your claims and helps UBC reviewers understand the grounds for your appeal\.

For example: If your appeal is due to personal illness, you must provide medical documentation, transcripts, letters of support, and/or email correspondence that clearly outline:

-   The start and end dates of your illness
-   How the illness affected your academic performance
-   What treatments you received for the illness
-   Whether the illness is resolved and will no longer affect your academic performance

## What makes an appeal successful

Every application to UBC is evaluated carefully several times\. For this reason, admission decisions are rarely overturned\. In recent years, the average success rate for submitted appeals has been around 8%\.

Your appeal will **not be successful** if you fail to:

-   Outline an acceptable rationale to support your appeal
-   Provide evidence and supporting documentation
-   Establish a clear link between the mitigating circumstances and your academic performance
-   Show that the mitigating circumstance has been resolved and will no longer affect your academic performance

## Re\-applying to UBC in the future

If you wish to re\-apply to UBC after studying at another post\-secondary institution, review our requirements for [university or college transfer students](https://you.ubc.ca/applying-ubc/requirements/university-college-transfer/) and [contact us](https://you.ubc.ca/contact-us/) to speak to a UBC representative about your application\.

### More on After you’ve applied:

-   [Admissions decisions](https://you.ubc.ca/applying-ubc/applied/admissions-decisions/)
-   [Submit your documents](https://you.ubc.ca/applying-ubc/applied/submit-documents/)
-   [First\-year credit](https://you.ubc.ca/applying-ubc/applied/first-year-credit/)
-   [First\-year study options](https://you.ubc.ca/applying-ubc/applied/first-year-study-options/)
-   [How to change the degree you applied to](https://you.ubc.ca/applying-ubc/applied/change-degree/)
-   [Appeals](https://you.ubc.ca/applying-ubc/applied/admission-appeals/)

title: Dates and deadlines
content_markdown:
Whether you’re thinking about applying, you’ve submitted your application, or you’ve received an offer of admission to UBC, there are important deadlines to keep in mind\. Find out which dates you need to watch out for in this phase of your journey\.

### More on Applying to UBC:

-   [Admission requirements](https://you.ubc.ca/applying-ubc/requirements/)
-   [Indigenous admissions](https://you.ubc.ca/applying-ubc/indigenous-admissions/)
-   [How to apply](https://you.ubc.ca/applying-ubc/how-to-apply/)
-   [After you've applied](https://you.ubc.ca/applying-ubc/applied/)
-   [After you’ve been admitted](https://you.ubc.ca/applying-ubc/admitted/)
-   [What we look for](https://you.ubc.ca/applying-ubc/application-evaluation/)
-   [Dates and deadlines](https://you.ubc.ca/applying-ubc/dates-deadlines/)

## On this page:

-   [You’re preparing to apply to UBC](https://you.ubc.ca/applying-ubc/dates-deadlines/#section-1)
-   [You’ve applied to UBC](https://you.ubc.ca/applying-ubc/dates-deadlines/#section-2)
-   [You’ve been admitted to UBC](https://you.ubc.ca/applying-ubc/dates-deadlines/#section-3)

## You’re preparing to apply to UBC

- **Row 1**

  - **Cell 1:**
  
    ##### Early October 2026
  
  - **Cell 2:**
  
    ##### Application opens
    
    -   Online application opens for Winter Session \(September 2027 to April 2028\) and Summer Session \(May to August 2027\)\. [Apply here\!](https://myapplication.ubc.ca/apply)

- **Row 2**

  - **Cell 1:**
  
    ##### November 15, 2026
    
    \(11:59 p\.m\. PST\)
  
  - **Cell 2:**
  
    ##### Scholarships and awards
    
    -   International applicants: Deadline to [apply to UBC](https://myapplication.ubc.ca/apply) and submit an award application if you’re an international student and you wish to be considered for the [UBC International Scholars Program awards](https://you.ubc.ca/financial-planning/scholarships-awards-international-students/international-scholars "https://you.ubc.ca/financial-planning/scholarships-awards-international-students/international-scholars?openModal=2")\.

- **Row 3**

  - **Cell 1:**
  
    ##### December 1, 2026
    
    \(11:59 p\.m\. PST\)
  
  - **Cell 2:**
  
    ##### Scholarships and awards
    
    -   Canadian citizens and permanent residents: Deadline to [apply to UBC](https://myapplication.ubc.ca/apply) if you wish to be considered for the [Presidential Scholars Awards](https://you.ubc.ca/financial-planning/scholarships-awards-canadian-students/presidential-scholars/), [UBC Centennial Scholars Entrance Awards](https://you.ubc.ca/financial-planning/scholarships-awards-canadian-students/entrance-award/), or the [Beyond Tomorrow Scholars Award\.](https://you.ubc.ca/financial-planning/scholarships-awards-canadian-students/beyond-tomorrow/)

- **Row 4**

  - **Cell 1:**
  
    ##### January 15, 2027
    
    \(11:59 p\.m\. PST\)
  
  - **Cell 2:**
  
    ##### Applications due
    
    -   Deadline to apply for Winter Session \(September 2027 to April 2028\)\.
    -   Deadline to apply for Summer Session \(May to August 2027\), unless you’re a [visiting, unclassified, or Access Studies student](https://you.ubc.ca/applying-ubc/#section-5)\.

## You’ve applied to UBC

- **Row 1**

  - **Cell 1:**
  
    ##### November 2026 through to June 2027
  
  - **Cell 2:**
  
    ##### Admissions decisions
    
    -   Admissions decisions are made for high school applicants on a continuous basis\.

- **Row 2**

  - **Cell 1:**
  
    ##### January through to July 2027
  
  - **Cell 2:**
  
    ##### Admissions decisions
    
    -   Canadian post\-secondary applicants: Admissions decisions are made\.

- **Row 3**

  - **Cell 1:**
  
    ##### January 31, 2027
  
  - **Cell 2:**
  
    ##### International Scholars Program applicants
    
    -   Meet [UBC’s English Language Admission Standard for direct\-entry](https://you.ubc.ca/applying-ubc/requirements/english-language-competency/), or the [English language requirement for UBC Vantage College](https://vantagecollege.ubc.ca/admission-requirements) if you have applied to a Vantage One program\.
    
    -   [Submit any documents](https://you.ubc.ca/applying-ubc/applied/submit-documents/) required for your admission to UBC\. Please submit by this deadline, not the date indicated in your “next steps” email\.

- **Row 4**

  - **Cell 1:**
  
    ##### February 15, 2027
  
  - **Cell 2:**
  
    ##### Interim transcripts
    
    -   Canadian post\-secondary applicants currently attending another institution: Deadline to [submit your official interim transcript](https://you.ubc.ca/applying-ubc/applied/submit-documents/#section-4)\. Interim transcripts are those that include final grades for courses completed to December, and that list any courses in\-progress from January – April\.

- **Row 5**

  - **Cell 1:**
  
    ##### February 15, 2027
  
  - **Cell 2:**
  
    ##### ELAS
    
    -   Deadline to submit documents showing you meet the [English Language Admission Standard](https://you.ubc.ca/applying-ubc/requirements/english-language-competency/) \(ELAS\)\.

- **Row 6**

  - **Cell 1:**
  
    ##### March through to April 2027
  
  - **Cell 2:**
  
    ##### Scholarship announcements
    
    -   [Presidential Scholars Award](https://you.ubc.ca/financial-planning/scholarships-awards-canadian-students/presidential-scholars/)
    -   [Centennial Scholars Entrance Award](https://you.ubc.ca/financial-planning/scholarships-awards-canadian-students/entrance-award/)
    -   [Beyond Tomorrow Scholars Award](https://you.ubc.ca/financial-planning/scholarships-awards-canadian-students/beyond-tomorrow/)
    -   [International Major Entrance Scholarships](https://you.ubc.ca/financial-planning/scholarships-awards-international-students)
    -   [Outstanding International Student Award](https://you.ubc.ca/financial-planning/scholarships-awards-international-students)

- **Row 7**

  - **Cell 1:**
  
    ##### March 1 to March 15, 2027
  
  - **Cell 2:**
  
    ##### Grade submissions
    
    -   Canadian high school applicants outside of BC and Ontario: Upload your Spring transcript of grades including grades for distributed learning courses that are 50% complete to the [Applicant Service Centre](https://myapplication.ubc.ca/) for your UBC academic assessment\.

- **Row 8**

  - **Cell 1:**
  
    ##### March 15, 2027
  
  - **Cell 2:**
  
    ##### Grade submissions
    
    -   Students who graduated from a Canadian high school before applying to UBC: Deadline to submit your final grades\. All courses required for admission to UBC, including distributed learning courses, must be completed and appear with a final grade on an official Ministry of Education transcript by this date\. Upgraders are encouraged to submit confirmation of completed courses as soon as possible\.

- **Row 9**

  - **Cell 1:**
  
    ##### March 15, 2027
  
  - **Cell 2:**
  
    ##### Out\-of\-country documents
    
    -   Post\-secondary applicants from the United States: Deadline to [submit required documents](https://you.ubc.ca/applying-ubc/applied/submit-documents/#section-5) to UBC\.
    -   High school applicants from outside Canada: Deadline to [submit required documents](https://you.ubc.ca/applying-ubc/applied/submit-documents/#section-3) to UBC\.

- **Row 10**

  - **Cell 1:**
  
    ##### April 2027
  
  - **Cell 2:**
  
    ##### Scholarship announcements
    
    -   [International Scholars Program award](https://you.ubc.ca/financial-planning/scholarships-awards-international-students/international-scholars)

- **Row 11**

  - **Cell 1:**
  
    ##### May 31, 2027
  
  - **Cell 2:**
  
    ##### International documents
    
    -   Out\-of\-country post\-secondary applicants \(except US applicants\): Deadline to submit all required documents\.

- **Row 12**

  - **Cell 1:**
  
    ##### June 30, 2027
  
  - **Cell 2:**
  
    ##### Course completion
    
    -   Canadian high school applicants: Deadline to complete all high school courses, including distance and distributed\-learning courses to meet the conditions of your offer of admission\.

- **Row 13**

  - **Cell 1:**
  
    ##### September 15, 2027
  
  - **Cell 2:**
  
    ##### Bursary applications
    
    -   Canadian citizens and permanent residents: Deadline to submit general bursary applications\.

## You’ve been admitted to UBC

- **Row 1**

  - **Cell 1:**
  
    ##### May 1, 2027 or June 1, 2027
  
  - **Cell 2:**
  
    ##### Accept your offer\!
    
    -   Deadline for most students to accept UBC’s offer of admission and pay the acceptance deposit\. Please refer to your letter of admission or the [Applicant Service Centre](https://myapplication.ubc.ca/) to find your assigned offer deadline date\.

- **Row 2**

  - **Cell 1:**
  
    ##### As soon as you accept your offer of admission
  
  - **Cell 2:**
  
    ##### Study permits
    
    -   International applicants: Getting a study permit can take several months, so be sure to [apply for a study permit](https://you.ubc.ca/applying-ubc/admitted/study-permit/) as soon as you accept your offer of admission\.

- **Row 3**

  - **Cell 1:**
  
    ##### May 1, 2027
  
  - **Cell 2:**
  
    ##### Housing applications
    
    -   Application deadline for first\-year housing guarantee \(see [Vancouver housing](https://vancouver.housing.ubc.ca/applications/how-we-assign-rooms/first-year-guarantee/) or [Okanagan housing\)](https://okanagan.housing.ubc.ca/applications/how-we-assign-rooms/who-gets-priority/)\. If you’re considering a degree on both campuses, you must complete a separate residence application for each campus\.

- **Row 4**

  - **Cell 1:**
  
    ##### May 15, 2027
  
  - **Cell 2:**
  
    ##### Final transcripts
    
    -   Canadian post\-secondary applicants: Submit your final transcripts electronically or by mail to UBC’s Undergraduate Admissions Office\. \(Final transcripts are required to finalize conditional offers of admission\. Please review your application status in the [Applicant Service Centre](https://myapplication.ubc.ca/) for more information\.\)

- **Row 5**

  - **Cell 1:**
  
    ##### Early June 2027
  
  - **Cell 2:**
  
    ##### Housing offers
    
    -   If you’ve qualified for the first\-year guarantee \(see [Vancouver housing](https://vancouver.housing.ubc.ca/applications/how-we-assign-rooms/first-year-guarantee/) or [Okanagan housing\)](https://okanagan.housing.ubc.ca/applications/how-we-assign-rooms/who-gets-priority/) you’ll receive a housing offer\.

- **Row 6**

  - **Cell 1:**
  
    ##### Late June 2027
  
  - **Cell 2:**
  
    ##### Course registration
    
    -   [Course registration](https://you.ubc.ca/applying-ubc/admitted/register/) opens for first\-year students\.

- **Row 7**

  - **Cell 1:**
  
    ##### June 30, 2027
  
  - **Cell 2:**
  
    ##### Final transcripts
    
    -   US applicants: Deadline to submit final transcripts to UBC to confirm your offer of admission\.
    
    ##### Loan applications
    
    -   US applicants: Recommended deadline to submit UBC’s [US Loan Request form](https://students.ubc.ca/enrolment/finances/student-loans/funding-us) to ensure loan funding for September\.

- **Row 8**

  - **Cell 1:**
  
    ##### Late June 2027
  
  - **Cell 2:**
  
    ##### Jump Start Vancouver orientation
    
    -   Deadline to register for [Jump Start orientation](https://you.ubc.ca/jump-start-vancouver/) on the Vancouver campus\.

- **Row 9**

  - **Cell 1:**
  
    ##### July 1, 2027
  
  - **Cell 2:**
  
    ##### Deferred admission
    
    -   Deadline to apply for [deferred admission](https://you.ubc.ca/applying-ubc/admitted/deferring-admission/) for the Vancouver campus\.

- **Row 10**

  - **Cell 1:**
  
    ##### July 25, 2027
  
  - **Cell 2:**
  
    ##### Loan applications
    
    -   Canadian citizens and permanent residents: Recommended deadline to apply for Canadian and provincial loans to ensure funds for September and to qualify for the [UBC bursary program](https://you.ubc.ca/financial-planning/loans-bursaries/bursaries/)\.
    
    ##### Out\-of\-province and out\-of\-country high school transcripts
    
    -   Out\-of\-province applicants: Deadline to have your final official transcript mailed to UBC to confirm your offer of admission\.
    -   Out\-of\-country applicants \(except US and A\-Level applicants\): Deadline to submit your final transcript to confirm your offer of admission\. Please check your letter of admission for curriculum\-specific deadlines\.

- **Row 11**

  - **Cell 1:**
  
    ##### August 1, 2027
  
  - **Cell 2:**
  
    ##### Jump Start Okanagan orientation
    
    -   Deadline to register for [Jump Start orientation](https://students.ok.ubc.ca/new-to-ubc/orientations/jump-start/) on the Okanagan campus\.

- **Row 12**

  - **Cell 1:**
  
    ##### Early August, 2027
  
  - **Cell 2:**
  
    ##### Early arrival to residence
    
    -   Deadline to apply for early arrival to residence\. \(If you register for Jump Start, you’ll automatically qualify to move in early\.\)

- **Row 13**

  - **Cell 1:**
  
    ##### August 15, 2027
  
  - **Cell 2:**
  
    ##### Deferred admission
    
    -   Deadline to apply for [deferred admission](https://you.ubc.ca/applying-ubc/admitted/deferring-admission/) for the Okanagan campus\.

- **Row 14**

  - **Cell 1:**
  
    ##### August 20, 2027
  
  - **Cell 2:**
  
    ##### A\-Level results
    
    -   Applicants from the British\-patterned system: Deadline to submit final A\-Level results to UBC to confirm your offer of admission\.

- **Row 15**

  - **Cell 1:**
  
    ##### Early September 2027
  
  - **Cell 2:**
  
    ##### Jump Start
    
    -   Jump Start Okanagan for all new\-to\-UBC students\.
    -   Jump Start Vancouver orientation for all first\-year students coming to UBC from high school\.

- **Row 16**

  - **Cell 1:**
  
    ##### Early September, 2027
  
  - **Cell 2:**
  
    ##### Residence move\-in day
    
    -   Move\-in day\.

- **Row 17**

  - **Cell 1:**
  
    ##### Early September, 2027
  
  - **Cell 2:**
  
    ##### First day of classes
    
    -   First day of classes\. [Imagine UBC orientation](https://students.ubc.ca/new-to-ubc/orientations/imagine-ubc) on the Vancouver campus\.

- **Row 18**

  - **Cell 1:**
  
    ##### Early September, 2027
  
  - **Cell 2:**
  
    ##### Tuition payment
    
    -   Deadline to pay your first instalment of Winter Session tuition\.

### More on Applying to UBC:

-   [Admission requirements](https://you.ubc.ca/applying-ubc/requirements/)
-   [Indigenous admissions](https://you.ubc.ca/applying-ubc/indigenous-admissions/)

title: Former youth in care
content_markdown:
[Former youth in care](https://you.ubc.ca/wp-content/uploads/2019/10/IMG_5985.jpg)

UBC is committed to supporting the academic and personal achievements of former and current youth in care\. Both the Okanagan and Vancouver campuses have a number of programs and services in place to help applicants reach their potential\.

## Watch: Former Youth in Care Student Experience at UBC

[Embedded content: Former Youth in Care Student Experience at UBC](https://www.youtube.com/embed/T1pjsiOY7tU?feature=oembed)

[Image](https://you.ubc.ca/wp-content/uploads/2019/10/UBCFYIC_Verukah-62-768x512.jpg)

## Youth In Care Admissions Policy

UBC recognizes that, as a child in care, you may have faced challenges that have affected your education\. If you have satisfied the [general admission](https://you.ubc.ca/applying-ubc/requirements/) and [degree\-specific](https://you.ubc.ca/programs/) requirements, but have not met your degree’s competitive average, we are still able to consider you for admission\. UBC will assess your history, cultural knowledge, educational goals, and other achievements to determine your admissibility\.

[Learn more about the policy](https://vancouver.calendar.ubc.ca/admissions/british-columbia-youth-care-applicants)

    former or current youth in care enrolled at UBC
    
-   [Image](https://you.ubc.ca/wp-content/uploads/2025/04/message-dollar-solid.svg)

    students that have benefitted from tuition waivers
    
-   [graduation cap](https://you.ubc.ca/wp-content/uploads/2025/04/graduation-cap-solid.svg)

-   [graduation cap](https://you.ubc.ca/wp-content/uploads/2025/04/graduation-cap-solid.svg)

[Two students standing in Allard Hall](https://you.ubc.ca/wp-content/uploads/2024/10/how-to-apply-former-youth-in-care-768x512.jpg)

## How to apply

Be sure to self\-identify as a youth in or from care on your application\. UBC will provide you with important information on youth in care programs, financial awards, and student services specific to your situation\.

Submitting your application requires you to pay the application fee\. If you are prevented from submitting your application due to financial reasons, please contact [Joseph Stevens](mailto:joseph.stevens@ubc.ca) \(Vancouver campus\) or [Halyna Petryshyn](mailto:halyna.petryshyn@ubc.ca) \(Okanagan campus\) to discuss your options\.

[Learn more about how to apply](https://you.ubc.ca/applying-ubc/how-to-apply/)

### After you apply

There are a few more steps you’ll need to take after submitting your application\. Find out what’s next depending on where you are in the process:

-   [After you’ve applied](http://you.ubc.ca/applying-ubc/applied/)
-   [After you’ve been admitted](https://you.ubc.ca/applying-ubc/admitted/)

If you’ve self\-identified as a youth in or from care in your online application to UBC, your [admissions deposit will be automatically deferred](http://you.ubc.ca/applying-ubc/blog/tuition-awards-scholarships/registration-deposit-deferrals/)\. If you need to defer your housing deposit too, please contact [Joseph Stevens](mailto:joseph.stevens@ubc.ca) \(Vancouver campus\) or [Halyna Petryshyn](mailto:halyna.petryshyn@ubc.ca) \(Okanagan campus\)\.

## Awards for youth in and from care

### The Provincial Tuition Waiver Program

The BC Provincial Tuition Waiver Program covers the total cost of your tuition and mandatory fees for a range of programs if you were a youth in care in BC for a combined two years or aged out at 19\.

[Learn more about the program](https://studentaidbc.ca/explore/grants-scholarships/provincial-tuition-waiver-program)  

### The UBC Post Care Tuition Waiver Program

The UBC Post Care Tuition Waiver covers the cost of tuition and mandatory fees toward the completion of a first undergraduate degree for eligible students who have lived as a youth in care in BC\.

[Learn more about the program](https://you.ubc.ca/financial-planning/loans-bursaries/youth-in-care-funding/)  

### Youth in Care Awards

A number of scholarships and bursaries from private industry and not\-for\-profits are available to former youth in care\. Each has its own requirements and deadlines, and offer different funding amounts\. Some are available to youth with experience in care nationwide, not just in BC\.

[Learn more about the awards](https://agedout.com/topic-resources/find-scholarships-and-bursaries/)  

### Learning for Future Grant

Students receiving the Provincial Tuition Waiver for an eligible program can receive the Learning for Future Grant of $3,500 each program year\. The LFG contributes to educational costs not included in tuition and fees, like textbooks, technology, or home internet\.

[Learn more about the grant](https://studentaidbc.ca/explore/grants-scholarships/learning-future-grant)  

### Youth Futures Education Fund

The Youth Futures Education Fund provides funds to help with educational costs beyond tuition and fees for students who were previously in government care and are attending a post\-secondary institution on a tuition waiver\.

[Find out more about the fund](https://give.vancouverfoundation.ca/s/YouthFutures)  

### Strengthening Abilities and Journeys of Empowerment \(SAJE\)

The SAJE program can assist you if you have been in foster care or had a youth agreement between ages 12 and 19\. This program can provide a range of benefits towards housing, life skills and cultural connections, income stability, and health & wellness while you go back to school\.

[Learn more about the program](https://www2.gov.bc.ca/gov/content/family-social-supports/youth-and-family-services/youth-transitions)  

### UBC Entrance Awards

The UBC **Centennial Scholars Entrance Award** program assists students in transition from secondary school and other post\-secondary institutions to UBC\. This initiative supports academically qualified students who show an interest in joining the UBC community, but who would not otherwise be able to attend without significant financial aid\.

[Learn more about the award](https://you.ubc.ca/financial-planning/scholarships-awards-canadian-students/entrance-award/)

The **Beyond Tomorrow Scholars Program** for Black Canadian Scholars launched in September 2021 and creates a cross\-campus community of Scholars who already bring diverse academic, community involvement and leadership experience\. More than award recipients, Scholars participate in a range of programming and support designed for them to thrive at UBC\.

[Learn more about the award](https://beyondtomorrow.ubc.ca/)

## Finding a home

Verukah began her undergraduate studies at Langara College before arriving at UBC as a transfer student, where, as a youth from care, she didn’t have to pay tuition fees\. Now having graduated with two UBC degrees, she has excelled in her classes, built a strong network of lifelong friends, and is proud to call UBC home\.

-   [Verukah Poirier Former Youth in Care](https://you.ubc.ca/wp-content/uploads/2019/10/UBCFYIC_Verukah-77-768x512.jpg)
    
    “University can be so daunting to youth in care because it is a four\-year commitment\. However, there is no other place that I would have rather spent these last few years than here\. I can honestly say that I have found the family I always wanted at UBC\.”
    
    Verukah \| Cree and Métis \| Williams Lake, BC \| First Nations and Indigenous Studies, minor in Law and Society
    
    [Read more](https://you.ubc.ca/ubc-life/blog/finding-a-home/)
    

## Support at UBC

The Youth in Care Alumni Program \(YICAP\) student group has been created to support you during your transition to post\-secondary education\. It will provide you with access to a network of students and staff, stimulate connections across campus, and open opportunities within the UBC community\.

### Former Youth in Care Student Welcome Orientation \(Vancouver campus\)

The annual welcome orientation introduces all new students to the UBC Vancouver community\. You can meet your peers, alumni, and staff, and get acquainted with the campus, its people, and its resources\.

### Former Youth in Care events

UBC Vancouver hosts events and social gatherings for the diverse Former Youth in Care community every two weeks in our designated study lounge\. You can meet other students and discover new opportunities to get involved on campus or in the community\.

### Connect with an advisor

After you are admitted, you will be connected to an academic advisor to help navigate your studies\. There are designated academic advisors in several faculties on the Vancouver campus, including Arts and Social Work\.

You will also connect with an enrolment advisor, Joseph Stevens \(Vancouver campus\) or Halyna Petryshyn \(Okanagan campus\)\. Josepha and Haylna are the designated campus contacts for youth in and from care and work directly with students from application to graduation, helping you understand the services offered by the university and external sources\.

## Housing

Former youth in care have priority access to housing on both UBC campuses, and all direct\-entry first\-year students are guaranteed housing\. If you have a family and apply to the Vancouver campus, you’ll also have access to child\-friendly residences\. Be sure to review [important dates and deadlines to apply\.](https://vancouver.housing.ubc.ca/applications/important-dates/)

#### Okanagan Campus

[Housing on UBC’s Okanagan campus](http://okanagan.housing.ubc.ca/getting-started/prospective/)

#### Vancouver Campus

[Housing on UBC’s Vancouver campus](http://vancouver.housing.ubc.ca/getting-started/prospective/)

[Family housing on UBC’s Vancouver campus](http://vancouver.housing.ubc.ca/residences/acadia-park/)

[ubc okanagan, ubc residence, ubc virtual tour](https://you.ubc.ca/wp-content/uploads/2015/03/UBC-Okanagan-residence.jpg)

## Childcare

UBC gives students the option to study and live on campus with their families\. Both UBC Okanagan and UBC Vancouver have a number of childcare facilities for infants and children up to five years of age, as well as occasional out\-of\-school care\.

#### Okanagan Campus

[Childcare on UBC’s Okanagan campus](http://www.ubcodaycare.com/)

#### Vancouver Campus

[Childcare on UBC’s Vancouver campus](http://www.childcare.ubc.ca/)

If you have questions about applying to UBC as a former youth in care, please contact us\.

title: How UBC determines your tuition fees
content_markdown:
At UBC, your citizenship status usually determines whether you’ll pay domestic or international tuition fees, but there are a few exceptions\.

## Canadian students

As a Canadian student, you are eligible for domestic tuition fees at UBC if:

-   You are a Canadian citizen;
-   You hold multiple citizenships and one of them is Canadian;
-   You are a permanent resident of Canada;
-   You have refugee status in Canada; or
-   You are the dependent of a diplomat assigned to Canada\.

**Note:** You may be required to provide documents that verify your eligibility for domestic tuition fees\.

## International students

If you are not a Canadian citizen or permanent resident of Canada, you will be required to pay international tuition fees at UBC unless you are eligible for one of the following exceptions\.

#### You may be eligible for domestic tuition fees at UBC if:

-   You have an affiliation with an Indigenous nation of Canada \(First Nations, Métis, or Inuit\);
-   You identify as a member of an Indigenous nation that extends across the Canada\-US border \(American Indian or Alaska Native\);
-   You are in Canada with an employer\-specific, full\-time, long\-term work permit; or
-   You are the dependent or spouse of an individual who is in Canada with an employer\-specific, full\-time, long\-term work permit\.

**Note:** If you are eligible for the one of these exceptions, please provide supporting documentation to [Student Services](https://students.ok.ubc.ca/about/contact/) \(UBC Okanagan\) or your [Enrolment Services Advisor](https://students.ubc.ca/about-student-services/enrolment-services-advisors) \(UBC Vancouver\) before the tuition fee payment deadline\.

## Calculate your first\-year costs

Now that you know which tuition fees you’ll pay at UBC, use our [cost calculator](https://you.ubc.ca/financial-planning/cost/) to estimate the first\-year costs for your chosen campus and degree\.

title: First-year study options
content_markdown:
Transitioning from high school to university can seem daunting at first\. To make the move as easy as possible, UBC offers a selection of first\-year study options designed to help you build a community, take the stress out of registering for classes, and offer greater access to instructors\.

### More on After you’ve applied:

-   [Admissions decisions](https://you.ubc.ca/applying-ubc/applied/admissions-decisions/)
-   [Submit your documents](https://you.ubc.ca/applying-ubc/applied/submit-documents/)
-   [First\-year credit](https://you.ubc.ca/applying-ubc/applied/first-year-credit/)
-   [First\-year study options](https://you.ubc.ca/applying-ubc/applied/first-year-study-options/)
-   [How to change the degree you applied to](https://you.ubc.ca/applying-ubc/applied/change-degree/)
-   [Appeals](https://you.ubc.ca/applying-ubc/applied/admission-appeals/)

First\-year study options are available in a number of faculties, and each has its own requirements and curricula\. You can choose a first\-year study option in place of creating your own custom timetable\.

## Options for Arts students

After you’ve been accepted into the Bachelor of Arts degree at UBC Vancouver, you’ll have to decide which classes to take when registration opens in **June**\. If you choose to join a first\-year study option, you’ll enjoy a predesigned course schedule and you’ll take nearly all of your classes with the same people\.

There are two to choose from\. Both offer an integrated curriculum that covers many different disciplines, such as English, Philosophy, and Political Science\.

### Arts One

[Arts One](https://artsone.arts.ubc.ca/) is a single, integrated course led by five instructors who work together to create the assignments and a reading list based on the year’s theme\. You’ll read and discuss classical and contemporary texts and their influence on culture and society, including novels, philosophical and political works, films, drama, graphic memoirs, and more\.

-   Attend lectures led by one of your professors once a week\.
-   Participate in twice\-weekly seminar discussions \(20 students\) led by one instructor\.
-   Enjoy once\-weekly tutorials, where you and three classmates will read and evaluate each other’s essays\.

#### **Coordinated Arts Program**

In the [Coordinated Arts Program](https://cap.arts.ubc.ca/) \(CAP\), you’ll get to choose from one of [five streams](https://cap.arts.ubc.ca/our-streams/), each offering a different combination of courses from across the Faculty of Arts\. The stream topics for 2021/2022 were Globalization, Power and Society; Individual and Society; Law and Society; Politics, Philosophy, and Economics; and Media Studies, and allow students and faculty to discuss ideas from various perspectives\.

-   CAP courses are separate, but faculty work together to connect the concepts and issues you’ll study and to make sure your deadlines won’t overlap\.
-   CAP classes are smaller than if you choose to create your own custom timetable, ranging from 25 students in the writing course to around 100 to 125 students in a lecture\.

**How to register**

Registration for both Arts One and CAP is first\-come, first\-served\. Both programs simplify the process by offering easy\-to\-use forms on their websites, or you can register directly in Workday when first\-year registration opens in June\. Find out more about [registering for Arts One](https://artsone.arts.ubc.ca/program/registration/ "https://artsone.arts.ubc.ca/program/registration/") and [registering for CAP](https://cap.arts.ubc.ca/program/registration/ "https://cap.arts.ubc.ca/program/registration/") on their websites\.

**Looking for more information?** Read what it’s like to be an [Arts One student](https://www.arts.ubc.ca/news/choosing-arts-one/ "https://www.arts.ubc.ca/news/choosing-arts-one/") and a [Coordinated Arts Program student](https://www.arts.ubc.ca/news/choosing-the-coordinated-arts-program-cap/ "https://www.arts.ubc.ca/news/choosing-the-coordinated-arts-program-cap/") and why students chose each program\.

## Options for Science students

Science students at UBC Vancouver can choose between creating their own timetable, requesting a [Course\-Bundle Early Registration](https://science.ubc.ca/students/registration/bundles), or [Science One](https://scienceone.ubc.ca/) which offers courses integrating Biology, Chemistry, Physics, and Mathematics\. Science One provides small class sizes, dedicated study spaces, and lower student\-to\-instructor ratios\.

Science One will allow you to build a strong foundation in science, be part of a tight\-knit community with your classmates, and take some of the stress out of registering for classes\.

[medical laboratory science, ubc](https://you.ubc.ca/wp-content/uploads/2013/06/Medical-Laboratory-Science-768x511.jpg.webp)

### Course Bundle Early Registration

[Course Bundle Early Registration](https://science.ubc.ca/students/registration/bundles) is a registration option that allows first\-year science students to request to be registered into a bundle of first\-year courses before regular registration opens\. With Course Bundle Early Registration, you will be registered to take a number of first\-year science courses together with the same group of other Science students who have requested the same courses\.

By requesting a course bundle, you simplify your registration process, and your course bundle will make it easier for you to connect with new friends in multiple courses\.

#### **Science One**

[Science One](https://scienceone.ubc.ca/) will allow you to build a strong foundation in science, be part of a tight\-knit community with your classmates, and take some of the stress out of registering for classes\.

Science One can be challenging\. It has a competitive application process, an intense schedule, and teaches first\-year science at one of the highest levels at UBC to a tight\-knit group of students\.

-   You’ll be one of just 75 individuals, and will be supported by eight to nine instructors\.
-   All Science One teachers attend each other’s classes to dynamically shape your curriculum
-   Share your own work and study space with your instructors\.
-   Take part in weekly tutorials, learn from guest lecturers, and have extra instruction in science literacy and computer programming\.
-   Be mentored on two major research projects – the results of which can be published in undergraduate journals\.
-   Attend student conferences and enjoy two field trips\.

Science One is also a social experience\. You’ll help elect student representatives to sit in on the Science One student council and the Science Undergraduate Society \(SUS\), and take part in alumni\-led mentorship and social activities such as the Winter Formal and Pie Day events\.

##### How to apply

If you want to join Science One, you’ll need to [submit an application](https://scienceone.ubc.ca/apply) at the same time or shortly after you [apply to UBC](https://ssc.adm.ubc.ca/sscportal/apply.xhtml)’s Bachelor of Science degree, as registration opens on **November 1**\. Applications received after **April 30** may be considered, but not with the same priority as those received before that date\.

## Options for Forestry, Applied Biology, and Food, Nutrition, and Health students

If you have been accepted into the [Forestry](https://forestry.ubc.ca/) or [Land and Food Systems](https://www.landfood.ubc.ca/) faculties, you are eligible to apply for the [Land One](https://landone.ubc.ca/) first\-year study option\.

[Image](https://you.ubc.ca/wp-content/uploads/2013/08/770x350-Corn-and-sqaush-Mayan-Garden-768x349.jpg.webp)

### Land One

Land One includes a selection of core courses in Biology, Economics, Math, and English, as well as an integrative seminar\. You’ll take all of these key classes with the 50 to 60 students who are admitted to the program\.

Land One’s seminar course covers a range of issues related to land use, climate change, food security, and sustainability\.

-   Discuss and address how to solve these problems
-   Visit the UBC Farm to learn more about sustainable food systems, and count the Museum of Anthropology as one of your learning spaces
-   Participate in a two\-day field trip to UBC’s Malcolm Knapp Research Forest, where you’ll experience the coastal old\-growth rainforest first\-hand\.

#### How to apply

You will need to be accepted by your Forestry or Land and Food Systems degree program, and then [submit an online application](https://landone.ubc.ca/apply-now/) through Land One’s website\. Applications open in the spring, and the deadline is **May 31\.** Enrolment in Land One is limited by size, so apply early\!

## Options for English language instruction \(Vantage One\)

UBC’s [Vantage One programs](https://vantagecollege.ubc.ca/) are designed to allow international students who do not yet meet the [English language requirements](https://you.ubc.ca/applying-ubc/requirements/english-language-competency/) to enter directly into a UBC faculty\. Vantage One courses last 11 months, and add English language instruction to first\-year degree courses\. You can choose from [Arts](https://vantagecollege.ubc.ca/arts), [Engineering](https://vantagecollege.ubc.ca/engineering), or [Science](https://vantagecollege.ubc.ca/science), and you’ll be taught by award\-winning UBC faculty members\.

[vantage one, science, ubc](https://you.ubc.ca/wp-content/uploads/2016/12/Vantage-One-Science-768x432.jpg.webp)

### Arts, Science, or Engineering Vantage One

The Arts and Science Vantage One programs take place at UBC Vancouver, while Engineering involves studying at both [UBC Vancouver](https://you.ubc.ca/ubc-life/vancouver/) and [UBC Okanagan](https://you.ubc.ca/ubc-life/okanagan/)\. When you successfully complete your Vantage One program, you’ll progress into your second year at UBC, where you can study the following degree programs:

-   [Bachelor of Arts](https://you.ubc.ca/programs/#mode=by-topic&viewMode=grid&filters%5Bsearch%5D=Bachelor%20of%20Arts) \(at UBC Vancouver\)
-   [Bachelor of Science](https://you.ubc.ca/programs/#mode=by-topic&viewMode=grid&filters%5Bsearch%5D=Bachelor%20of%20Science) \(at UBC Vancouver\)
-   [Bachelor of Applied Science](https://you.ubc.ca/programs/#mode=by-topic&viewMode=grid&filters%5Bsearch%5D=Bachelor%20of%20Applied%20Science%20%28Engineering%29) \(at either UBC Okanagan or UBC Vancouver\)

Vantage One accepts students with a minimum score of 70 on the TOEFL and 5\.5 on the IELTS\. Certain sub\-scores apply for each test, so be sure to review the [full English language requirements](https://vantagecollege.ubc.ca/admission-requirements) on the Vantage College website\.

#### How to apply

[Applications open](https://vantagecollege.ubc.ca/how-apply) in **early September**, and the deadline is **January 15**\. If you wish to be considered for the [Vantage One Excellence Award](https://you.ubc.ca/financial-planning/scholarships-awards-international-students/international-scholars/), you must submit your application before **November 15**\.

Both of our campuses offer the best of both worlds – breathtaking British Columbia nature and challenging, engaging courses\. What you plan to study determines which campus you’ll call home\. Each campus has a lot to offer, including state\-of\-the\-art facilities, thriving city centres nearby, and activities like hiking and skiing practically at your doorstep\.

You did it\! First things first – accept your offer and pay your acceptance deposit before the date indicated in your letter of admission to save your spot\.

## Next steps for admitted students

From accepting your offer to building a budget, to choosing where you’ll live and registering for courses, learn what lies ahead\.

Step 1 [Accept your offer](https://you.ubc.ca/applying-ubc/admitted/your-offer/)

Step 7 [Plan your degree](https://you.ubc.ca/applying-ubc/admitted/degree-planning/)

Step 8 [Register for your courses](https://you.ubc.ca/applying-ubc/admitted/register/)

Step 9 [Get ready for UBC life](https://you.ubc.ca/applying-ubc/admitted/get-ready/)

## How to accept your offer

1

Log in to the Applicant Service Centre\. Confirm that your address is correct by clicking **Edit Profile** and selecting **Contact Summary***\.*

2

Next, click **Admissions**, then select **Accept or** **Decline Offer**\.

3

Select **Yes, I accept this offer**\.

4

Follow the steps to pay your deposit\. The fee is $500 for Canadian citizens and permanent residents and $3,000 for students on a study permit\. You must pay your deposit with a credit card\.

[Accept your offer](https://myapplication.ubc.ca/)

## Advisor Tip

-   [Image](https://you.ubc.ca/wp-content/uploads/2025/05/Claudia_Profile_300x300_acf_cropped.jpg.webp)
    
    “As an enrolment services advisor, I wear many hats\. I specialize in financial advising, but I can also answer questions about undergraduate admissions, fees, tuition, registration, financial support, exams, graduation, transcripts, and so much more\. If you have a question I can’t answer, I likely know the person or department who can\.”
    
    Claudia, UBC advisor
    

## Offer information

### Conditional offers

Your spot at UBC is subject to the conditions outlined in your letter of admission\. It’s important that you maintain your grades and submit your final documents to confirm your offer\. Any significant changes in your academic standing could lead to [your offer being reassessed](https://you.ubc.ca/applying-ubc/admitted/keep-offer/)\.

### If you applied to two degrees

If you’re still waiting to hear back about your first choice, check the [Applicant Service Centre](https://myapplication.ubc.ca/) regularly for status updates\. If you receive offers to both your first\- and second\-choice degrees, you can choose either one\.

### Deferring your offer

Under certain circumstances, UBC will consider deferring your offer of admission by one year \(or two years for mandatory military service\) if you’re joining UBC as a first\-year undergraduate\. For more information, review our [deferral eligibility requirements and deadlines](https://you.ubc.ca/applying-ubc/admitted/deferring-admission/)\.

## Get your questions answered

Have more questions? Your campus advisor is here to help\.

[Image](https://you.ubc.ca/wp-content/uploads/2019/12/29948790611_6b0abb2760_k-e1576264474150-768x332.jpg.webp)

### Your Enrolment Services Advisor at UBC Okanagan

As a student at UBC Okanagan, you’ll have access to Enrolment Services Advisors\. These advisors are there to help you decipher university policy, connect you with resources, and help you plan your finances\. Contact Enrolment Services to get help with all things related to your finances: student loans, tuition, & creating a spending plan\.

 [https://students\.ok\.ubc\.ca/courses\-money\-enrolment/advising/](https://students.ok.ubc.ca/courses-money-enrolment/advising/)

### Your Enrolment Services Advisor at UBC Vancouver

As a student at UBC Vancouver, you’ll be paired with an Enrolment Services Advisor shortly after you accept your offer\. Find your Enrolment Services Advisor in Workday by navigating to the **Student** menu, opening the **Academics** app, then clicking the **Support** tab\. Ask them for help with planning your finances, registering for courses, and finding resources online and on campus\.

 [https://students\.ubc\.ca/about\-student\-services/enrolment\-services\-advisors/](https://students.ubc.ca/about-student-services/enrolment-services-advisors/)

### Academic Advisors

Our campuses have Academic Advisors who can help with course planning, degree requirements, and transfer credits\.

Connect with an Academic Advisor on the [Okanagan campus](https://students.ok.ubc.ca/academic-success/advising-options/academic-advising/) or the [Vancouver campus\.](https://students.ubc.ca/enrolment/academic-learning-resources/academic-advising/)

International students need a valid study permit to attend UBC\. Getting a permit can take several months, so be sure to begin the process as soon as you can\.

## Next steps for admitted students

From accepting your offer to building a budget, to choosing where you’ll live and registering for courses, learn what lies ahead\.
