[University of British Columbia](https://you.ubc.ca/wp-content/uploads/2026/06/UBC-Webcover-2027.png)

## It is yours

UBC’s motto is *tuum est* – “it is yours”\. It is a place to challenge the ordinary, meet peers from around the world, and discover how to make a difference\. Through UBC’s vast network of clubs, leadership opportunities, undergraduate research, experiential learning and more, you’ll gain an unparalleled university experience that prepares you for your future\.

-   [pantheon icon](https://you.ubc.ca/wp-content/uploads/2025/04/building-columns-solid.svg)
    
    ### Top 45 university in the world
    
-   [globe icon](https://you.ubc.ca/wp-content/uploads/2025/04/globe-stand-solid.svg)
    
    ### \#2 most international university in North America
    
-   [Image](https://you.ubc.ca/wp-content/uploads/2025/03/microscope-solid.svg)
    
    ### Top 30 university globally by subject area
    

-   [pantheon icon](https://you.ubc.ca/wp-content/uploads/2025/04/building-columns-solid.svg)
    
    ### Top 45 university in the world
    
-   [globe icon](https://you.ubc.ca/wp-content/uploads/2025/04/globe-stand-solid.svg)
    
    ### \#2 most international university in North America
    
-   [Image](https://you.ubc.ca/wp-content/uploads/2025/03/microscope-solid.svg)
    
    ### Top 30 university globally by subject area
    

[three students smiling and waving mini blue flags at JumpStart event](https://you.ubc.ca/wp-content/uploads/2026/02/JumpStart-Vancouver-2026-768x512.jpg)

## Key dates

**November 15:** International Scholars Program Award deadline \(UBC application is due at the same time\)\.

**December 1:** Application deadline to be eligible for entrance scholarship awards for Canadians and permanent citizens\.

**January 15:** Application deadline for upcoming winter and summer sessions\. Winter session is from September to April\. Summer session is from May to August\.

**May–June:** Deadline to accept UBC’s offer of admission and pay the acceptance deposit\. Most students will need to accept by May 1\. Please check your offer of admission to confirm your deadline\.

[See key dates](http://you.ubc.ca/deadlines)

## Choose what to study

When you apply to UBC, you may select up to two choices \(first and second choice\)\. For each choice, you will choose a degree and a campus\. At UBC, a program is considered your area of academic focus\. Degrees are the designation you earn upon graduation\. Most bachelor’s degrees take approximately four years of full\-time study to complete\.

View our programs to see the many study options available, and customize your degree to fit your goals\.

[Visit our Programs section](https://you.ubc.ca/programs/)

-   Okanagan
    
    [data science, ubc](https://you.ubc.ca/wp-content/uploads/2016/11/Data-Science-768x505.jpg)
    
    ### Data Science
    
    Data Science is an in\-demand field that focuses on making decisions supported by data\. It’s grounded in statistics to formulate relevant questions and determine the answer based on data, and in computer science to manipulate and visualize data effici\.\.\.
    
    [Learn more](https://you.ubc.ca/programs/data-science/ "Learn more about Data Science")
    
-   Vancouver
    
    [Image](https://you.ubc.ca/wp-content/uploads/2019/09/food-nutrition-health-768x511.jpg)
    
    ### Food, Nutrition, and Health
    
    Explore the economic, ecological, social, and technological components of managed landscapes, agrifood systems, and communities comprising the land, food, nutrition, and health continuum\. In Food, Nutrition, and Health, you can customize your degree\.\.\.
    
    [Learn more](https://you.ubc.ca/programs/food-nutrition-and-health/ "Learn more about Food, Nutrition, and Health")
    
-   Okanagan
    
    [Image](https://you.ubc.ca/wp-content/uploads/2013/06/nursing-okanagan-sim-lab-768x432.jpg)
    
    ### Nursing
    
    Discover an essential understanding of people within the context of health and healing in today’s society while you prepare for a professional licensure as a registered nurse\. As a professional nurse, and a graduate of this program, you will be quali\.\.\.
    
    [Learn more](https://you.ubc.ca/programs/nursing-okanagan/ "Learn more about Nursing")
    
-   Vancouver
    
    [Image](https://you.ubc.ca/wp-content/uploads/2013/06/Forest-Operations-768x512.jpg)
    
    ### Forest Operations
    
    If you seek the challenge of applying technology and science to create environmentally and economically sound harvesting plans, then the Forest Operations program, a major in the Bachelor of Science in Nature Resources degree, may be for you\.
    
    [Learn more](https://you.ubc.ca/programs/forest-operations/ "Learn more about Forest Operations")
    
-   Vancouver
    
    [mechanical engineering, ubc](https://you.ubc.ca/wp-content/uploads/2013/06/Mechanical-Engineering-Vancouver-2-768x432.jpg)
    
    ### Mechanical Engineering
    
    Mechanical Engineering is a diverse field that applies physics and mathematics to analyze, design, and maintain mechanical systems\. Mechanical Engineers continuously innovate, then refine and simplify solutions to the problems we face in our everyday\.\.\.
    
    [Learn more](https://you.ubc.ca/programs/mechanical-engineering-vancouver/ "Learn more about Mechanical Engineering")
    
-   Okanagan
    
    [Zoology student with a leopard](https://you.ubc.ca/wp-content/uploads/2025/07/ubc-okanagan-zoology-768x348.jpg)
    
    ### Zoology
    
    Explore the animal kingdom as a biological scientist by studying behaviours, physiology, anatomy, and the entire animal organism\. You'll gain practical experience and skills in laboratory and fieldwork, computers, and communication\.
    
    [Learn more](https://you.ubc.ca/programs/zoology/ "Learn more about Zoology")
    
-   Vancouver
    
    [economics, ubc vancouver](https://you.ubc.ca/wp-content/uploads/2013/06/Economics-Vancouver-768x432.jpg)
    
    ### Economics
    
    Gain a deep understanding of the economy and examine the social, cross\-cultural, and ethical dimensions of economic decision\-making\. You’ll learn how to choose and apply appropriate quantitative methods to a range of economic issues, and effectively\.\.\.
    
    [Learn more](https://you.ubc.ca/programs/economics-vancouver/ "Learn more about Economics")
    
-   Okanagan
    
    [Indigenous woman in traditional dress stretching an animal skin\.](https://you.ubc.ca/wp-content/uploads/2013/06/indigenousstudies-okanagan-768x297.jpg)
    
    ### Indigenous Studies
    
    In the interdisciplinary Indigenous studies program, you'll learn about Indigenous perspectives and governance, the justice system, land claims, traditional ecological knowledge and the protection of heritage in the Okanagan, Canada, U\.S\., and world\.\.\.
    
    [Learn more](https://you.ubc.ca/programs/indigenous-studies/ "Learn more about Indigenous Studies")
    

[Embedded svg \(view source\)](https://you.ubc.ca/itsyours/)

## One UBC\. Two campus experiences\.

UBC has two distinct campuses, each offering unique academic programs, experiences and opportunities\. Visit our campus pages or book a tour to decide whether our Okanagan or Vancouver campus fits you best\.

[Okanagan campus](https://you.ubc.ca/okanagan) [Vancouver campus](https://you.ubc.ca/ubc-life/vancouver/)

## How to apply

Ready to join the UBC community?

As one of the world’s top 45 universities, UBC has competitive admission requirements and attracts elite students from around the globe\. Your journey to UBC begins with your online application\. We’re here to provide you with the information, deadlines, and tips to help you put your best foot forward\.

[two students looking at a computer](https://you.ubc.ca/wp-content/uploads/2026/09/042-hull-6X5A9786-768x512.jpg)

### Admission requirements

To be considered for admission to UBC, you must meet the general admission requirements, degree\-specific requirements, and English Language Admission Standard\. Use your high school curriculum, plus your chosen campus and degree, to find a complete list of your requirements\.

 [https://you\.ubc\.ca/applying\-ubc/requirements/](https://you.ubc.ca/applying-ubc/requirements/)

[Image](https://you.ubc.ca/wp-content/uploads/2021/06/49747722397_1217d9ac9b_k-768x949.jpg)

### English Language Admission Standard

English is the language of instruction at UBC\. To study here, you must be able to demonstrate a minimum level of English language competency\. There are nine different ways to meet UBCs English Language Admission Standard \(ELAS\)\.

 [https://you\.ubc\.ca/applying\-ubc/requirements/english\-language\-competency/](https://you.ubc.ca/applying-ubc/requirements/english-language-competency/)

[Image](https://you.ubc.ca/wp-content/uploads/2020/01/Student-Learning-Hub-Okanagan-768x400.jpg)

### How and when to apply

Applying to UBC is a straightforward four\-step process, but be sure to give yourself plenty of time\. Applications are due by January 15 \(or earlier if you wish to be considered for the University’s entrance scholarships and awards\)\.

 [https://you\.ubc\.ca/applying\-ubc/dates\-deadlines/](https://you.ubc.ca/applying-ubc/dates-deadlines/)

[international students, ubc](https://you.ubc.ca/wp-content/uploads/2019/04/international-students-ubc.jpg)

### How UBC makes decisions

UBC’s admission process is competitive and comparative\. No matter what degree you apply for, UBC will broadly evaluate your academic history\. Your Grade 11 \(junior\-level\) and Grade 12 \(senior\-level\) courses will be considered, with particular focus on subject categories related to your intended area of study\.

 [https://you\.ubc\.ca/applying\-ubc/applied/application\-evaluation/](https://you.ubc.ca/applying-ubc/applied/application-evaluation/)

## Academics outside the box

***84%** **of*** ***undergraduate students participate in enriched learning experiences by the time they graduate, earning practical experience employers value\.***

Venture off campus and out into the world\. Learn from professionals in your field through co\-operative education, contribute to community\-based projects with global significance, or experience other cultures on academic exchange\. Collaborate with your professors on your own undergraduate research, or take part in a number of hands\-on learning opportunities\.

Whatever path you choose, you’ll have the freedom to craft a university experience that’s enriching and uniquely yours\.

[Girl climbing mountain in Kelowna](https://you.ubc.ca/wp-content/uploads/2017/11/ugc10-768x768.png)

### Leadership and volunteering

***240\+ exchange, research, and study\-abroad partners worldwide\.*** Make the most of your time at UBC through volunteering, joining the student government or attending leadership conferences\. There are [many ways you can get involved](https://you.ubc.ca/ubc-life/getting-involved/leadership-volunteering/) during your time at UBC\.

[UBC student engaged in a work program](https://you.ubc.ca/wp-content/uploads/2013/06/student-work-program-768x480.jpg)

### Work programs

***3,500\+ on\-campus job placements annually\.*** Gain paid work experience through a part\-time UBC job while taking classes\. Learn from a mentor and expand your professional network with our [Work Study program](https://students.ok.ubc.ca/career-experience/hire-a-student/work-study/) on the Okanagan campus, or [Work Learn](http://students.ubc.ca/career/campus-experiences/work-learn) on the Vancouver campus\.

[Image](https://you.ubc.ca/wp-content/uploads/2017/01/co-op-placement-768x313.jpg)

### Co\-op learning

***8,000\+ co\-op placements each year\.*** UBC has the largest Co\-operative Education Program in Western Canada\. With co\-op, you can combine your studies with full\-time, paid work experience in a variety of fields\. Co\-op grads see **15% higher starting salaries** and graduate with experience that match employer demands\.

[Image](https://you.ubc.ca/wp-content/uploads/2017/03/programs-1-768x511.jpg)

### Undergraduate research

***$936 million in research funding\.*** Work alongside award\-winning faculty, boldly testing new theories and developing technologies that have the potential to change the world\. Both campuses offer you the chance to collaborate with your professors on research projects that excite you\.

## Find out if UBC is right for you\.

UBC hosts many events throughout the year, including campus tours, student experience events, and school visits so you can learn more about life at UBC\.

Join us for one of our events, and see if UBC if right for you\.

[Sign up for an info session or tour](https://account.you.ubc.ca/s/events)

## Your dream university experience

Be part of new communities, make lifelong friends, and learn new skills to make the most of your university experience\. With a wide array of [events, clubs](https://you.ubc.ca/ubc-life/getting-involved/), and [arts and culture](https://you.ubc.ca/ubc-life/arts-and-culture/) to explore, you can delve deeper into your passions, while discovering new interests\.

[Group of students at Jump Start Vancouver](https://you.ubc.ca/wp-content/uploads/2025/07/jumpstart-vancouver-studentgroup.jpeg)

### 500\+ clubs and course unions

Choose from hundreds of [student\-run clubs and course unions](https://you.ubc.ca/ubc-life/getting-involved/clubs/) including boxing, anime, and debate, or create your own\! Build lifelong friendships, or discover new skills with a new hobby\.

[Axel playing soccer, about to kick the ball](https://you.ubc.ca/wp-content/uploads/2024/11/axel-l-studentstory-768x512.jpg)

### Recreational or competitive sports

UBC has extensive recreational facilities including a new 101,000 sq ft recreation centre and Olympic\-sized pool\. It is also home to two major varsity athletic teams: Okanagan Heat and the Vancouver Thunderbirds\. [Learn more about UBC’s sports and recreation](https://you.ubc.ca/ubc-life/sports-recreation/)\.

[three students walking](https://you.ubc.ca/wp-content/uploads/2026/09/three-Indigenous-students-2-768x512.jpeg)

### Diverse community and spaces

With a community representing over 160 countries, our campus is truly a global community\. From diverse cultural spaces to year\-round events, there’s something for everyone\.

Are you an Indigenous student? See [information for Indigenous students](https://you.ubc.ca/indigenous?_gl=1*i90i2n*_gcl_aw*R0NMLjE3ODgyOTU1MTEuQ2p3S0NBanc3cmJFQmhCNUVpd0ExVjQ5blhZcHJBZFg2RjhwTVZ2NU5iVl9jV1RqWm1DVEh0dE1jc29lcFBGMGdLZzh0Z2I2SS0yNUpCb0N3VlVRQXZEX0J3RQ..*_gcl_au*NjQ3ODQ1NTIyLjE3ODc4NzA2ODIuLS4tLjE3ODgzMDAzNzkuNTc0MDU5NTc5LjE3ODgzMDAzNzkuMTc4ODMwMDM3OQ..*_ga*Mzk0OTE2MzQwLjE3NTg4NjAwNjU.*_ga_4HEE092K89*czE3ODg1MzQwNTIkbzckZzAkdDE3ODg1MzQwNTIkajYwJGwwJGgw)\.

[Student sitting with recruiter at a table](https://you.ubc.ca/wp-content/uploads/2025/09/StudentandRecruiter-768x512.jpeg)

### Student services

If you need support, it’s here\. Student Services can assist with accessibility, safety, career development, finances, health and wellness, and more\. Learn more about [our campus community](https://you.ubc.ca/ubc-life/campus-community/), including [services for students with disabilities](https://you.ubc.ca/ubc-life/campus-community/students-disabilities/)\.

[Image](https://you.ubc.ca/wp-content/uploads/2019/01/Finances_Hero_1600x900_v3-768x432.jpg)

## Budgeting for first year

***UBC provides over $50 million each year in [scholarships and awards for Canadian and International students](https://you.ubc.ca/financial-planning/) for academic excellence and leadership\.***

The cost of attending UBC will vary depending on your program, campus, and personal lifestyle\. In addition to tuition, students should plan for housing, food, transportation, books, and personal expenses\. Most bachelor degrees take four years of full\-time study to complete\.

A UBC education is an investment that will pay off for years to come\.

Estimate your costs and plan your budget for first year\.

[Use the cost estimator](https://you.ubc.ca/financial-planning/cost/)

[Embedded svg \(view source\)](https://you.ubc.ca/itsyours/)

## Get your 2027 Student Guide

If you’d like a print copy of our 2027 Student Guide, you can request one to be delivered by mail, free of charge\. In order to request a copy, you’ll first need to create an account\. From there, you can order a student guide, register for a campus tour, sign up online and in\-person events, and receive important UBC updates\.

[Get your guide](https://account.you.ubc.ca/s/get-guide)

-   [Headshot of Georgiana S](https://you.ubc.ca/wp-content/uploads/2025/01/studentstories-georgianas-768x774.jpg)
    
    “UBC has truly allowed me to create my own path\. They have countless degree programs and great opportunities such as the mentorship program I am in\. In this program, I got paired with an upper\-year student in my degree as well as a graduate who is already in the field, and they both give me the best advice\. As well, UBC offers every club you could think of\. Whatever your niche is, you will find a group of like\-minded people here\. On top of all that, UBC also has an incredible array of courses to choose from\. Anything you are curious about and want to learn more about, UBC almost always has a course for it\.”
    
    Georgiana S\. \| Natural Resources \| Toronto, Canada
    
    [Read more student stories](https://you.ubc.ca/ubc-life/blog)
    
-   [Image](https://you.ubc.ca/wp-content/uploads/2022/07/StudentStories_JasonSamuelSuwito-768x512.jpg)
    
    “UBC provides more than just a university experience\. It provides me with opportunities to explore beyond the textbook and to test and apply the knowledge that I learned in the classroom in real\-life situations\. Being able to get work experience even before you graduate is a very valuable opportunity for international students which is not offered by many universities around the world\.”
    
    Jason S\. \| Data Science \| Indonesia
    
    [Read more student stories](https://you.ubc.ca/ubc-life/blog)
    
-   [Abby with her laptop on the UBC Okanagan campus](https://you.ubc.ca/wp-content/uploads/2024/05/student-stories-abby-n-768x512.jpg)
    
    “The ability to be in a smaller tight\-knit community while having access to the resources of a larger institution is a large reason as to why I chose the Okanagan campus\. I love being a big fish in a small pond and getting to pursue different opportunities in a competitive yet supportive environment has allowed me to put myself out there, learn from my mistakes, and more importantly try again\! I also love that I'm not just a number, my faculty and professors know me by name and we're able to have meaningful conversations about their research, shared interests, and their journey of getting to where they are today\.”
    
    Abby N\. \| Management \| St\. John's, Canada
    
    [Read more student stories](https://you.ubc.ca/ubc-life/blog)
    
-   [Jamie walking outside the Longhouse on the Vancouver campus](https://you.ubc.ca/wp-content/uploads/2024/05/student-stories-jamie-c-768x512.jpg)
    
    “When I chose to study Kinesiology at UBC, I knew I wanted to find ways I could connect my degree with my Indigeneity\. Throughout my degree I have been a member of multiple committees that promote equity and diversity for Indigenous peoples, taken courses directly related to Indigenous health & wellness, and have learned from numerous Indigenous professors and mentors in Kinesiology\. All of these experiences have strengthened my desire to use my degree to connect with community and advocate for Indigenous representation in health and physical activity spaces\.”
    
    Jamie C\., Gitxsan \| Kinesiology \| Nanoose Bay, Canada
    
    [Read more student stories](https://you.ubc.ca/ubc-life/blog)
    
-   [Elleda standing in front of a concrete wall](https://you.ubc.ca/wp-content/uploads/2024/08/studentstory-elleda-e1727298346613-768x792.jpg)
    
    “When I originally came to UBC as a transfer student, I was unsure of what I wanted my academic and career futures to be\. I had just spent a year studying musical theatre in the United States, and realized it wasn't the right path for me\. After taking a campus tour of UBC Vancouver and speaking to the incredible student ambassadors, I knew transferring to UBC was a step onto the right path\. Two years later, and it is the best decision I have ever made, though it was extremely scary and nerve\-wracking at first\.”
    
    Elleda S\. \| Political Science \| Santa Cruz, USA
    
    [Read more student stories](https://you.ubc.ca/ubc-life/blog)
    
-   [Rahman sitting on stairs at UBC Okanagan](https://you.ubc.ca/wp-content/uploads/2024/09/studentstory-rahman-768x512.jpg)
    
    “There are many opportunities available at UBC to customize your own university experience\. Right from first year, I have been involved in clubs on campus, participated in numerous events, held campus positions, and so much more\. All of these allowed me to create experiences and memories I would have otherwise missed and opened doors I wouldn’t have known existed\. These experiences have also allowed me to meet and get to know people I might not have otherwise and given me many opportunities, from awards to jobs to great friends\.”
    
    Rahman G\. \| Manufacturing Engineering \| Beijing, China
    
    [Read more student stories](https://you.ubc.ca/ubc-life/blog)

title: UBC’s Vancouver campus
content_markdown:
[Ariel view of UBC's Vancouver campus](https://you.ubc.ca/wp-content/uploads/2025/05/ubc-vancouver-campus.jpg)

## On the ocean, surrounded by mountains

At UBC’s Vancouver campus, you can get a top\-tier education while living in one of the most beautiful cities in the world\. Situated on a peninsula surrounded by the Pacific Ocean, UBC Vancouver provides endless cosmopolitan experiences, breathtaking natural adventures, and an environment of academic excellence\.

[Embedded content: University of British Columbia Vancouver](https://www.youtube.com/embed/IsfRRADxqBQ?feature=oembed)

## Academic excellence

As one of the top ranked universities in the world, UBC Vancouver’s research\-intensive campus is an incubator for bright ideas and a jumping\-off point for adventure, both inside and outside the classroom\. With its cosmopolitan community and award\-winning professors, UBC’s Vancouver campus offers the chance for you to learn from some of the best faculty worldwide, contribute to projects with global significance, and have the freedom to develop your academic interests\.

-   [Danilo on a beach wearing a Yale Law School tshirt](https://you.ubc.ca/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/DaniloAM-Yale-768x440.jpeg)
    
    “What stands out most from my time at UBC is how much the university made Tuum Est feel real\. The motto, It is yours, captured the culture I experienced at UBC\. Students were encouraged to take ownership of their education, pursue what genuinely interested them, and shape their own paths\.”
    
    Danilo A\.M\. \| Political Science and International Relations
    
-   [Image](https://you.ubc.ca/wp-content/uploads/2024/09/studentstory-juliat-768x512.jpg)
    
    “I was able to get involved in diverse experiences at UBC that helped me build skills relevant to many parts of my life, including my career but also personal development and community engagement\. Not only did I discover things that I was passionate about, but equally helpful was getting to try out new experiences and figure out when they weren’t a good fit for me\. ”
    
    Julia T\. \| Global Resource Systems
    
-   [Valeria M\. UBC Story Vantage One](https://you.ubc.ca/wp-content/uploads/2020/11/Screen-Shot-2020-10-29-at-9.39.55-AM-768x547.png)
    
    “The academic excellence and prestige that we have as a university is great, but what it really makes it distinct from other universities is the endless opportunities to make your own pathway\. No\-one has the same university experience because there are so many options to make your journey unique\.”
    
    Valeria M\. \| Psychology
    

## Explore unique programs

Many programs at UBC are unique to the Vancouver campus\. With its state\-of\-the\-art facilities and modern teaching methods, UBC Vancouver helps you combine your learning with co\-op placements, undergraduate research, and work positions\. Find out which of our 150\+ programs are right for you\.

[Visit our Programs section](https://you.ubc.ca/programs/#mode=by-topic&viewMode=list&filters%5Bcampus%5D%5B%5D=9)

-   Vancouver
    
    [applied animal biology, ubc](https://you.ubc.ca/wp-content/uploads/2013/06/Applied-Animal-Biology-768x511.jpg)
    
    ### Applied Animal Biology
    
    Study the fundamentals of animal behaviour, animal physiology, and examine related fields as they apply to farm, companion, and other animals\. You’ll learn about the role of animals in human society and the ethical, environmental, and other issues th\.\.\.
    
    [Learn more](https://you.ubc.ca/programs/applied-animal-biology/ "Learn more about Applied Animal Biology")
    
-   Vancouver
    
    [Image](https://you.ubc.ca/wp-content/uploads/2013/06/Forest-Operations-768x512.jpg)
    
    ### Forest Operations
    
    If you seek the challenge of applying technology and science to create environmentally and economically sound harvesting plans, then the Forest Operations program, a major in the Bachelor of Science in Nature Resources degree, may be for you\.
    
    [Learn more](https://you.ubc.ca/programs/forest-operations/ "Learn more about Forest Operations")
    
-   Vancouver
    
    [Manufacturing Engineering on UBC's Vancouver campus](https://you.ubc.ca/wp-content/uploads/2019/08/manufacturing-engineering-hero-768x576.jpg)
    
    ### Manufacturing Engineering
    
    Learn how to design, operate, and optimize advanced manufacturing environments in UBC's Manufacturing Engineering program\.
    
    [Learn more](https://you.ubc.ca/programs/manufacturing-engineering-vancouver/ "Learn more about Manufacturing Engineering")
    
-   Vancouver
    
    [Image](https://you.ubc.ca/wp-content/uploads/2016/11/Beaty-biodiversity-museum-768x284.jpg)
    
    ### Archaeology
    
    Learn about world archaeology – from the emergence of humankind to the beginning of state societies – and examine the beginnings of the economic, social, political, and artistic traditions and systems of the great civilizations\. You can pursue studie\.\.\.
    
    [Learn more](https://you.ubc.ca/programs/archaeology/ "Learn more about Archaeology")
    
-   Vancouver
    
    [Image](https://you.ubc.ca/wp-content/uploads/2017/03/UBC-Bamfield-Marine-Sciences-Centre-768x512.jpg)
    
    ### Environmental Engineering
    
    Learn how science and engineering combine to preserve our natural environment\. The Environmental Engineering degree at UBC will teach you how to address the issues surrounding waste treatment, reuse, and recycling, as well as how to mitigate air and\.\.\.
    
    [Learn more](https://you.ubc.ca/programs/engineering-environmental/ "Learn more about Environmental Engineering")
    
-   Vancouver
    
    [International Relations, ubc vancouver](https://you.ubc.ca/wp-content/uploads/2013/06/International-Relations-Vancouver-768x511.jpg)
    
    ### International Relations
    
    Gain a deeper understanding of pertinent world issues such as international diplomacy, global economics, security, and much more\. Your coursework will span myriad subjects, from geography, anthropology, and Asian studies, to political science, sociol\.\.\.
    
    [Learn more](https://you.ubc.ca/programs/international-relations-vancouver/ "Learn more about International Relations")
    
-   Vancouver
    
    [law, ubc](https://you.ubc.ca/wp-content/uploads/2013/06/Law-768x432.jpg)
    
    ### Law
    
    At the Peter A\. Allard School of Law, you'll receive a first\-rate legal education that balances traditional areas of practice with emerging fields of specialization\. Your first year will cover common curriculum – with classes in Canadian Constitution\.\.\.
    
    [Learn more](https://you.ubc.ca/programs/law/ "Learn more about Law")
    
-   Vancouver
    
    [religion, literature, arts, ubc](https://you.ubc.ca/wp-content/uploads/2013/06/Religion-Literature-Arts-768x432.jpg)
    
    ### Religion
    
    The Program in the Study of Religion provides a solid education in a variety of religions from a number of disciplinary perspectives\. It incorporates different regions and historical periods while allowing you to focus on the religious traditions of\.\.\.
    
    [Learn more](https://you.ubc.ca/programs/religion/ "Learn more about Religion")
    

[Embedded content: Marine animal research \- UBC Faculty of Science](https://www.youtube.com/embed/RH3WMCFizX4?feature=oembed)

## Research intensive

UBC Vancouver offers you the chance to conduct your own research in the upper years of your undergraduate degree\. Work with your award\-winning faculty to pursue projects that drive your education forward\.

Find out why Sara chose UBC Vancouver, and how her studies led to opportunities in conservation and marine animal research\.

[Embedded svg \(view source\)](https://you.ubc.ca/ubc-life/vancouver/)

## Take the first step

The first step to becoming a UBC Vancouver student is to create an account\. From there, you can register for a tour of the Vancouver campus, sign up for an event in your area, attend an online info session, and be the first to receive important UBC updates\.

[Create an account](https://account.you.ubc.ca/s/create/)

## Meet your UBC Vancouver community

UBC’s community goes back over a hundred years, and connects tens of thousands of students and faculty, and hundreds of thousands of alumni\. We pride ourselves on being welcoming, inspiring, innovative, and inviting\.

At UBC’s Vancouver campus, our diverse community is made up of 49,165 undergraduate students from 147 different countries\. Here, you can make friends from across the world who share the same passions and interests as you\. Find out more about who you might meet on campus\.

[Elleda standing in front of a concrete wall](https://you.ubc.ca/wp-content/uploads/2024/08/studentstory-elleda-e1727298346613-768x792.jpg)

### Elleda, Political Science

**Santa Cruz, USA**

“UBC has empowered me to take advantage of all the resources and opportunities we have on campus to create my own tailored, unique experiences\. There are so many campus opportunities to choose from, and so many diverse students, so every individual has the chance to create their own distinctive path\.”

[Read Elleda's story](https://you.ubc.ca/ubc-life/blog/political-science-student-elleda-on-why-transferring-to-ubc-was-the-best-decision-she-ever-made/)  

[Image](https://you.ubc.ca/wp-content/uploads/2022/08/StudentStories-AndrewK.jpeg)

### Andrew, Applied Science

**Manila, Phillipines**

“UBC allowed me to have conversations with a large variety of people from different backgrounds and with widely differing perspectives\. I made sure to engage in these conversations as often as I could, whether it was with classmates, my professors, people I would meet through clubs or volunteer groups, or even prospective students and families who would come on campus tours with me\.”

[Read Andrew's story](https://you.ubc.ca/ubc-life/blog/from-applied-science-to-engineer-at-tesla/)  

[Headshot of Afnan A](https://you.ubc.ca/wp-content/uploads/2022/08/StudentStories-AfnanA.jpeg)

### Afnan, Applied Animal Biology

**Toronto, Canada**

“The nature at UBC is unmatched\! I am in constant awe that I go to such a beautiful campus\. Walking down main mall, I am mesmerized by how green and stunning our campus is\. It’s incredible to have beaches on campus\. Especially with the ocean being a huge factor in why I chose Vancouver, knowing that I don’t have to leave campus to look out onto the ocean or go to the beach is amazing\.”

[Read Afnan's story](https://you.ubc.ca/ubc-life/blog/experiential-learning-in-applied-animal-biology/)  

[Axel playing soccer, about to kick the ball](https://you.ubc.ca/wp-content/uploads/2024/11/axel-l-studentstory-768x512.jpg)

### Axel, Commerce

**Sweden**

“From playing soccer at a national level, to having fun at the best ski\-resort in the world, to traveling through Canada and working in Germany, all while studying at one of the best business schools in the world, I really could not have asked for more during my Bachelor’s degree\.”

[Read Axel's story](https://you.ubc.ca/ubc-life/blog/commerce-alum-and-soccer-player-axel-on-the-support-he-received-at-ubc-as-an-international-student-athlete/)  

## Take a self\-guided virtual tour

[https://virtualtour\.you\.ubc\.ca/ubc/vancouver\-campus](https://virtualtour.you.ubc.ca/ubc/vancouver-campus)[Image](https://you.ubc.ca/wp-content/uploads/2025/10/vancouver-virtualtour.png)

[Image](https://you.ubc.ca/wp-content/uploads/2020/01/Chan-Centre-768x481.jpg)

[Polar bear swim](https://you.ubc.ca/wp-content/uploads/2021/08/19468891253_5b3c862e79_k-768x513.jpg)

[Image](https://you.ubc.ca/wp-content/uploads/2017/03/main-life-768x444.jpg)

## Over 400 museums, art galleries, theatres, music venues, and other cultural spaces

UBC’s Vancouver campus hosts many cultural opportunities, and is minutes away from the city’s vibrant downtown district

### In the top 10 for world's most livable cities

Vancouver is known for its outdoorsy culture, 200 parks and green spaces, and three local ski hills

[Embedded svg \(view source\)](https://you.ubc.ca/ubc-life/vancouver/)

## Apply to UBC

At UBC Vancouver, you’ll find a vibrant and diverse community that will help you build your network around the world\.

Want to be part of it? Apply to UBC now, and choose “Vancouver campus”

title: Contact us

We’re here to answer your prospective undergraduate student questions, and to help you complete your application to UBC\.

For questions about graduate admissions and applying to UBC as a graduate student, visit the [Graduate Students](https://www.askme.ubc.ca/form/s/) page\.

### Need help?

Start by browsing our most common questions to see if that helps you\.

[See common questions](https://account.you.ubc.ca/s/need-help)

title: Indigenous admissions
content_markdown:
The term "Indigenous" refers inclusively to status and non\-status First Nations, Métis, and Inuit peoples of Canada, in accordance with the BC Declaration on the Rights of Indigenous Peoples Act \(DRIPA\), which defines "Indigenous peoples" as aboriginal peoples under section 35\(2\) of the Constitution Act, 1982\.

### More on Applying to UBC:

-   [Admission requirements](https://you.ubc.ca/applying-ubc/requirements/)
-   [Indigenous admissions](https://you.ubc.ca/applying-ubc/indigenous-admissions/)
-   [How to apply](https://you.ubc.ca/applying-ubc/how-to-apply/)
-   [After you've applied](https://you.ubc.ca/applying-ubc/applied/)
-   [After you’ve been admitted](https://you.ubc.ca/applying-ubc/admitted/)
-   [What we look for](https://you.ubc.ca/applying-ubc/application-evaluation/)
-   [Dates and deadlines](https://you.ubc.ca/applying-ubc/dates-deadlines/)

## On this page:

-   [UBC Aboriginal Admission Policy](https://you.ubc.ca/applying-ubc/indigenous-admissions/#section-2)
-   [Pathway programs](https://you.ubc.ca/applying-ubc/indigenous-admissions/#section-3)
-   [Application fee and housing](https://you.ubc.ca/applying-ubc/indigenous-admissions/#section-4)
-   [Connect with an advisor](https://you.ubc.ca/applying-ubc/indigenous-admissions/#section-5)

As an Indigenous student, it is important for you to self\-identify in your UBC application in order to be considered for Indigenous\-specific awards and admissions policies, and to receive information about culturally unique programs and services for First Nations, Métis, and Inuit students\.

**Most Indigenous students are admitted based on a comprehensive review of their academic average and personal profile, within [the curriculum](https://you.ubc.ca/applying-ubc/requirements/) they are studying\. However, UBC offers a number of pathways to a post\-secondary degree\.** 

## UBC Aboriginal Admission Policy

All applicants to UBC, both Indigenous and non\-Indigenous, are required to meet the university’s general admission and degree\-specific [requirements](https://you.ubc.ca/applying-ubc/requirements/)\. As with all applicants, we will review your academic history \(and depending on your degree and year level, we may also review your personal profile\), to make an admission decision\. Most Indigenous students are admitted based on meeting the requirements set out by their degree of choice\.

If you are not initially admitted, we will take a second look at your application using the Aboriginal Admission Policy\.

[Okanagan’s Aboriginal Admission Policy](http://www.calendar.ubc.ca/okanagan/index.cfm?tree=2,14,0,0)

[Vancouver’s Aboriginal Admission Policy](http://www.calendar.ubc.ca/vancouver/index.cfm?tree=2,14,0,0)

**Note about the policy name:** At UBC, we use the term “Indigenous” to refer inclusively to status and non\-status First Nations, Métis, and Inuit Peoples of Canada, in accordance with the BC Declaration on the Rights of Indigenous Peoples Act \(DRIPA\)\. The term “Aboriginal” was used in the names of some UBC policies or programs, and many of these are in the process of being updated to “Indigenous\.”

## Pathway programs

### Okanagan

**Aboriginal Access Studies**

[Aboriginal Access Studies](https://students.ok.ubc.ca/aboriginal-students/access-studies-program/) is an entrance program for UBC Okanagan that prepares and transitions Indigenous learners into degree programs at UBC\. The program combines both academic and non\-academic activities to form a rich, full\-time schedule in a supportive university setting\.

If you do not meet UBC’s general admission requirements, you can also start your studies at another college or university, and transfer to UBC later to complete your degree\. Plan carefully to ensure the courses you take are recognized by UBC and applied to your degree\-specific requirements\. The [BC Transfer Guide](https://www.bctransferguide.ca/) is a great resource for this\.

**Note about the policy name:** At UBC, we use the term “Indigenous” to refer inclusively to status and non\-status First Nations, Métis, and Inuit Peoples of Canada, in accordance with the BC Declaration on the Rights of Indigenous Peoples Act \(DRIPA\)\. The term “Aboriginal” was used in the names of some UBC policies or programs, and many of these are in the process of being updated to “Indigenous\.”

### Vancouver

**UBC\-Langara Indigenous Transfer Partnership**

If you do not meet UBC’s general admission requirements, consider starting your studies at another college or university and transferring to UBC to complete your degree\. If you plan carefully, the courses you take will be recognized by UBC and will be applied to your degree\-specific requirements\. The [BC Transfer Guide](https://www.bctransferguide.ca/) is a great resource that shows you how your college courses will be recognized by UBC\.

The [UBC\-Langara Indigenous Transfer Partnership](https://you.ubc.ca/applying-ubc/indigenous-admissions/indigenous-transfer-partnership/) at UBC Vancouver, in particular, provides the academic and personal preparation required for Indigenous students to successfully transition from Langara College to UBC’s Vancouver campus\. If you complete the Partnership’s requirements, you will be guaranteed admission to a participating UBC degree and may be eligible to receive scholarships and awards\.

## Application fee and housing

An application fee is required to submit your application\. If financial difficulty keeps you from submitting your application, please email our Indigenous recruitment team to discuss your options\.

Newly admitted Indigenous students are given priority assignment in UBC’s single\-student and year\-round housing\. If you are interested in living on campus, [apply for housing](https://vancouver.housing.ubc.ca/applications/how-to-apply/) when you [complete UBC’s online application\.](https://you.ubc.ca/applying-ubc/how-to-apply/application/) You may also apply directly to [Student Housing and Community Services](https://vancouver.housing.ubc.ca/applications/how-to-apply/application-forms/) before May 1\.

## Connect with an advisor

If you are thinking about applying to UBC, we would be pleased to meet you in person or by telephone to discuss your options and how to plan for the application process\. Already started an application? We’re here to answer your questions about the application, documents required, or the admission process\. We’re here to help\. Please contact [the UBC Indigenous recruiters\.](https://you.ubc.ca/indigenous)

**Get more information:** [indigenous\.recruitment@ubc\.ca](mailto:indigenous.recruitment@ubc.ca)  
**Book a campus tour:** [indigenous\.tours@ubc\.ca](mailto:indigenous.tours@ubc.ca)

[Find out how to apply to UBC](https://you.ubc.ca/applying-ubc/how-to-apply/) [Apply now](https://you.ubc.ca/apply/)

title: Working with an education agent
content_markdown:
Researching and applying to overseas universities can be overwhelming, and a third\-party recruiter or education agent can sometimes simplify the process\. If you are thinking of working with an agent, here are some important points to consider\.

### More on How to apply:

-   [Plan for UBC](https://you.ubc.ca/applying-ubc/how-to-apply/course-planning/)
-   [Choosing a university](https://you.ubc.ca/applying-ubc/how-to-apply/choosing-a-university/)
-   [Choose what to study](https://you.ubc.ca/applying-ubc/how-to-apply/degrees-programs/)
-   [Write your personal profile](https://you.ubc.ca/applying-ubc/how-to-apply/personal-profile/)
-   [Complete the application](https://you.ubc.ca/applying-ubc/how-to-apply/application/)
-   [Disability\-related considerations](https://you.ubc.ca/applying-ubc/how-to-apply/disability/)
-   [Working with an education agent](https://you.ubc.ca/applying-ubc/how-to-apply/working-with-an-education-agent/)

## On this page:

-   [Do you need to work with an agent to apply to UBC?](https://you.ubc.ca/applying-ubc/how-to-apply/working-with-an-education-agent/#section-1)
-   [What an agent can do for you](https://you.ubc.ca/applying-ubc/how-to-apply/working-with-an-education-agent/#section-2)
-   [What an agent cannot do for you](https://you.ubc.ca/applying-ubc/how-to-apply/working-with-an-education-agent/#section-3)
-   [Other points to consider when working with an agent](https://you.ubc.ca/applying-ubc/how-to-apply/working-with-an-education-agent/#section-4)
-   [UBC Okanagan authorized education agents](https://you.ubc.ca/applying-ubc/how-to-apply/working-with-an-education-agent/#section-5)
-   [UBC Okanagan Agent Management Team](https://you.ubc.ca/applying-ubc/how-to-apply/working-with-an-education-agent/#section-7)
-   [UBC South Asia Hub and Regional Leads](https://you.ubc.ca/applying-ubc/how-to-apply/working-with-an-education-agent/#section-8)

## Do you need to work with an agent to apply to UBC?

No\. Students are encouraged to apply directly to UBC and use the information provided in our [Applying to UBC](http://you.ubc.ca/applying-ubc/) section\.

You – not the agent – are responsible for submitting your application to UBC on time, paying your fees, and ensuring you [meet the requirements](https://you.ubc.ca/applying-ubc/requirements/)\. You are also responsible for completing all the other necessary steps to be considered for admission\.

## What an agent can do for you

-   An agent can give you information about various schools and programs that will suit your academic goals\.
-   An agent can guide you through the application process \(i\.e\. where to set up an account, where to find information, key deadlines, etc\.\)\.
-   An agent can assist you with applying for your visa and study permit \(if they are certified by [ICCRC](https://college-ic.ca/)\)\.
-   An agent can assist you with transportation\.
-   An agent can give you information and tips on living and studying in Vancouver, Kelowna, and Canada\.
-   An agent can give you information on study costs and any available funding or scholarships\.

## What an agent cannot do for you

-   Working with an agent does not increase your chances of admission or of obtaining a scholarship at UBC\. All students are assessed on the merit of their grades and overall application\.
-   An agent cannot write or assist in writing your personal profile or any part of your application\.
-   An agent cannot submit false records or documents\.
-   An agent cannot access your UBC records without your consent\. You must complete a Third\-Party Authorization for your agent to have access to your UBC information in the [Applicant Service Centre](https://myapplication.ubc.ca/)\.
-   An agent cannot submit payments for any UBC\-related fees on your behalf\.

## Other points to consider when working with an agent

-   Look for evidence that the agent specializes in Canadian higher education\.
-   Does your agent give you information on a broad enough variety of institutions?
-   Is your agent suggesting institutions and programs that fit your academic goals?
-   Does your agent have the qualifications to assist you with your Canadian visa and study permit?

**Please note:** working with an agent is your decision and it will not affect your status as an applicant to UBC\.

### Arriving by air

UBC has arranged for free airport shuttles throughout the day on Friday, April 26th which will drop you off at your accommodations at UBC \(address below\)\. These shuttles will run several times throughout the day and UBC representatives will be at the airport, near the baggage claim area, to help you locate the shuttle\.

If you experience any significant delays such as missed flights, and/or have any challenges finding UBC reps and/or the shuttle, please call or text Chloe Erlendson at **604\-362\-4993\.**

**Residence Address**  
Walter Gage Residences  
5959 Student Union Blvd\.  
Vancouver, B\.C\. V6T 1K2  
Tel: 604\.822\.1020

Once you arrive at the UBC Gage Residence, follow the signs to the Isabel MacInnes Ballroom where you will check into the event for the weekend\.

UBC has also arranged for free airport shuttles from UBC to the airport on Sunday, April 28th\. There will be rides throughout the morning based on flight departure times\. The final 2 shuttle buses will leave campus at 11am and 12pm\. If you have a later flight and do not want to head to the airport on the last shuttle, you will be responsible for your own transportation\.

### Arriving by car

When you arrive at UBC, please head to the Walter Gage Residences and use the Gage parking lot\. Destination UBC will pay for your parking for the weekend using the license plate information you provided during registration\. If this has changed, please email [chloe\.erlendson@ubc\.ca](mailto:chloe.erlendson@ubc.ca) with the updated license plate number\.

If you need help finding the parking lot, contact Chloe at **604\-362\-4993\.**

[Sponsors](https://you.ubc.ca/wp-content/uploads/2025/05/ubc-vancouver-campus.jpg)

## Welcome to UBC’s dedicated resource for sponsors

At UBC, we cherish the meaningful partnerships we have built over the years with sponsors from around the world\. These partnerships have allowed us to welcome talented students from diverse backgrounds into our vibrant academic community\. We understand that nurturing these relationships and ensuring a seamless experience for sponsored students are crucial aspects of our mission\.

## Our shared journey

UBC has long been a global leader in higher education, attracting students who aspire to make a difference in the world\. Through our strong collaborations with sponsors, we have had the privilege of hosting bright minds from every corner of the globe\. These students bring with them unique perspectives, talents, and ambitions, enriching our campus and contributing to the rich tapestry of our academic community\.

### Supporting your vision

We deeply appreciate the trust that sponsors place in UBC by sending their students to pursue undergraduate programs here\. To better serve our valued partners, we have developed a range of resources and initiatives aimed at enhancing the educational experience of sponsored students\. Our commitment to you includes:

-   **Dedicated strategic partnerships team:** UBC assigns dedicated Advisors to facilitate smooth communication and support between sponsors, sponsored students, and the university\.
-   **Customized support:** Our comprehensive support services include in\-country pre\-departure gatherings and personalized virtual one\-on\-one guidance to assist sponsored students in seamlessly becoming part of the campus community\.
-   **Online learning opportunities:** To expand access to world\-class education, UBC is proud to offer free access to select online courses through the edX platform\.

[UBC Vancouver landing page](https://you.ubc.ca/wp-content/uploads/2021/08/29468450274_9a29d82fdf_k-768x432.jpg)

### Exploring edX courses

As part of our commitment to providing valuable resources, UBC is excited to offer sponsors and their students access to a selection of free online courses\. These courses cover a wide range of subjects, from humanities to STEM, and are taught by UBC’s renowned faculty\. We believe that access to high\-quality online education can be a transformative experience, and we are delighted to share this opportunity with our partners\.

#### Getting Started with edX

Currently, UBC provides access to [65 free interactive online classes](https://www.edx.org/school/ubcx) through edX only\. Enrolling in these courses enables individuals to dive into these courses, access the materials, and have a blast learning\! Navigating the edX platform is easy, and here’s how you can get started:

-   **Visit the edX platform:** Head to the [edX website](https://www.edx.org/school/ubcx) and explore the course catalog to discover a wealth of knowledge waiting to be unlocked\.
-   **Create an account:** Individuals can create free accounts on edX to access course materials\.
-   **Enroll in courses:** Once an account is created, participants can enroll in their desired courses and begin their online learning journey\. Some UBC courses on edX offer a certificate of completion as well\.

## Gratitude and Commitment

UBC is truly honoured to be in partnership with sponsors who share our commitment to education, innovation, and global citizenship\. We look forward to strengthening our bonds as we work together to shape a brighter future through education\. Should you have any questions or require further assistance, our dedicated Advisors are here to help and can be reached at [sponsorstudent\.intl@ubc\.ca\.](mailto:sponsorstudent.intl@ubc.ca)

title: Applied Science (Engineering) at UBC Okanagan
content_markdown:
[Applied Science \(Engineering\) at UBC Okanagan](https://you.ubc.ca/wp-content/uploads/2022/09/applied-science-ubc-okangan.jpg)

## Innovative research\. Integrated project\-based learning\.

UBC Okanagan’s Applied Science program is among the fastest growing engineering programs in Canada\. With four degree options to choose from that focus on research and project\-based learning, you will open the door to in\-demand careers and be a part of global solutions\.

[Image](https://you.ubc.ca/wp-content/uploads/2022/09/applied-science-facilities-768x480.png)

## World\-class facilities

The engineering program on UBC’s Okanagan campus has state\-of\-the\-art new facilities for teaching and research, including undergraduate laboratories and research labs\.

Get a glimpse of life as an undergraduate student at UBC’s Faculty of Applied Science by reading our student and faculty stories, and find out whether one of their degrees will be right for you too\.

[Image](https://you.ubc.ca/wp-content/uploads/2017/07/Joses-Akampurira.jpg)

[Life in the School of Engineering](https://you.ubc.ca/ubc-life/blog/joses-akampurira-ubc-okanagan-engineering/)

[The research connection](https://you.ubc.ca/ubc-life/blog/jonathan-holzman-research-connection/)  

### Among the fastest growing engineering programs in Canada\.

[Image](https://you.ubc.ca/wp-content/uploads/2022/09/applied-science-program-options-e1727971362393-768x411.jpeg)

## Explore your program options

The curriculum emphasizes interdisciplinary, project\-based learning\. Our world\-class faculty and researchers are committed to an instructional approach that is varied, experiential, and engaging\. Our close\-knit, student\-centred program affords high levels of student\-professor interaction and collaborations\.

[Visit our Programs section](https://you.ubc.ca/programs/)

-   Okanagan
    
    [civil engineering, ubc](https://you.ubc.ca/wp-content/uploads/2013/06/Civil-Engineering-Okanagan-768x512.jpg)
    
    ### Civil Engineering
    
    In Civil Engineering, you’ll build a solid foundation, from the ground up – from soil mechanics and foundation engineering, to the design of structures, roads and transportation networks, river and flood management systems, construction management an\.\.\.
    
    [Learn more](https://you.ubc.ca/programs/civil-engineering-okanagan/ "Learn more about Civil Engineering")
    
-   Okanagan
    
    [Manufacturing Engineering on UBC's Okanagan campus](https://you.ubc.ca/wp-content/uploads/2019/09/manufacturing-engineering-okanagan-768x512.jpg)
    
    ### Manufacturing Engineering
    
    Important notice: The Manufacturing Engineering program is currently not accepting new students\. Contact UBC Okanagan's School of Engineering for questions at soe\.advising@ubc\.ca\.  
    
    [Learn more](https://you.ubc.ca/programs/manufacturing-engineering-okanagan/ "Learn more about Manufacturing Engineering")
    
-   Okanagan
    
    [electrical engineering, ubc](https://you.ubc.ca/wp-content/uploads/2013/06/Electrical-Engineering-Okanagan-768x512.jpg)
    
    ### Electrical Engineering
    
    Study at the cutting\-edge of technology and be part of global solutions related to energy conservation, power grids, communications networks, and intelligent products\. You’ll be solidly schooled from the ground up before studying modern topics in ele\.\.\.
    
    [Learn more](https://you.ubc.ca/programs/electrical-engineering-okanagan/ "Learn more about Electrical Engineering")
    
-   Okanagan
    
    [mechanical engineering, ubc okanagan](https://you.ubc.ca/wp-content/uploads/2013/06/Mechanical-Engineering-Okanagan--768x512.jpg)
    
    ### Mechanical Engineering
    
    Investigate practical, hands\-on ways of creating and improving physical systems to meet the demand of modern industries, from aircraft and energy systems to biomedical, mechatronics, and manufacturing\.
    
    [Learn more](https://you.ubc.ca/programs/mechanical-engineering-okanagan/ "Learn more about Mechanical Engineering")
    

-   [Image](https://you.ubc.ca/wp-content/uploads/2017/07/Joses-Akampurira.jpg)
    
    “I am proud to belong to UBC \- the institution and the community\. UBC is like family\.”

## Meals

We will provide your meals during your stay on campus\. Please let us know about your dietary restrictions \(if you haven’t done so already\)\. Email us at [destination\.ubc@ubc\.ca](mailto:destination.ubc@ubc.ca)\. **Note:** parents and/or other guests will not be provided with meals\.

## What to pack

In addition to any personal items and clothes you bring with you, consider bringing:

-   -   Any medications you require for the duration of your stay
    -   Comfortable shoes walking and running
    -   A small backpack or bag to carry your things

-   Outdoor clothing in case of rain, including a raincoat and umbrella
-   Cell phone and charger
-   Personal toiletries, including a towel and a hair dryer
-   Personal items such as musical instruments, a yoga mat, sunglasses, etc\.
-   Spending money for the UBC Bookstore and snacks
-   A reusable water bottle

The weather can be a bit unpredictable at this time of year, it’s a good idea to check the forecast when you pack\!

title: Jump Start Vancouver’s frequently asked questions
content_markdown:
## Eligibility 

**Can I participate in the Jump Start program?** 

The Jump Start program is designed for students who are transitioning directly from high school to university\. You are eligible to participate if you meet any of the following criteria: 

-   You are entering UBC directly from high school or CEGEP 

-   You have taken a gap year of up to two years after high school 

-   You have completed no more than 4 months of post\-secondary study \(e\.g\., UBC Summer Session courses\) 

If you have any questions about eligibility or if you have issues with registration, please email us at [orientations\.jumpstart@ubc\.ca](mailto:orientations.jumpstart@ubc.ca)  

## Residence stream

**Can I register for Jump Start before I get my Winter Session housing offer?**

Yes, you can register for Jump Start before you receive and accept your housing offer\. The fee for meals and housing during Jump Start is paid when accepting your Winter Session housing offer\.

## Indigenous students 

**I am an Indigenous student, what do I need to know about registering for Jump Start?** 

If you are an Indigenous student and have self\-identified in UBC’s Workday system, the Jump Start program fee of $75 \(\+ tax\) will be waived\. 

## International students

**I’m waiting for an update on the status of my Visa application\. Can I register for Jump Start?**

Yes, you can still register for Jump Start while you wait on the status of your visa application\.

## Transfer students 

**Can transfer students participate in the Jump Start program?** 

The Jump Start program is designed specifically for students transitioning directly from high school to university academics\. As a result, registration for Jump Start is not open to transfer students\. 

Transfer student’s orientation to UBC happens during [Imagine UBC](https://students.ubc.ca/new-to-ubc/orientations/imagine-ubc) on Tuesday Sept 8\. This will be an opportunity for you to familiarize yourself with the campus and meet other transfer students\.  You will receive information about Imagine UBC closer to the event\. 

## Options for financial support 

**Are there any financial support options for me?** 

If cost is a barrier to participating in Jump Start, financial support is available\. [Your Enrolment Services Advisor \(ESA\)](https://workday.students.ubc.ca/ubc-advisor-contacts/finding-your-enrolment-services-advisors-contact-information/) can help you explore payment plans, fee deferrals, or full fee waivers based on your situation\. Reach out to discuss your options and get support\. 

## Program schedules 

**How long does Jump Start run each day?** 

For students living in residence, typically, the days start around 9:00am and the main programming ends around 4:30pm\. Following that, there are various social programs available for students to choose from approximately 7:00pm to 9:00pm\. The schedule includes meal breaks and other breaks throughout the day\. 

For students commuting to campus, typically the days start around 9:00am and end around 5:00pm\. There are optional social activities in the evening\.

## Event attendance 

**Is it okay if I miss an event during Jump Start?** 

We understand that you may be busy, and it is completely okay if you miss an event during Jump Start\. However, we highly recommend attending as many events as possible to fully benefit from the program and make the most of your Jump Start experience\! Make sure to tell your orientation leaders if you cannot attend any event\. 

## Residence stream 

### Move\-in date 

**When is the move\-in date? Do I need to apply for an early move\-in?** 

The move\-in date for Jump Start students in residence is Tuesday, September 1st\. There is no additional application for early move\-in\. It is important to note that students cannot move into UBC housing before September 1st, 2026\.

### Late arrival 

**What should I do if I am unable to move into residence on September 1st as a Jump Start residence student?** 

For Move\-in Day, you will need to reserve a move\-in time slot\. Details on how to reserve your check\-in time will be sent to you in August\. If you arrive after 3pm, you can still move in by checking in at your residence area front desk upon arrival\.

We strongly recommend residence students arrive no later than the evening of Tuesday, September 1st, so that you have enough time to connect with your group and participate in the program\. However, we understand that there may be situations where this is not possible\. If you are unable to arrive on the specified move\-in date, you will still be able to check in at a later date\. Simply go to your residence area front desk to check in upon your arrival and they will assist you with checking into your residence room\. You will receive your welcome pack, including your UBC card, during the check\-in process\. 

Please note that the front desks are closed from 11:00pm until 7:00am, so it is not possible to check in during these hours\. 

The additional Jump Start housing and meals fee for residence students remains the same, even if you are moving in late\. 

## Housing after Jump Start 

**Will I be able to live in the same room after Jump Start?** 

Yes, the room you are assigned during Jump Start is the same for the rest of the year\. This means that you can continue to live there in the time between Jump Start and when classes begin \(September 5 – 8\)\. The Jump Start fee will cover your meals and accommodation for the time in between when Jump Start ends and when the non\-Jump Start students move in\. 

## Commuter stream 

**Which stream am I part of if I live at University Village or Wesbrook Village?** 

If you live in University Village or Wesbrook Village you are considered a commuter student\. You are therefore eligible to be part of the [Collegia program](https://students.ubc.ca/new-to-ubc/ubc-collegia) and would be in the commuter stream for Jump Start\.

title: Bachelor of Applied Science (Engineering)
content_markdown:
[Bachelor of Applied Science \(Engineering\)](https://you.ubc.ca/wp-content/uploads/2019/08/manufacturing-engineering-hero.jpg)

## Engineering a better future\.

The Bachelor of Applied Science \(Engineering\) opens doors to a future where your curiosity can thrive\. With 14 degree programs on two campuses, you will join a top\-ranked engineering program where you can collaborate, design and develop innovative solutions that make a difference in people’s lives\. Develop highly sought\-after skills that prepare you for a versatile career where you can contribute to solving the world’s most complex challenges\.

[Image](https://you.ubc.ca/wp-content/uploads/2022/09/applied-science-program-options-e1727971362393-768x411.jpeg)

## Learn from professors who are outstanding leaders in their field\.

Your professors are innovative thinkers who will inspire and nurture you to find bold solutions in an entrepreneurial and innovative learning environment\.

Meet a few members of UBC’s engineering community and learn how their engineering education opened the door to exciting opportunities

[Rahman sitting on stairs at UBC Okanagan](https://you.ubc.ca/wp-content/uploads/2024/09/studentstory-rahman-768x512.jpg)

[Manufacturing Engineering student Rahman on how his passions helped shape his university experience](https://you.ubc.ca/ubc-life/blog/manufacturing-engineering-student-rahman-on-how-his-passions-helped-shape-his-university-experience/)  

[Image](https://you.ubc.ca/wp-content/uploads/2015/03/Photo_Fawaz_Al_Nassar_Profile_Viewbook_2015-626x360-1.jpg)

[Opportunities for student\-professor collaboration](https://you.ubc.ca/ubc-life/blog/fawaz-story/)  

[Image](https://you.ubc.ca/wp-content/uploads/2017/07/Joses-Akampurira.jpg)

[Life in the School of Engineering](https://you.ubc.ca/ubc-life/blog/joses-akampurira-ubc-okanagan-engineering/)  

### 14 undergraduate Engineering program options at UBC

[electrical engineering, ubc](https://you.ubc.ca/wp-content/uploads/2013/06/Electrical-Engineering-Vancouver-2-768x432.jpg)

[environmental engineering, ubc](https://you.ubc.ca/wp-content/uploads/2013/06/Environmental-Engineering-768x511.jpg)

[Students in the UBC LIfe Building on their laptops](https://you.ubc.ca/wp-content/uploads/2024/04/ubc-campus-wide-login-768x511.jpg)

## Your BASc program

Pursue your interests and watch them flourish in a collaborative, inclusive engineering community\. You’ll gain a broad understanding of engineering in your foundational first year, then select a program to focus on for the remainder of your BASc degree\.

[Biomedical Engineering](https://you.ubc.ca/wp-content/uploads/2020/10/MD1_1240-768x513.jpg)

## A strong foundation for your 1st year

UBC’s Engineering foundation year will introduce you to math, chemistry, physics and communication courses, giving you the fundamental knowledge you need to succeed as an engineer\. You’ll also get hands\-on opportunities to apply your knowledge and work on exciting engineering design projects\. After your first year, you’ll be in a great place to decide which engineering program you’d like pursue in your BASc degree\.

Explore [First Year BASc Vancouver](https://you.ubc.ca/programs/)

Explore [First Year BASc Okanagan](https://you.ubc.ca/programs/)

[international students, ubc](https://you.ubc.ca/wp-content/uploads/2019/04/international-students-ubc.jpg)

## 2nd Year Placement

This is when you will need to make some decisions about a specific engineering program you’d like to specialize in during your BASc degree\. But no matter where your curiosity takes you, each program will offer an exciting opportunity to develop your unique skills and discover new ones through coursework, applied research, co\-ops and involvement opportunities\.

## BASc program options

Explore some of the programs in the BASc degree but keep in mind, not all programs are offered on both campuses\. Additionally, if you have more than 26 credits of engineering transfer credit, you may be eligible for second\-year engineering\. See [Admission from a Post\-Secondary Institution](https://vancouver.calendar.ubc.ca/node/14478#1061)\.

[Visit our Programs section](https://you.ubc.ca/programs/)

-   Okanagan
    
    [civil engineering, ubc](https://you.ubc.ca/wp-content/uploads/2013/06/Civil-Engineering-Okanagan-768x512.jpg)
    
    ### Civil Engineering
    
    In Civil Engineering, you’ll build a solid foundation, from the ground up – from soil mechanics and foundation engineering, to the design of structures, roads and transportation networks, river and flood management systems, construction management an\.\.\.
    
    [Learn more](https://you.ubc.ca/programs/civil-engineering-okanagan/ "Learn more about Civil Engineering")
    
-   Okanagan
    
    [Computer Engineering student at her computer](https://you.ubc.ca/wp-content/uploads/2024/03/computer-engineering-okanagan-768x511.jpg)
    
    ### Computer Engineering
    
    UBC Okanagan's Computer Engineering program blends a selection of foundational courses from Electrical Engineering and Computer Science with specialized Computer Engineering courses\.  
      
    The program integrates a project\-based learning envi\.\.\.
    
    [Learn more](https://you.ubc.ca/programs/computer-engineering-okanagan/ "Learn more about Computer Engineering")
    
-   Vancouver
    
    [Image](https://you.ubc.ca/wp-content/uploads/2020/10/MD1_9170-768x513.jpg)
    
    ### Biomedical Engineering
    
    Learn how to apply engineering principles and design to medicine and biology for healthcare purposes in Biomedical Engineering\. You'll start by building a foundation in biomechanics and biomaterials, cellular and molecular bioengineering, biomedical\.\.\.
    
    [Learn more](https://you.ubc.ca/programs/biomedical-engineering/ "Learn more about Biomedical Engineering")
    

## Explore all BASc programs

Learn more about UBC Engineering and all [14 undergraduate engineering programs](https://engineering.ubc.ca/programs/undergraduate) offering exciting research, team collaboration and co\-op opportunities\.

-   [Rahman sitting on stairs at UBC Okanagan](https://you.ubc.ca/wp-content/uploads/2024/09/studentstory-rahman-768x512.jpg)
    
    “From a young age, I've been captivated by how things are made and how they work, which sparked my curiosity about engineering in the first place\. This passion led me to choose Manufacturing Engineering, a field that perfectly aligns with my fascination with creating efficient, innovative, and sustainable manufacturing systems\. I was able to be involved in interesting projects as part of my degree, ranging from creating a \(highly detailed\) CAD model of an A380, to creating chatbots, to building a motor from scratch, to programming entire automated assembly lines, and so much more\.”
    
    Rhaman G\.
    

[UBC Vancouver Arial](https://you.ubc.ca/wp-content/uploads/2021/08/47954308962_b0a74a9545_k-768x432.jpg)

### Your future

The BASc degree will equip you with highly employable skills\. See where a degree in engineering has taken our graduates\!

[civil engineering, ubc](https://you.ubc.ca/wp-content/uploads/2013/06/Civil-engineering-Vancouver-2-768x432.jpg)

### What our graduates are doing with their BA degrees

-   Business Development Executive, Unity Technologies
-   Project Manager, Microsoft Education Product Team
-   Vice President, Planning & Strategy, Base Metals
-   Project Engineer with the Vancouver Board of Parks and Recreation
-   Mechanical Staff Engineer at Intel Corporation
-   Materials & Sustainability Engineer at Boeing
-   Senior Hardware Engineer, Apple
-   ADAS Software Engineer, General Motors
-   Ports and Marine Engineer at WSP

[mechanical engineering, ubc](https://you.ubc.ca/wp-content/uploads/2013/06/Mechanical-Engineering-Vancouver-2-768x432.jpg)

### Meet our alumni

Discover more [Engineering Alumni stories](https://engineering.ubc.ca/spotlight/alumni)  and get inspired by where your BASc may take you\!

[Embedded svg \(view source\)](https://you.ubc.ca/engineering/)

## Take the first step

The first step to becoming a student in the Faculty of Applied Science is to create an account\. From there, you can register for a campus tour of the Vancouver or Okanagan campus, attend an online info session, and be the first to receive important UBC updates\.

[Create an account](https://account.you.ubc.ca/s/create)

Start your online application

If you have any questions about the collection, use, or disclosure of your personal information, please [contact us](https://you.ubc.ca/contact-us/)\.

title: Choosing a university
content_markdown:
Choosing which universities to apply to isn’t easy\. How do you know which one is right for you? Here are a few tips to help you get started\.

### More on How to apply:

-   [Plan for UBC](https://you.ubc.ca/applying-ubc/how-to-apply/course-planning/)
-   [Choosing a university](https://you.ubc.ca/applying-ubc/how-to-apply/choosing-a-university/)
-   [Choose what to study](https://you.ubc.ca/applying-ubc/how-to-apply/degrees-programs/)
-   [Write your personal profile](https://you.ubc.ca/applying-ubc/how-to-apply/personal-profile/)
-   [Complete the application](https://you.ubc.ca/applying-ubc/how-to-apply/application/)
-   [Disability\-related considerations](https://you.ubc.ca/applying-ubc/how-to-apply/disability/)
-   [Working with an education agent](https://you.ubc.ca/applying-ubc/how-to-apply/working-with-an-education-agent/)

## Consider how the school stacks up

A university education is a big investment, and the school you choose sends a signal to the world\. At a top\-ranked school, you’ll enjoy one of the best educations in the world and join the workforce with a wealth of options\. Graduating with a degree from a [top 45 research university](https://www.ubc.ca/about/) like UBC says something about you, and can open doors around the globe when you’re looking to begin your career\.

## Check out your academic options

If you have a [program](https://you.ubc.ca/programs/) in mind, check out what and where you’ll learn\. If you’re still not sure what to study, look for a school and degree that will give you lots of options down the road\. Some universities provide the opportunity for combined programs, or let you select from a range of different electives across multiple subjects while still fulfilling the requirements for your degree\. At UBC, you can choose from among 43 undergraduate degrees and hundreds of opportunities for specialization\.

## Choose a place you want to live

It’s important that the campus you choose is the right fit for you\. Universities can be rural or urban, in a major metropolis, or form mini\-cities of their own\. Some schools place more of an emphasis on academics, while others have a tradition of excellence in sports or the arts\. UBC’s Okanagan and Vancouver campuses both have [inclusive, well\-rounded communities](https://you.ubc.ca/ubc-life/campus-community/) that will welcome and support you in whatever you’re passionate about, and each one offers a [distinctive experience](https://you.ubc.ca/ubc-life/) and unique path to a UBC degree\.

## Picture yourself on campus

Most schools offer campus tours, and many also offer online events for you to get to know the campuses you’re considering\. At UBC, we have [in\-person campus tours](https://account.you.ubc.ca/s/events), where you’re invited to check out the facilities in person\. If you’re unable to make it to Vancouver or the Okanagan, you can take advantage of a [live virtual campus tour from home](https://account.you.ubc.ca/s/events) or a [self\-guided virtual tour](https://you.ubc.ca/tours-events/virtual-tour/) that you can take at any time\. You’ll get a sense of where you could be going to lectures and studying for exams, eating lunch, and hanging out with friends between classes\.

## Explore your career opportunities

It’s important that the university you choose will prepare you for the future\. Will going to the university help you land your dream job? Does it offer the [program](https://you.ubc.ca/programs) you need to get the career you want? Are there opportunities for [hands\-on experiences](https://you.ubc.ca/ubc-life/getting-involved/work-programs/) like research opportunities, academic exchanges, or co\-op programs to get paid work experience before you graduate? Does the university offer resume and other [career services](https://students.ubc.ca/career/career-resources/)?

## Estimate your costs

Going to university is an investment in your future, and the costs can add up\. Tuition varies across schools, as do the living costs, financial assistance, and awards available to you\. You can usually find out all you need to know about planning your finances from a university’s website\. For UBC, you can estimate your costs and put together a budget with our [cost estimator](https://you.ubc.ca/financial-planning/cost/)\.

-   [Kelsey standing in the UBC Okanagan library](https://you.ubc.ca/wp-content/uploads/2025/10/Kelsey-Library-768x432.jpeg.webp)
    
    “I wanted a place where I could grow both personally and academically, and UBCO stood out because of its sense of community and support\. I loved that it wasn’t too big or overwhelming; I could build genuine connections with professors and peers\. I felt confident that UBCO would give me the space to figure out who I wanted to be while still having strong academic programs and opportunities\.”
    
    Kelsey, fourth year Arts student at UBC Okanagan

## Your admission requirements

Admission to UBC is competitive, and your requirements change depending on your degree and campus of choice\. All applicants must meet UBC’s general admission requirements and English Language Admission Standard\.

[International high school applicant requirements](https://you.ubc.ca/applying-ubc/requirements/international-high-schools)  
[International Baccalaureate applicant requirements](https://you.ubc.ca/applying-ubc/requirements/international-baccalaureate/)  
[University or college student applicant requirements](https://you.ubc.ca/applying-ubc/requirements/university-college-transfer/)

## Scholarships and awards for International students

UBC recognizes the academic achievement of outstanding students from around the world by devoting more than $35 million annually to awards, scholarships, and other forms of financial support for international undergraduate students\. [Find out more about awards for International students](https://you.ubc.ca/financial-planning/scholarships-awards-international-students/)\.

## English Language Admissions Standard

English is the primary language of instruction at UBC\. All prospective students are required to demonstrate a minimum level of English before they’re admitted\. [Find out how to meet UBC’s English Language Admission Standard\.](https://you.ubc.ca/applying-ubc/requirements/english-language-competency/)

## How to apply for a study permit

International students need a valid study permit to attend UBC\. Getting a permit can take several months, so be sure to begin the process as soon as you can\. [Find out how to apply\.](https://you.ubc.ca/applying-ubc/admitted/study-permit/)

## International student supports

### Enrolment Services Advisors

Get advice and support from Enrolment Services Advisors on the [Okanagan](https://ok.ubc.ca/faculty-and-staff/enrolment-services/) or [Vancouver](https://students.ubc.ca/about-student-services/enrolment-services-advisors/) campus

### Study permit concierge

To help students apply for a study permit and navigate Immigration, Refugees and Citizenship Canada \(IRCC\), UBC offers complimentary [study permit concierge services\.](https://you.ubc.ca/applying-ubc/admitted/study-permit/study-permit-concierge/) These services are designed to provide you with resources and real\-time guidance as you work through your study permit application process\.

### Global Pathways \(Okanagan\)

Global Pathways is for international students on the Okanagan campus to assist with planning their career and immigration success\.

[Find out more about Global Pathways](https://students.ok.ubc.ca/career-experience/global-pathways/)

I had just spent a year studying musical theatre in the United States, and realized it wasn’t the right path for me\. After taking a campus tour of UBC Vancouver and speaking to the incredible student ambassadors, I knew transferring to UBC was a step onto the right path\. Two years later, and it is the best decision I have ever made\.”
    
    Elleda S\. \| Political Science \| USA

I loved that it wasn’t too big or overwhelming; I could build genuine connections with professors and peers\.
