title: Plan your future in Arts at UBC Vancouver
content_markdown:
Thinking about a Bachelor of Arts at UBC Vancouver? We’ll send you all the information you need to make your decision and prepare your application\.

Sign up for:

-   Info on Arts Vancouver programs that **match your interests**
-   **Key admission reminders** and deadline alerts
-   Invites to **exclusive UBC events** \(online and in your area\)

## Sign up to get an email about Arts

Indicates required fields

**Collection of personal information**

The University of British Columbia \(UBC\) collects your personal information under the authority of section 26\(c\) of the BC Freedom of Information and Protection of Privacy Act, for the purpose of connecting you to relevant UBC programs, services, awards, and opportunities offered by the university\. If you have any questions about the collection, use, or disclosure of your personal information, please [contact us](https://you.ubc.ca/contact-us/)\.

[Instructor teaching in a classroom\.](https://you.ubc.ca/wp-content/uploads/2024/10/Teacher46890965155_836b3027d6_k-e1727910150283-768x438.jpg)

## Learn with internationally renowned instructors

The Bachelor of Arts instructors are recognized researchers and leaders in social sciences, humanities, and the creative and performing arts, delivering an unparalleled learning experience for their students\.

## Student life

Meet the diverse community of students and professors and learn how they shaped their unique academic experience\.

[Hammad J stands in road with a pack and water bottle\.](https://you.ubc.ca/wp-content/uploads/2024/11/HammadJabr-1-scaled-e1731607324552-768x483.jpg)

[Geography student Hammad on how the small class sizes made it easier to build friendships and express himself in class](https://you.ubc.ca/ubc-life/blog/interdisciplinary-studies-offers-space-to-grow/)  

[Elleda standing in front of a concrete wall](https://you.ubc.ca/wp-content/uploads/2024/08/studentstory-elleda-e1727298346613-768x792.jpg)

[Political Science student Elleda on why transferring to UBC was the best decision she ever made](https://you.ubc.ca/ubc-life/blog/political-science-student-elleda-on-why-transferring-to-ubc-was-the-best-decision-she-ever-made/)  

[Danilo on a beach wearing a Yale Law School tshirt](https://you.ubc.ca/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/DaniloAM-Yale-768x440.jpeg)

[Political Science alum Danilo on how UBC helped him achieve his career goals and shaped his path to Yale Law School](https://you.ubc.ca/ubc-life/blog/political-science-alum-danilo-on-heading-to-yale-law-school/)  

### 70\+ undergraduate Arts program options at UBC Vancouver

[Students hanging out at the quad at UBC Vancouver](https://you.ubc.ca/wp-content/uploads/2026/02/thebigquestion-768x512.jpg)

[Ariel view of UBC's Vancouver campus](https://you.ubc.ca/wp-content/uploads/2025/05/ubc-vancouver-campus-768x431.jpg)

[A row of students in a Commerce class](https://you.ubc.ca/wp-content/uploads/2025/10/commerce-studentclass-768x461.png)

## Explore your program options

Create a customized curriculum that tackles global issues and explores the opportunities and challenges of the 21st century\. Deeply engage with subjects that matter to you and align with your personal, educational, and career goals\.

[View our programs section](https://you.ubc.ca/programs/)

## Arts programs

-   Vancouver
    
    [creative writing, ubc vancouver](https://you.ubc.ca/wp-content/uploads/2013/06/Creative-Writing-BFA-Vancouver-768x511.jpg)
    
    ### Creative Writing
    
    This two\-year studio program offers workshops in the following genres: fiction, poetry, creative non\-fiction, writing for children, translation, stage play, radio, television, song lyric and libretto, screenwriting, new media, and writing for graphic\.\.\.
    
    [Learn more](https://you.ubc.ca/programs/creative-writing-vancouver/ "Learn more about Creative Writing")
    
-   Vancouver
    
    [Image](https://you.ubc.ca/wp-content/uploads/2013/06/Mathematics-BA-Vancouver-768x432.jpg)
    
    ### Mathematics \(BA\)
    
    Mathematics majors apply math, probability, statistics, and the principles of business and finance to analyze statistical data and assess business risks\. Mathematics at UBC provides an excellent balance of pure and applied mathematics and is useful,\.\.\.
    
    [Learn more](https://you.ubc.ca/programs/mathematics-vancouver-ba/ "Learn more about Mathematics (BA)")
    
-   Vancouver
    
    [UBC Psychology](https://you.ubc.ca/wp-content/uploads/2013/06/UBC-Vancouver-Psychology-768x432.jpg)
    
    ### Psychology
    
    Study human and animal behaviour using scientific methods and from a variety of perspectives including behavioural neuroscience, cognition, clinical, health, developmental, social and personality psychology, and quantitative methods\.
    
    [Learn more](https://you.ubc.ca/programs/psychology-vancouver-ba/ "Learn more about Psychology")
    
-   Vancouver
    
    [first nations and indigenous studies, ubc](https://you.ubc.ca/wp-content/uploads/2013/06/First-Nations-Indigenous-Studies-768x508.jpg)
    
    ### First Nations and Indigenous Studies
    
    Gain an understanding of the histories, contemporary realities, and political concerns of Indigenous peoples in Canada and beyond\. This interdisciplinary program reflects the belief that deep understanding and ethical engagement are central to the we\.\.\.
    
    [Learn more](https://you.ubc.ca/programs/first-nations-indigenous-studies/ "Learn more about First Nations and Indigenous Studies")
    
-   Vancouver
    
    [film studies, ubc](https://you.ubc.ca/wp-content/uploads/2013/06/Film-Studies-768x432.jpg)
    
    ### Cinema Studies
    
    Learn about the diversity of World Cinema and cinematic aesthetic practices\. As a Cinema Studies student, you will explore the cultural roles of films and how they impact our political and social perceptions\.
    
    [Learn more](https://you.ubc.ca/programs/cinema-studies/ "Learn more about Cinema Studies")
    
-   Vancouver
    
    [economics, ubc vancouver](https://you.ubc.ca/wp-content/uploads/2013/06/Economics-Vancouver-768x432.jpg)
    
    ### Economics
    
    Gain a deep understanding of the economy and examine the social, cross\-cultural, and ethical dimensions of economic decision\-making\. You’ll learn how to choose and apply appropriate quantitative methods to a range of economic issues, and effectively\.\.\.
    
    [Learn more](https://you.ubc.ca/programs/economics-vancouver/ "Learn more about Economics")
    
-   Vancouver
    
    [computer science, ubc vancouver](https://you.ubc.ca/wp-content/uploads/2013/06/Computer-Science-Vancouver-BA-768x511.jpg)
    
    ### Computer Science \(BA\)
    
    Learn how to use and improve computers while you explore topics such as databases and operating systems, software engineering, security, web development, and numerical methodology\. Computer Science gives you a thorough grounding in computer software\.\.\.
    
    [Learn more](https://you.ubc.ca/programs/computer-science-vancouver-ba/ "Learn more about Computer Science (BA)")
    
-   Vancouver
    
    [International Relations, ubc vancouver](https://you.ubc.ca/wp-content/uploads/2013/06/International-Relations-Vancouver-768x511.jpg)
    
    ### International Relations
    
    Gain a deeper understanding of pertinent world issues such as international diplomacy, global economics, security, and much more\. Your coursework will span myriad subjects, from geography, anthropology, and Asian studies, to political science, sociol\.\.\.
    
    [Learn more](https://you.ubc.ca/programs/international-relations-vancouver/ "Learn more about International Relations")
    

[Students hanging out on the Vancouver campus in the Nest\.](https://you.ubc.ca/wp-content/uploads/2024/07/ubc-business-markets-768x432.jpg)

## Personalized pathways

Start your first year of studies in a supportive cohort or customize your timetable to suit your schedule and subject interests\. Learn more about [first\-year study options](https://you.ubc.ca/applying-ubc/applied/first-year-study-options/) in the BA degree\.

-   [Danilo on a beach wearing a Yale Law School tshirt](https://you.ubc.ca/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/DaniloAM-Yale-768x440.jpeg)
    
    “Looking back, my studies in Political Science and International Relations at UBC laid the foundation for everything that followed…More than any specific class or experience, what I remember most is being empowered to take initiative and build a path that felt uniquely my own\.”
    
    Danilo A\.M\. \| Political Science
    
-   [Elleda standing in front of a wall at UBC Vancouver](https://you.ubc.ca/wp-content/uploads/2024/08/elleda-studentstory-768x512.jpg)
    
    “UBC has empowered me to take advantage of all the resources and opportunities we have on campus to create my own tailored, unique experiences\.”
    
    Elleda S\. \| BA in Political Science
    
-   [Hammad J stands in road with a pack and water bottle\.](https://you.ubc.ca/wp-content/uploads/2024/11/HammadJabr-1-scaled-e1731607324552-768x483.jpg)
    
    “One of the highlights of my program has been connecting with people who have similar interests and values\. The smaller class sizes have allowed me to build close relationships with students and award\-winning faculty, participate in class discussions and engage with others\. I experienced a sense of belonging and support\. ”
    
    Hammad J\. \| Geography
    

[UBC Vancouver Arial](https://you.ubc.ca/wp-content/uploads/2021/08/47954308962_b0a74a9545_k-768x432.jpg)

### Your future

The flexibility of the BA degree lets you choose subjects that align with your career goals, gain hands\-on experience with employers during your studies, and equip you with highly employable skills as you graduate\.

[Image](https://you.ubc.ca/wp-content/uploads/2022/07/StudentStories_AndrejG_VancouverCampus.jpg)

### What our graduates are doing with their Arts degrees

-   Product designer at Yahoo
-   Policy officer, Department of National Defence
-   Project manager, Aboriginal Health, Vancouver Coastal Health
-   Trade Policy Analyst, Global Affairs Canada
-   Mobile Game Developer
-   Lawyer, Ontario Ministry of the Attorney General
-   Senior Editorial Producer, ABC News

[Image](https://you.ubc.ca/wp-content/uploads/2013/08/buchanan-768x512.jpg)

### Meet our alumni

Read more [Arts alumni stories](https://www.arts.ubc.ca/alumni/profiles/) and get inspired by where your BA may take you\!

title: How to change the degree you applied to
content_markdown:
If you want to change the degree that you applied to, make sure you understand the admission requirements for the new degree, that making the change may affect your award eligibility, and the deadline to make your changes\.

### More on After you’ve applied:

-   [Admissions decisions](https://you.ubc.ca/applying-ubc/applied/admissions-decisions/)
-   [Submit your documents](https://you.ubc.ca/applying-ubc/applied/submit-documents/)

-   [First\-year study options](https://you.ubc.ca/applying-ubc/applied/first-year-study-options/)
-   [How to change the degree you applied to](https://you.ubc.ca/applying-ubc/applied/change-degree/)
-   [Appeals](https://you.ubc.ca/applying-ubc/applied/admission-appeals/)

## How to change your degree

Before you change your degree you need to:

-   Check the [admissions requirements](https://you.ubc.ca/applying-ubc/requirements/) for your new degree choice and make sure you meet the criteria\.
-   Be absolutely sure you want to change your degree, because you may no longer be eligible for certain UBC awards\.
    -   If you are a Canadian citizen or permanent resident and you apply by **December 1,** your first\-choice degree will be considered for a [Presidential Scholars Award](https://you.ubc.ca/financial-planning/scholarships-awards-canadian-students/presidential-scholars/) if you select that option on the online application\.
    -   If you are an international student and you apply by **January 15,** your first\-choice application will be automatically considered for an [International Major Entrance Scholarship](https://you.ubc.ca/financial-planning/scholarships-awards-international-students/#merit)\.
    -   For all students, your new first\-choice application will not be considered for an award if you make a change after those dates\.

After you’ve thought through the above, you can [submit the changes](https://you.ubc.ca/contact-us/) of your first\-choice and second\-choice applications until **January 15**\. Be sure to include your full name and UBC reference number, and we will update your UBC application accordingly\. Your application changes will not be updated if your request is made **after January 15**\. We will notify you if we cannot accommodate a change to your application\.

**Note:** this information is for high school applicants\. If you are a post secondary transfer applicant, then the dates listed above may differ\.

## First\-choice and second\-choice degrees

Remember that you use the same UBC application to apply for degrees on both UBC campuses\. Your first choice and second choice can be on the same campus or on two different campuses\. Some degrees \(for example [Bachelor of Nursing at UBC Okanagan](https://you.ubc.ca/ubc_programs/nursing-okanagan/), or [Bachelor of Design](https://you.ubc.ca/ubc_programs/architecture-landscape-architecture-and-urbanism/), [Bachelor of Media Studies](https://you.ubc.ca/ubc_programs/media-studies/) or [Bachelor of Pharmaceutical Sciences](https://you.ubc.ca/ubc_programs/pharmaceutical-sciences/) at UBC Vancouver\) can only be considered first\-choice degrees\. This means that if you select that program as your second choice, it will not be evaluated\.

## Deadline to change the degree you applied to

The deadline for changing the program you’re applying to is **January 15\.**

title: Study permit concierge
content_markdown:
[Study permit concierge](https://you.ubc.ca/wp-content/uploads/2025/12/54689515481_b5b994c006_k.jpg.webp)

Now that you have an offer of admission to UBC, we would like to be among the first to welcome you to the university’s diverse and dynamic community\. We are here to support you on your exciting new journey\.

As you get ready to tackle your next steps, we understand that applying for a study permit and navigating Immigration, Refugees and Citizenship Canada \(IRCC\) regulations can be a challenge\. To help, we would like to offer you **complimentary study permit concierge services**\. These services are designed to provide students like you with resources and real\-time guidance as you work through your study permit application process\. If you choose to use these services, you will receive the following support\.

[Image](https://you.ubc.ca/wp-content/uploads/2025/12/54688699112_ed8252a303_resized-768x413.jpg.webp)

## Before you apply

**Before you apply for your study permit, you will get:**

-   Personalized consultations on study permit eligibility and requirements\.
-   Step\-by\-step guidance on the application process\.
-   Timelines and best practices for early application submission\.
-   Support in your local time zone\.

**As you prepare and review your documents, you will be provided with:**

-   Assistance in gathering required documents such as your Letter of Acceptance, Provincial Attestation Letter \(PAL\), proof of financial support, and statement of purpose\.
-   A review of your application forms for accuracy and completeness\.
-   Guidance on securing medical exams, police clearances, or biometric appointments, if required\.

[Students walking down the stairs at Allard Hall](https://you.ubc.ca/wp-content/uploads/2025/10/canadian-students-768x512.jpg.webp)

## While you're applying

**When you submit your study permit application, you will get support:**

-   Setting up an IRCC account\.
-   Submitting your forms and tracking your study permit application\.
-   Understanding country\-specific study permit processing guidelines\.

**As you prepare your financial documentation, you will receive guidance:**

-   On how to demonstrate sufficient funds to meet IRCC requirements\.
-   On how to prepare your bank statements, sponsor letters, and Guaranteed Investment Certificate \(GIC\) applications\.

[A group of students hanging out on student boulevard](https://you.ubc.ca/wp-content/uploads/2025/10/international-students-768x512.jpg.webp)

## After you've applied

**After you have applied for your study permit, you may also receive:**

-   Support if you are facing delays or additional document requests\.
-   Guidance on responding to visa refusals and exploring options for reapplication\.
-   Help connecting with lawyers or immigration consultants for complex cases and advanced legal support\.

## International Student Guides

For more information about being an international student, including applying for a study permit, visit our International Student Guides\.

[UBC Okanagan](https://students.ok.ubc.ca/international/) [UBC Vancouver](https://students.ubc.ca/international-student-guide/)

The study permit concierge services are designed to assist with routine study permit applications, and they do not cover every situation\. Some immigration matters need to be supported by a lawyer or specialized immigration consultant\. For these more complex cases, UBC can provide recommendations for lawyers or immigration consultants who can assist you\. However, this assistance would come at your own expense\.

**Note that once you become a UBC student, UBC offers extensive international student services to support you, including study permit related services\.**

## Schedule a session

Email us your questions or schedule your personalized one\-on\-one session now:

[Email us](mailto:study.permit@ubc.ca) [Schedule a session](https://outlook.office.com/book/bookingsISTIStudypermitconcierge@m365.svc.ubc.ca/?ismsaljsauthenabled)

**Please note:**

The study permit concierge services are being offered to you by UBC for informational and support purposes only\. These services are facilitated through third\-party consultants and professionals who are completely independent of UBC\. While we aim to assist you in navigating the study permit application process, the final responsibility for submitting applications, meeting immigration requirements, and ensuring compliance with IRCC regulations remains with you\. Any guidance or support received from third\-party professionals is subject to their terms and conditions, and UBC does not guarantee the quality of the advice they provide\. UBC is not liable for any decisions, delays, or outcomes related to study permit applications, even if you follow the advice of third\-party professionals\. You are encouraged to verify information directly with IRCC and seek additional licensed immigration advice at your own expense if needed\.

For official immigration guidance, please visit the Government of Canada’s immigration website at [www\.canada\.ca/immigration](https://click.em.svc.ubc.ca/?qs=c38a867c45764d8e50b775037f4abd7dfcc189b0182d8235e7e5681c97925a5836d95b8135c3f12877d3eee788cfd72c4f5a8873eeafb665 "https://click.em.svc.ubc.ca/?qs=c38a867c45764d8e50b775037f4abd7dfcc189b0182d8235e7e5681c97925a5836d95b8135c3f12877d3eee788cfd72c4f5a8873eeafb665")\.

title: The Big Question by UBC
content_markdown:
[The Big Question by UBC](https://you.ubc.ca/wp-content/uploads/2026/02/thebigquestion.jpg)

The Big Question is a case study competition where you’ll get an opportunity to experience UBC thinking to solve a real\-world challenge with the best and brightest of your peers\.

[Embedded content: The Big Question](https://www.youtube.com/embed/u5YfQ7PYZkQ?feature=oembed)

## One room\. Twenty teams\. A question worth solving\.

The Big Question is a case study competition where you’ll face real\-world problems, build a solution under time pressure, and present those solutions to a panel of UBC professors and notable alumni \(including business leaders based in India\)\. This is a genuine university experience\.

[Image](https://you.ubc.ca/wp-content/uploads/2025/12/54688699112_ed8252a303_k-copy-768x512.jpg)

## Competition details

### One day\. One venue\. One question that will change everything\.

Registration is by invitation only\. There will be a pre\-learning session on Tuesday, May 5, 2026 at 9:00 am\. Then you’ll be ready for the main event:

-   **Date:** Saturday, May 16, 2026
-   **Time:** 9:00 am – 6:00 pm \(IST\)
-   **Location:** Shangri\-La Hotel, New Delhi
-   **Who can participate:** Students in Grade 11 and Grade 12
-   **Size of teams:** 4 students per school
-   **Stream:** Open to all streams

## How it works

1

**Learn from UBC professors in a pre\-competition masterclass**  
Before competition day, a UBC professor will run a live online session to sharpen your skills and introduce you to UBC thinking\. This online session is open to all Grade 11 and Grade 12 students – even if you are not on the team\. Think of it as a free masterclass from one of the world’s top 40 universities\.

2

**Your school selects a team**  
Your counsellor or teacher will select four students to represent your school at the competition\.

3

**The Big Question drops**  
On competition day, you’ll receive a sealed brief that contains a problem that none of the teams has seen before\. You’ll have hours – not weeks – to solve the problem\. You’ll work in a breakout room, with UBC faculty and alumni guiding the process\.

4

**You’ll present your solution**  
All teams will present, defend, and debate their ideas and their solutions to a panel of esteemed judges – made up of UBC faculty and accomplished UBC alumni\.

5

**The best solution wins**  
The panel of judges evaluate every team\. The top teams will present their solutions to the entire group of competition participants\. The winning team will walk away with The Big Question title and prizes for every team member\. And competing students will receive a certificate of participation\.

## Two engines that drive change\. Your team needs both\.

Engineering builds the systems that make things work\. Business builds the case that makes things happen\. The Big Question sits at the intersection of both disciplines – and this is where the best solutions emerge\.

### UBC Sauder School of Business

How do you turn a concept into a plan that works? Who pays for it? What’s the market? The Bachelor of Commerce teaches you how to take new ideas, shape them into business plans, and make them real\.

### UBC Faculty of Applied Science

Can it be built? How does it scale? What could go wrong? The Bachelor of Applied Science prepares students for a simple reality: The most complex challenges ahead will not be solved by improving what we have today\.

## Faculty members and alumni

UBC faculty members and UBC alumni will be in the room, guiding the process\. They are travelling to you from the other side of the world because they believe in challenging the next generation to think bigger about the future\.

[Image](https://you.ubc.ca/wp-content/uploads/2026/04/prof-rajesh-sq.jpg)

### Dr\. Rajesh Vijayaraghavan

[Sauder School of Business](https://www.sauder.ubc.ca/)  
DBA \(Harvard\)\.  
Corporate governance, risk management, and machine learning\.

[Image](https://you.ubc.ca/wp-content/uploads/2026/04/prof-oleary-sq.jpg)

### Dr\. Stephen O'Leary

[Faculty of Applied Science](https://apsc.ubc.ca/)  
School of Engineering\.  
Systems thinking, feasibility, and real\-world design\.

### Another faculty member

And the info  
More info  
More info

## Some answers to your questions about the competition

[Do you need a background in business or engineering to participate?](https://you.ubc.ca/big-question/#accordion-6-panel-1)

No\. The competition is designed to be accessible for students from any stream\. What matters is how you think, not what you’ve studied\.

[How do schools select their teams?](https://you.ubc.ca/big-question/#accordion-6-panel-2)

Your counsellor or teacher will decide how to select the four students to represent your school\. This may be done through an internal competition, by nomination, or some other method\.

[Is there a registration fee?](https://you.ubc.ca/big-question/#accordion-6-panel-3)

No\. The competition is free for those schools that have been invited to participate\.

[Can students who aren't on the team still benefit from the competition?](https://you.ubc.ca/big-question/#accordion-6-panel-4)

Yes\. The online session on May 5, 2026, is open to all Grade 11 and Grade 12 students from the participating schools\. This session will provide you with an opportunity to learn from world\-class faculty, regardless of whether you’re on a competing team\.

[How can schools get involved in future competitions?](https://you.ubc.ca/big-question/#accordion-6-panel-5)

As this is our inaugural year, we are working with a select number of schools\. If you’d like your school to be considered for future The Big Question competitions, you can email [south\.asia@ubc\.ca](mailto:south.asia@ubc.ca)\.

[Embedded svg \(view source\)](https://you.ubc.ca/big-question/)

## Connect with us

As this is the inaugural year of The Big Question, we are inviting a select number of schools to participate\. To find out how to participate or to learn about future competitions, email us at [south\.asia@ubc\.ca](mailto:south.asia@ubc.ca)\.

[Apply to UBC at EducationPlannerBC](https://apply.educationplannerbc.ca/)

Already submitted? [View the status of your application\.](https://myapplication.ubc.ca/)

If you have already submitted an application to UBC for the 2026/27 academic year and want to make changes to your application, please contact using this [online form](https://account.you.ubc.ca/s/ask-ubc)\. Do not submit a new application\.

After you apply to UBC, you are able to check your application status within a few days in our [UBC Applicant Service Centre](https://myapplication.ubc.ca/) or visit our [Undergraduate Programs and Admissions website](https://you.ubc.ca/applying-ubc/applied/) for more information on your next steps\.

Once you’ve submitted your application, here’s what you can expect about the admissions decision process\.

-   [Appeals](https://you.ubc.ca/applying-ubc/applied/admission-appeals/)

## Receiving your admissions decision

The UBC Admissions Office is meticulously reviewing your application so that we can give you our decision as soon as we can\. That being said, we’re not going to rush through our evaluation of your application – we want to make sure you get a carefully considered decision from us\. As soon as we have evaluated your application, you will see our decision on the [Applicant Service Centre](https://myapplication.ubc.ca/) under **Admissions > Application Status**\.

## Rolling admissions

UBC [evaluates your UBC application](https://you.ubc.ca/applying-ubc/applied/application-evaluation/) once it’s complete, which means we need to receive all your grades and other required information first\. With thousands of applications coming in from different school systems around the world, we receive all those grades and supporting documents at different times\.

We can’t evaluate everyone’s application at the same time, so we send out admissions decisions as we receive and review information\. That’s what we mean by rolling admissions\.

If we received your grade information early in the year, we may have evaluated your application in January or February\. But don’t worry: UBC uses the same admissions criteria for everyone\. Students who receive offers by the end of February have to meet the same admissions criteria as those who receive offers in March or April, for example\.

## Admission decisions are *not* first come, first served

We use the same evaluation criteria for everyone when their files are complete\. If your files are complete in March, we will evaluate your application exactly as we have done for those whose files were complete in January\. Our decisions are not made on a first\-come, first\-served basis, and we take great care to make sure you get the right decision shortly after your application is complete\.

title: Orientations
content_markdown:
Whether you are a first\-year student, a student coming here from the other side of the globe, an Aboriginal student, or a transfer student, we provide an [orientation program](http://students.ubc.ca/campus/orient-yourself-campus-life/orientations/undergraduate-students "UBC - Orientation on Vancouver Campus") to get your UBC experience off to a great start\.

## All UBC students

New student orientations will help you make new friends, meet with student leaders and professors, get to know more about your faculty, and learn all about the services we offer to support you, as well as the many ways you can get involved on campus\. Learn more about each campus’s unique orientations\.

**Vancouver Campus: Imagine UBC**

[Imagine UBC](http://www.students.ubc.ca/newtoubc/orientations.cfm?page=imagine) is the main orientation program at UBC’s Vancouver campus, is one of the largest in Canada and is run by students for students\. This campus\-wide orientation program is held every year on the Tuesday after Labour Day\. It replaces the first day of classes\. All UBC students – new, returning, and transfer students – attend Imagine UBC\.  And Imagine UBC doesn’t end after just one day\. Events and email newsletters throughout the year will help you get the most out of your first two terms at UBC\.

**Okanagan Campus: Create UBC** 

[Create UBC](http://web.ubc.ca/okanagan/students/newtoubc/orientations/create.html) is the new student orientation program at UBC’s Okanagan campus and is held on the first day of classes\. It’s a day\-long series of events that will introduce you to the wide range of programs and services available to ensure your success\. You’ll make new friends, meet with student leaders and professors, and learn about how you can get involved on campus\.

## International students

### Vancouver Campus

There are two main programs at UBC’s Vancouver campus provided to help international students transition to life in Canada\.

**Jump Start**  
[Jump Start](http://students.ubc.ca/campus/get-oriented/attend-orientation/undergrads/jumpstart/register) is a first\-year transition program for new undergraduate international students\. It begins with a two\-week immersion program in August that will introduce you to the university, academic life and, most importantly, your faculty\. It continues from September through to April to guide you through your first year of studies, providing ongoing academic coaching and peer\-to\-peer support\.

International students who are not able to arrive in Vancouver in time to participate in the two\-week immersion program will still be integrated into the year\-long academic programming once they arrive at UBC\.

**International Welcome**  
[International Welcome](http://students.ubc.ca/campus/orient-yourself-campus-life/orientations/undergraduate-students/international-undergraduates) is held in September, January, and May for new international exchange, visiting, and transfer students\. In attending International Welcome, you’ll learn everything you need to know about study permits, entry visas, health insurance, employment, and the services and resources offered on campus\.

### Okanagan Campus

Each year we run two programs to help prepare international students for life at UBC’s Okanagan campus\.

**Jumpstart**  
[Jumpstart](http://web.ubc.ca/okanagan/students/newtoubc/orientations/jumpstart.html) will provide you with the chance to settle in before the start of classes\. You’ll enjoy preparation sessions focused on Canadian academic culture, plus the opportunity to build your social and academic support network to help you succeed in your first year\. There are also exciting adventures in and around Kelowna\.

**International Student Information Session**  
The [International Student Information Session](http://students.ok.ubc.ca/newtoubc/orientations/international.html) covers practical matters such as medical insurance and study permits, and includes information on various services for international students\.

## Students living in residence

Residence move\-in day is on the weekend before classes begin\. Residence staff and student volunteers are on hand to answer your questions and help you settle into your new home\.

Move\-in Day Information: [Vancouver](http://vancouver.housing.ubc.ca/residence-life/moving-in/move-in-day/) \| [Okanagan](http://okanagan.housing.ubc.ca/residence-life/moving-in/move-in-day/)

## Parents

At UBC, we recognize the critical role parents play in helping their children make the right post\-secondary choice and then supporting them as they pursue their dreams\. Parents with students living in residence should pick up a Rez Parent Guide when their student moves in\. There are also useful [resources for parents of residents](http://vancouver.housing.ubc.ca/ "UBC - Housing ") online\.

title: Students with disabilities
content_markdown:
UBC is committed to providing an environment free of structural and attitudinal barriers for students with disabilities\.

Students with physical and/or learning disabilities are provided with a wide range of services and support, including mobility assistance, interpreting, captioning, and facilitating accommodations needed by students\.

You’re invited to make an appointment with a Diversity Advisor to discuss [academic accommodations](http://students.ubc.ca/success/student-supports/academic-accommodations) and programs you’re eligible for\. Academic accommodations are determined on the basis of a student’s documentation of disability and the essential learning outcomes of courses\.

Your journey to UBC begins with your online application, and we’re here to provide you with the information, deadlines, and tips to help you put your best foot forward\.

## Your admission requirements

Admission to UBC is competitive, and your requirements change depending on your degree and campus of choice\. All applicants must meet UBC’s general admission requirements and English Language Admission Standard\.

[Canadian high school applicant requirements](https://you.ubc.ca/applying-ubc/requirements/canadian-high-schools)  
[International high school applicant requirements](https://you.ubc.ca/applying-ubc/requirements/international-high-schools)  
[International Baccalaureate applicant requirements](https://you.ubc.ca/applying-ubc/requirements/international-baccalaureate/)  
[University or college student applicant requirements](https://you.ubc.ca/applying-ubc/requirements/university-college-transfer/)[Mature student applicant requirements](https://you.ubc.ca/applying-ubc/requirements/mature-students/)

## English language competency

English is the primary language of instruction at UBC\. Before you’re admitted, you must demonstrate a minimum level of English\. There are nine different ways to meet this requirement, such as completing four or more consecutive years of full\-time education in English in Canada\. If you haven’t yet met the requirement, you may be interested in one of our academic English development programs\.

[Learn more](https://you.ubc.ca/applying-ubc/requirements/english-language-competency/)

## Important dates and deadlines

As a UBC applicant, you have a number of crucial deadlines to meet\. Find out when to apply, how you can be considered for scholarships and awards, and learn about many other important dates along the way\.

[Learn more](https://you.ubc.ca/applying-ubc/dates-deadlines/)

[Student on her laptop](https://you.ubc.ca/wp-content/uploads/2022/10/indigenous-students-howtoapply-768x480.webp)

## Indigenous admissions

Most Indigenous students are admitted based on a comprehensive review of their academic average and personal profile, within the curriculum they are studying\. However, UBC offers a number of pathways to a post\-secondary degree\.

[Learn more](https://you.ubc.ca/applying-ubc/indigenous-admissions/)

## Visiting, unclassified, and Access Studies

Visiting, unclassified, and Access Studies students are part of Non\-Degree Studies, which is for students taking UBC courses without pursuing a UBC degree\. Non\-Degree Studies is an option for you if:

-   You have already completed a degree
-   You are completing an undergraduate degree at another institution
-   You want to take courses through distance education outside of a degree program
-   You want to take a course for professional upgrading
-   You want to take courses for general interest outside of a degree program

[Non\-Degree Studies on UBC’s Okanagan campus](https://students.ok.ubc.ca/courses-money-enrolment/non-degree-studies/)  
[Non\-Degree Studies on UBC’s Vancouver campus](http://students.ubc.ca/enrolment/courses/non-degree)

## STEPS Forward initiative

STEPS Forward’s BC Initiative for Inclusive Post\-Secondary Education \(BC\-IPSE\) provides support for students with developmental disabilities to access post\-secondary education\.

If you are eligible, you may enrol in UBC courses for four years in a specific area of study\. You’ll be part of the same classes as UBC students studying for their degrees, but complete modified exams and assignments\. At the end of your studies, you’ll receive a Certificate of Completion at convocation alongside students earning their Bachelor’s degree in the same field\.

During your time at UBC, you’ll enjoy student life in the same clubs and social spaces as other undergraduates, and be supported in individualized ways to make decisions about what you want to explore on campus\.

[Learn more about STEPS Forward](https://www.bc-ipse.org/)
